After a word containing the element *dhanvan* or having a *y* or *v* as a penultimate letter (*upadha*), the suffix *vuñ* is applied.

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after a word denoting a desert (*dhanvan*) that is *vṛddha*, as well as after a word ending in *ya* or having *ya* as its penultimate letter. A desert is an arid region. Examples: *pāredhanvakaḥ* (belonging to the region beyond the desert), *sāṅkāśyakaḥ* (belonging to Sāṅkāśya).
[The suffix *vuñ* is also applied] after words ending in *prastha*, *pura*, or *vaha*.
The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after a name of a region that ends in these [suffixes] when it denotes an elder (*vṛddha*). Examples: *mālāprasthakaḥ*, *nāndīparakaḥ*, *pailuvahakaḥ*.
[The suffix *vuñ* is also applied] after names of regions of the easterners that end in *ropadha* (a penultimate *r*) or *eta* (the vowel *e*).

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after a word denoting an eastern region (*prāgdeśa*) that ends in a long vowel (*ī* or *ū*), has *ṛ* as its penultimate letter (*upadhā*), or is a *vṛddha* (containing *ai*, *au*, or *ār*) stem. For example: *pāṭaliputrakaḥ*, *aikacakrakaḥ*. After a word ending in *ṛ*: *mākandakaḥ*.
[The suffix *vuñ* is also applied] after a name of a country (*janapada*) and after a word denoting the boundary (*avadhi*) of such a country.

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after a name of a country that contains a *vṛddhi*-strengthened vowel. For example: *ābhisārakaḥ*. After a name of a country that functions as a limit (*avadhi*), the suffix is applied: *traigarttakaḥ*. This rule supersedes the application of *cha* when *gartta* occurs at the end of the compound.
Furthermore, the suffix is applied even after a country name that does not contain a *vṛddhi* vowel, provided it refers to a plural context.

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after a word denoting a country (*janapada*) that has multiple inhabitants, whether it ends in a *vṛddhi* vowel or not. This is an exception to the suffixes *cha* and *aṇ*. Examples: *āṅgakaḥ*, *ājamīḍhakaḥ*. From a *vṛddha* [country name]: *jāmbakaḥ*, *kālañjarakaḥ*.
[Also applied] after words ending in *kaccha*, *agni*, *vaktra*, or *garta* as their final members.

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after place-names ending in *kaccha* and so forth: *dārukacchakaḥ*, *kāṇḍāgnakaḥ*, *saindhuvaktrakaḥ*, *bāhugarttakaḥ*. It is also applied after [place-names] beginning with *dhūma*.

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied to these [names of] places; it is an exception to the rule for *chadir*. Examples: *dhaumakaḥ*, *vaidehakam*, and likewise *sāketa*, *rājagṛha*, *ujjayinī*, and *dakṣiṇāpatha*.
However, the form *dakṣiṇāpathī vṛttiḥ* should be considered [as requiring further analysis].

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after the words *samudra* (ocean) when meaning "boat" or "man. Examples: *sāmudrikā nauḥ* (a sea-going boat); *sāmudrakaḥ manuṣyaḥ* (a sea-faring man). It is not used here: *sāmudraṃ jalam* (sea water), *sāmudraṃ lavaṇam* (sea salt).
[The suffix *vuñ* is applied] after *nagara* (city) when expressing contempt or skill.
The suffix *vuñ* should be applied: *khalo nāgarakaḥ* ("a villager who is a city-dweller"), *kuśalā nāgarakāḥ* ("skilled city-dwellers").
Why [is it said] "in the sense of contempt or proficiency"? [Consider: *nāgarā viprāḥ* ("Brahmins from the city").
[The suffix *kan* is applied] after *araṇya* when referring to a human being.
The suffix *vuñ* may be applied [after the word *āraṇya*]. For example: *āraṇyaka-manuṣyaḥ* (a forest-dwelling person).

[It is also applied] after *pathin*, *adhyāya*, *nyāya*, *vihāra*, and *hastin*: *āraṇyakaḥ panthāḥ* (a forest path), and so forth. Optionally, when referring to cow dung (*gomaya*), [the suffix *aṇ* is used]: *āraṇyakam* or *āraṇyam gomayam* (forest cow dung).
The Vibhāṣā [states] that [the term applies] to both Kuru and Yugandhara.
The suffix *vuñ* may optionally occur after these two: *kauravakaḥ* or *kauravaḥ*; *yaugandharakaḥ* or *yaugandharaḥ*. After *madra* and *vṛji*, the suffix *kan* is used.
The suffix *kan* shall be applied after these two: *madrakaḥ*, *vṛjikaḥ*. After a stem having *k* as its penultimate letter, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after a country name ending in the letter *k*. This supersedes the suffix *vuñ*. Examples: born in the *Ṛṣika* country is *ārṣikaḥ*; *māharṣikaḥ*; *ārṣyakaḥ*.
Because of the explicit mention of *aṇ*, it is applied even after a country name ending in *u*: according to some, *aikṣvākaḥ*.
[The suffix *aṇ* is also applied] after [the group of words beginning with] *kaccha*.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied [to denote a place] when it is a country (*deśa*). Examples: *kācchaḥ*, *saindhavaḥ*. The following rule is desired for compounds ending in those [names]: *saurasaindhavam*.
[The names of countries are: *kaccha*, *sindhu*, *kamboja*, *gandhāra*, *kaśmīra*, *sālva*, *kuru*, *raṅku*.
The suffix *vuñ* is applied after the words *manuṣya* and those ending in *tad*.
The suffix *vuñ* (*-aka*) is applied after [words beginning with] *kaccha* and others in these two senses. For example: *kācchakaḥ manuṣyaḥ* (a person from Kaccha), *saindhavakaḥ*, *sālvakaḥ*.
When it refers to something situated there: *kācchakam asya hasitam* (his laugh is like that of a person from Kaccha), *kācchikā cūḍā* (a crest like that of a person from Kaccha), *saindhavikā*.
After *apadāti*, [the suffix *ṅasi* becomes *āt*] when *sālva* follows.
The suffix *vuñ* should be applied after the word *sālva* when it refers specifically to non-foot soldiers. For example: *sālvakaḥ* (a person from Sālva).
It does not apply here: *sālvaḥ padātiḥ* (a foot soldier from Sālva).
[The suffix *vuñ* is also applied] after *go* and *yavāgv*.
The suffix *vuñ* shall occur after these two [names] when preceded by *sālva*. Examples: *sālvaka* (a cow from Sālva); *sālvikā* (barley-gruel from Sālva).
After a word having *gartta* as its final member, the suffix *cha* occurs.
The suffix *cha* (forming *īya*) occurs after a place-name ending in *gartta*. For example: *vṛkagarttīyaḥ*, *hastagarttīyaḥ*. It also occurs after words beginning with *gaha*.

The suffix *cha* (which becomes *īya*) shall be applied after these: *gaha*, *antastha*, *nāntara*, *sama*, *viṣama*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class of words). By this, forms such as *aṅgādhikārīyaḥ*, *nagarīyaḥ*, and *pūrvatrāsiddhīyaḥ* are established. Examples: *gahīyaḥ* (belonging to a cave), *antasthīyaḥ* (relating to a semi-vowel), *nāntarīyaḥ* (inevitable), *ekagrāmīyaḥ* (belonging to the same village). [The base words are: *gaha*, *antastha*, *nāntara*, *sama*, *viṣama*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa*;
therefore, [forms like] *aṅgādhikārīyaḥ*, *nagarīyaḥ*, *pūrvatrāsiddhīyaḥ*, and so forth, are validated.

The suffix *madhyamañ* is applied to *pṛthivīmadhya*; [the form] is *madhyamīya*. The suffix *aṇ* is also applied to *caraṇa*; [the forms are] *mādhyamaḥ* and *madhyamīyaḥ*. There is elision of the suffixes *-tas* and *-tasa* after *mukha* and *pārśva*; [the forms are] *mukhatīyaḥ* and *pārśvatīyaḥ*.
The suffix *kuk* is added after the words *jana*, *para*, and *deva*. Thus: *janakīya*, *parakīya*, and *devakīya*.
According to the Cāndras, however, they read the rule as: "After *para*, *jana*, *deva*, and *rājan*, the suffix *kuk* is also applied. [The suffix *cha* is also added] after *sva*: *svakīya*.
Vāmana, however, will cite the augment *aij* (i.e., *ai*) in the rule "after *dvāra* etc., when *aṇ* follows" (*dvārādīnāñ ca*), based on his own word: "this belongs to him" (*svasyedam*) = *sauvam*.

[The suffix *cha* is applied] after *veṇuka* etc., and there is also the *vṛddhi* [vowel substitute]: *vaiṇukīyam*, *caitrakīyam*. [The suffix *cha* is applied] after words beginning with *kaṭa* when they belong to the Easterners (*prācām*).

The suffix *cha* shall be applied after a word beginning with *kaṭa* when it denotes a location in the eastern region. Examples: *kaṭanagarīya*, *kaṭadhoṣīya*. [Furthermore,] after the word *rājan*, the suffix *cha* is applied and *ka* is substituted for the final phoneme.
The suffix *cha* shall be applied after the word *rājan*, and *ka* shall be the substitute for the final phoneme. Thus: *rājakīya*.
[The suffix *cha* is also applied] after words ending in *vṛddhi* vowels, except for those ending in *akekānta* or having *kha* as their penultimate letter.

The suffix *cha* shall be applied after a place-name ending in *vṛddha*, *adakānta*, or having *kha* as its penultimate vowel. Examples: *ārīhaṇakīyam*, *āśvatthikīyam*, *kauṭaśikhīyam*. [The suffix *cha* is also applied] after a place-name whose final member is *kanthā*, *palada*, *nagara*, *grāma*, or *hrada*.

The suffix *cha* shall be applied after a place-name beginning or ending with *kantha*, etc. This is an exception to the rule for Vāhīka villages. Examples: *dākṣikanthīyaḥ*, *dākṣipaladīyaḥ*, *dākṣinagarīyaḥ*; *vāhīkagrāmīyaḥ*, *māhiṣagrāmīyaḥ*; *vāhīkahradīyaḥ*, *māhiṣahradīyaḥ*. [The suffix *cha* is also applied] after the word *parvata*.

The suffix *cha* (forming *-īya*) may occur [after a word denoting a mountain]. Do not disregard the term "mountain-dweller" (*parvatīya*). [This applies] optionally (*vibhāṣā*) when the referent is not a human being.
Except when referring to a human being, [the suffix] may optionally be *cha* or *da* after the word *parvata*. Thus, the fruit of a mountain is called either *pārvatīyam* or *pārvtam*.
After the word *kṛkaṇaparna*, [the suffix *cha* is used] when it refers to Bhāradvāja.
In the region of Bhāradvāja, the suffix *cha* shall occur after the words *kṛkaṇa* and *parṇa*. [Examples: *kārkaṇīya*, *pārṇīya*. It has been stated regarding the region.
Thus ends the second quarter of the fourth chapter in the *Bhāṣāvṛtti* composed by the Great Professor Śrī Puruṣottamadeva;
and the section on suffixes (*rakta-pāda*) is completed.
Oṃ. In the third quarter of the fourth chapter:
after the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the suffix *khañ* is optionally applied as well.

The rule "in the remaining cases" (śeṣe) applies here as well. After the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the suffixes *khañ* and *cha* may optionally occur. Thus: *yauṣmākīṇam* and *āsmākīṇam*; or *yuṣmadīyam* and *asmadīyam*. In the alternative, the suffix *aṇ* also occurs—yielding *yauṣmākam* and *āsmākam*. And when that *aṇ* is present, the forms *yuṣmāka-* and *asmāka-* are substituted [for *yuṣmad-* and *asmad-*].

In that [context], when the suffixes *khañ* and *aṇ* follow, there shall be the substitutions *yuṣmāka-* and *asmāka-* for *yuṣmad* and *asmad*. This has already been illustrated. Furthermore, in the singular, there are the substitutions *tavaka-* and *mamaka-*.

When used with the same referent as *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the suffixes *khañ* and *aṇ* are applied to form the words *tāvaka* and *māmaka*; furthermore, the suffixes *tavaka* and *mamaka* are also formed. Examples include *tāvakīnam*, *māmakīnam*, *tāvakam*, and *māmakam*.
After the word *ardha*, the suffix *yat* is applied.

From this [word *ardha*], when it occurs as a member of a compound, the suffix *ṭhañ* (which becomes *īya*) should be stated [after the word *ardha*] provided it is preceded by another word. For example: *gautamārdhika*.
[The suffix is also applied] after words preceded by *para*, *avara*, *adhama*, and *uttama*.

The suffix *yat* shall be applied after this [word] when it has "half" (*ardha*) as its prior member: *parārdhya*, *avarārdhya*, *adhamārdhya*, *uttamārdhya*. When preceded by a word denoting a direction (*dik*), the suffix *ṭhañ* is also applied.

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñya* are applied after the word *ardha* when it is preceded by a word denoting a direction (*dik*). Thus: *paurvārdhikaḥ*, *pūrvārdhyaḥ*; *dākṣiṇārdhikaḥ*, *dakṣiṇārdhyaḥ*. The suffixes *añ* and *ṭhañ* are applied after a word denoting a part of a village or a district (*grāma-janapada*).

From one part (*ekadeśa*) of these two [words *pūrva* and *apara*], when used as the first member of a compound with *ardha*, the suffixes *añ* and *ṭhañ* shall apply. Examples: *paurvārdhāḥ* or *paurvārdhikāḥ*, meaning "those belonging to the eastern half of this village or region.
From *madhya*, the suffix *ma* applies.
After the word *madhya*, the suffix *ma* occurs in the sense of "remainder. Thus: *madhyama*.
According to some, there is also elision of the vowels *ava* and *adhas*: thus, *avama* and *adhama*. [The suffix *ma* occurs] in the sense of "not appropriate" (*asāmpratika*).
The letter *a* is from the middle [of the mouth]. It should be pronounced appropriately, neither too high nor too low. "Middle" refers to the middle wood;
a "middle logician. Regarding the suffix *yañ*, it occurs after the word *dvīpa* when followed by *samudra*.
Those who come from an island near the ocean are "island-merchants" (*dvaipya* vanij). [This concludes] the section on time within the rules for secondary suffixes (*taddhita*).
The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time.

In the remaining cases, the suffixes *ṭhañ* or *ñ* shall be applied to words denoting time. Examples: *dvivārṣikaḥ*, *dvaivarṣikaḥ*, *māsikaḥ*, *sāṃvatsarikaḥ*, *āhnikaḥ*, *mauhūrttikaḥ*. The section on time [suffixes] extends up to the rule for "born there" (*tatra jātaḥ*). However, in the case of the word *śrāddha*, it is applied after the word *śarad*.

In the sense of *śrāddha*, the suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *-ika*) shall be applied after the word *śarad*. Thus, *śāradikaṃ śrāddham* ("a funeral rite performed in autumn"); otherwise, it is *śāradaṃ* ("autumnal"). Regarding the words *roga* ("disease") and *ātapa* ("heat"), the application of the suffix is optional.

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñ* may optionally be applied to these two meanings [of "autumnal"]: *śāradikaḥ* or *śāradaḥ* refers to a disease or heat. Excluding *ṭhañ* and *ñ*, the suffix *ṛtvaṇ* is used;
furthermore, *ñ* is added after the words *niśā* and *pradoṣa*.

And after these two, the suffix *ṭhañ* may optionally occur: *naiśikam* or *naiśam* "darkness of night"; *prādoṣikaḥ* or *prādoṣaḥ* "belonging to the evening. After *śvas*, there is also the augment *tuṭ*.

After the word *śvas*, the suffixes *ṭhañ* or *ñ* may optionally occur, with the augment *tuṭ*. Thus, that which will happen tomorrow is *śauvastikaḥ*; those who do not possess the prosperity (*vibhava*) that belongs to tomorrow [are called] *śauvastikatvam*. In the alternative, there are the forms *śvastyam* and *śvastanam*.
After words denoting time such as *saṃdhivelā* and so forth, as well as seasons and lunar mansions, the suffix *aṇ* occurs.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied to these [words] in the sense of "the remainder" (*śeṣe*). From *saṃdhivelā* and so forth: *sāndhivelam*, *sāṃdhyam*, *āmāvāsyam*, *paurṇamāsam*, *trāyodaśam*, *cāturdaśam*, *prātipadam*. From a season name (*ṛtu*): *graiṣmam*, *śaiśiram*. From a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*): *taiṣam*. In the case of *tiṣya* and *puṣya*, there is the elision of *y* by the rule "the *y* of *tiṣya* and *puṣya* is elided when referring to lunar mansions. Thus: *pauṣam*. From *saṃvatsara*, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] only in the sense of "fruit" (*phala*) or "festival" (*parvan*): *sāṃvatsaraṃ phalam* or *parvam*. Not here: *sāṃvatsariko vyādhiḥ* ("an annual disease"). From *prāvṛṣ*, the suffix *eṇya* is applied.
It may be so: *prāvṛṣeṇya* means "a cloud of the rainy season" or "a rain-bearing cloud";
[the suffix] *ṭhak* is applied after *varṣā*.
[The suffix] syāt [is applied after words ending in] vārṣika; and [the suffix] tadanta—such as paurvavarṣika.
In the Vedic language (chandas), [the suffix] ṭhañ is applied.
And also from a learned person.
The *chandas* [section] consists of two *sūtras*. In reality, however, "and after *hemanta*" (*hemantācca*) is also a *chandas* *sūtra*; thus, this constitutes three *chandas* *sūtras*:
"and after *hemanta*."
And in all cases, there is the elision of the suffix *tal*.
The suffix *aṇ* occurs after *hemanta*, with the elision of the final *t*. Thus: *haimanam*. It is also used for nights: *haimanīṣu rajanīṣu*.
The suffix *ṛtvaṇ* is also desired [after this word]: *haimantam*.
Because of its connection with the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñ* in the preceding rule, it is also used in the common language (*bhāṣā*): *haimantikaḥ*.
The word "everywhere" (*sarvatra*) is used in this single rule (*ekavṛtti*) for the purpose of terminating the jurisdiction of the section on Vedic meters (*chandas*).

[Now follows: *sāyaṃ-ciraṃ-prāhṇe-prage-avyayebhyaṣṭyu-ṭyulau tuṭ ca* (Pāṇini 4.3.23). From the indeclinables *sāyam*, *ciram*, *prāhṇe*, *prage*, and from other indeclinables, the suffixes *ṭyu* and *ṭyul* are applied, and the augment *tuṭ* is added.

The suffixes *ṭyu* and *uṭyul* shall occur after [the word] *sāya*, and there is the augment *tuṭ*. Thus: *sāyantanam* (evening), *cirantanam* (long-standing). The letter *m* is due to a specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*). After an indeclinable: *divātanam* (by day), *doṣātanam* (at night).

Here, *ṭyu* and *uṭyul* occur by way of supersession (*vipratiṣedha*): *prāktanam* (eastern), *prātastanam* (morning). Jayāditya says that after *cira*, *parut*, and *parāri*, the suffix *tna* occurs: *ciratnam*, *parutnam*, *parāritnam*. Regarding *agrapaścāḍḍimac*, the Bhāgavṛtti states it is Vedic (*chāndasa*): *agrimam*, *paścimam*.
According to Jayāditya, the suffix *ḍimac* is applied after the final member [of a compound]. [The form] *antima*.
[The rule] *vibhāṣā pūrvāhṇāparāhṇābhyām* [applies].

From these two [words, *pūrvāhṇa* and *aparāhṇa*], the suffixes *ṭyu* and *ṭyul* may optionally occur, with the augment *tuṭ*. Thus: *pūrvāhṇetanam* and *aparāhṇetanam*. By the rule *ghakālataneṣu*, there is no elision (*aluk*) of the locative case-ending. In the alternative [when the suffixes are not used]: by the rule *kālāṭ ṭhañ*, we have *paurvāhṇikaḥ* and *āparāhṇikaḥ*. The section on time (*kāla*) is complete.
Born there.
In this sense, the suffixes *maṇ* and so forth, as well as *gha* and so forth, shall be applied according to the rules. Examples: *māthuraḥ*, *sraughraḥ*, *autsaḥ*, *rāṣṭriyaḥ*, *kātreyakaḥ*.
[The suffix] *ṭhap* is added after *prāvṛṣ*.
The suffix *ṭhaP* occurs after *prāvṛṣ* in the sense of "born in. Example: *prāvṛṣikaḥ*.
When used as a proper name (*saṃjñā*), the suffix *vuÑ* occurs after *śarad*.
The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after *śarat*. Examples: *śāradakā mudgāḥ* (mung beans harvested in autumn); *śāradam anyat* (anything else produced in autumn).
The suffix *vun* is applied after *pūrvāhṇa*, *aparāhṇa*, *ārdrā*, *mūla*, *pradoṣa*, and *avaskara*.

The suffix *vun* occurs after these words when expressing the sense of "born from" (*jātārtha*), provided that it does not form a name (*nāmni*). Examples: *pūrvāhṇakaḥ*, *aparāhṇakaḥ*, *ārdrakam*, *mūlakam*, *pradoṣakaḥ*, *avaskarakaḥ*.
After the word *pathin*, the substitute *pantha* is also applied.
The suffix *vuñ* may occur after *pathin*, and there is also the substitution of *pantha* when expressing the sense of "born therein" (*jātārtha*). For example: *panthaka* as a calf.
Or, [the suffix *vuñ* occurs] after *amāvāsyā*.
Alternatively, the suffix *vuñ* may be applied; thus, one may say either *amāvāsyakaḥ* or *āmāvāsyaḥ*.
And [the suffix] *a* [is also applied].
Its feminine form would be *akārī*. [The suffix] *aṇ* occurs [after the word] *amāvāsya*.
[The suffix] *kan* occurs after *sindhu* and *apakarā*.
The suffix *kan* shall be applied after these two [words] when the sense is that of "born therein. Examples: *sindhukaḥ*, *apakarakaḥ*.
Furthermore, the suffixes *aṇ* and *añ* [are also applied].
From these two [suffixes], these two forms would result: *saindhavaḥ* and *āpakaraḥ*. There is a difference in accent.
[The suffix *cha* is elided] after *śraviṣṭhā*, *phalgunī*, *anurādhā*, *svāti*, *tiṣya*, *punarvasu*, *hasta*, *viśākhā*, *āṣāḍhā*, and *bahula*.

The *luk* (elision) of the suffix *nakṣatra* occurs after these [words] when the sense of "born under" (*jātārtha*) is expressed. By the rule *luk taddhitaluki*, there is elision of the feminine suffix. Thus: *śraviṣṭhaḥ*; *phalgunyo 'rjunaḥ*. When the suffix *aṇ* is used in its own sense (*svārthe*), as in "the month Phālguna," it refers to the month and to Arjuna. *Punarvasuḥ* [refers to] Uvvararuci; *bahulaḥ*. After *citrā*, *revatī*, and *rohiṇī*, there is *luk* of the feminine suffix. Thus: *citrā*, *revatī*, *rohiṇī*. When the suffix has been elided, the suffix *ṭāp* is applied again; or, as the case may be, the suffix *ṅīṣ* from the *gaura*-group. After *phalgunī* and *aṣāḍhā*, the suffixes *ṭā* and *n* [respectively] occur in the feminine. Thus: *phalgunī* and *aṣāḍhā*.
The suffix *chaṇ* is applied after the words *śraviṣṭhā* and *āṣāḍhā*. [Examples: *śrāviṣṭhīyaḥ*, *āṣāḍhīyaḥ*.
[The suffix *chaṇ* is also applied] after words ending in *sthāna*, as well as after *gośāla* and *kharaśāla*.

The suffix expressing "born from these" shall be elided (*luk*). One born in a cow-pen is *gosthānaḥ*; one born in a horse-pen is *aśvasthānaḥ*. [Likewise,] *gośālaḥ* (born in a cow-shed) and *kharaśālaḥ* (born in a donkey-shed).
However, for *vatsaśālā*, *abhijit*, *aśvayuj*, and *śatabhiṣaj*, it is optional.

The suffix denoting "born under" (*jāta*) may optionally be elided after these [names of lunar mansions]. For example: *vatsaśālaḥ* or *vātsaśālaḥ*; *abhijit* or *ābhijitaḥ*; *aśvayuk* or *āśvayujaḥ*; *śatabhiṣak* or *śātabhiṣajaḥ*.
[This elision] occurs diversely (*bahulam*) after names of lunar mansions.

After words denoting lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), there is frequently the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *aṇ* [which forms adjectives meaning "born under"] when combined with *sa-*, *bandhu-*, *velā-*, *naḍa-*, etc. Examples: *rauhiṇaḥ* / *rohiṇaḥ*; *mārgaśīrṣaḥ* / *mṛgaśirāḥ*. The word *pūrṇaḥ* has the sense of "born" (*jāta*).
The word "therein" (tatra) continues [from the previous rule] up until "that which is endured by him" (tad asya soḍham). [The suffix ka is applied after these:
kṛta ("made"), labdha ("obtained"), krīta ("bought"), and kuśala ("skilled").

In this context, regarding [the suffixes] *kṛta* and so forth, it shall be as prescribed. In the case of *srudhna*, one who is made, obtained, bought, or skilled is called *sraudhna*. Similarly, *rāṣṭriya* and *prāyabhava*.

In the sense of "mostly occurring" (*prāyabhava*), the suffix shall be applied as prescribed. For example: *sraughnaḥ* (one who mostly stays in Srughna); *rāṣṭriyaḥ* (one who mostly stays in the kingdom).
The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after *upajānu*, *upakarṇa*, and *upanīvi*.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied to these [words] in the sense of "mostly existing" (*prāyabhava*). For example: one whose hands reach the knees is *aupajānukaḥ*; one whose eyes reach the ears is *aupakarṇikalocanaḥ*. It is said that a woman obstructed with her own hands the hand of her lover reaching her nape (*upanīvi*). [The suffix is also applied] in the sense of "produced there" (*saṃbhūta*).
In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *sraudhna* is a mountain (*kṣmābhṛt*) because it originates from *srudhna*;
here the word *sthāna* has the meaning of "origin," and the suffix *ḍhañ* is applied after *kośa*.

*Kauśeya* refers by convention to cloth itself; it is a designation for a derivative product [of silk]. [The suffix -ya] occurs after a word denoting time when it signifies that which is well-formed, blossomed, or ripened.

In these meanings, [the suffix -aṇ] shall apply according to the rule based on time (*kāla*). For example: *hemanta* (winter) → *haimanam* (winter garment); *śiśira* (cold season) → *śaiśiram* (ointment for the cold season); *grīṣma* (summer) → *graiṣmam* (summer garment). In spring (*vasanta*), the *vāsantī* creeper flowers; likewise, *mādhavī*. In autumn (*śarad*), the *śāradāḥ* beans ripen.
The governing rule "based on time" (*kālāt*) applies up until the word *tatra-bhava* ("occurring there").
It also applies after the word *upta* ("sown").
When the sense is "sown," [the suffixes] shall apply according to the rule based on time: *haimanā yavāḥ* ("winter barley") and *graiṣmāḥ śālayaḥ* ("summer rice"). Here the meaning is "sown therein.
[The suffix] *vuñ* is applied after the word *āśvayujī*.
After the word *āśvayujī*, the suffix *kuñ* occurs in the sense of "sown"; it supersedes the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ña*. For example: *āśvayujakā māṣāḥ* ("beans sown on the full moon day of Āśvayuja").
After the words *grīṣma* and *vasanta*, [the suffix *kuñ*] is optionally applied.
When the sense of "sown" is expressed by these two [words *grīṣma* and *vasanta*], the suffix *vuñ* may optionally be used; thus, *graiṣmakam* or *vāsantakam*.
In the alternative, the suffix *ṛtvaṇ* applies: *graiṣmam* or *vāsantam*.
[The suffix *vuñ* is also applied] when the sense is "to be given as a debt."
In this sense, it should be as prescribed: that which is to be paid in a month is *māsika*; likewise *sāṃvatsarika*. The suffix *vuñ* is applied after the words *kalāpa*, *aśvattha*, and *yavabus*.

That time in which peacocks possess their plumage (*kalāpin*), the *aśvattha* trees bear fruit, and barley chaff (*yavabusa*) appears—such is that time. Therefore, the suffix *vun* shall apply in the sense of "pertaining to that [time]. A debt to be paid at the time when the peacocks have their plumage is called *kalāpakam*; likewise, *aśvatthakam* and *yavavusakam*. After the words *grīṣma* and *avarasama*, the suffix *vuñ* is applied.
The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied to these two in the sense of "belonging to that time" (*pūrvārtha*). Examples: *graiṣmaka*, *āvarasamaka*.
Furthermore, the suffix *ṭhañ* is also applied after the words *saṃvatsara* and *āgrahāyaṇī*.

From these two [words], the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *vuñ* shall be applied. A debt to be paid in a year is *sāṃvatsarikaṃ* or *sāṃvatsarakam*. [A debt] pertaining to the month of Āgrahāyaṇa is *āgrahāyaṇikaṃ* or *āgrahāyaṇakam*.
"The deer utters [a cry]."

In this sense, it should be according to what has been prescribed based on time. A wild animal that cries out at night is called *naiśa* or *naiśika*. The word *tatra* is no longer applicable here. [The suffix *khañ* is added] in the sense of "that which is endured by him."

In this sense, [the suffix] should be applied from a word denoting time according to the prescribed rule. An action associated with the night is "niśā"; one who has endured, mastered, or practiced that is "naiśikaḥ" (nocturnal) or "naiśaḥ" (belonging to the night). Similarly, "prādauṣikaḥ" or "prādoṣaḥ" [is used for one who has endured, etc., the evening].
Thus, it has been stated regarding [suffixes] from words denoting time.
That which exists therein.

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *sraughraḥ* means "one who exists or resides in Srughna"; *rāṣṭriyaḥ* (a prince). This is because the authority for the suffix applies to the word *tatra-bhavaḥ* ("existing there") prior to the rule "from *diś* and so forth, *yat*" (*digādibhyo yat*).
The suffix *yat* occurs after these [words]: *diśyam* (belonging to a direction), *vanyam*, *rahasyam*, *ādyam*, *antyam*, *yūthyam*, *gaṇyam*, *rasyam*.
After *udaka-* when it forms a name: *udakyā* (a woman in her menses); otherwise, *audaka* (a fish). Also after words denoting parts of the body.
Whatever [sound] there may be: dental, palatal, guttural, labial, produced in the region of the heart, produced in the chest, produced on the head, or produced in the mouth.
[The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after the words *dṛti*, *kukṣi*, *kalaśi*, *vasti*, and *ahi*.

The suffix *ḍhañ* shall be applied after these [words]. Examples: *dārtteyaṃ* (a sword made from iron), *kaukṣeyaḥ asiḥ* (a sword made from steel), *kālaśeyaṃ jalam* (water from a water-jar), *vāsteyam*, *āsteyam*, *āheyam*. [As it is said: "One should avoid enjoyments as one would avoid snakes. After the word *grīvā*, the suffix *aṇ* is also applied.
The suffixes *añ* and *ña* may be applied after this [word *grīvā*]. [Examples: *graivam*, *graiveyam*.
The plural number is for the sake of variety.
After the word *gambhīra*, the suffixes *ñ* and *ñya* are applied.

[The suffix *yañ*] may occur [after *gambhīra*, *bāhya*, *daivya*, and *pāñcajanya*. There is elision of the final syllable of *bāhya*: *bāhyam*. [The forms] *daivyam* and *pāñcajanyam* [are likewise formed].
Also [after a compound ending in] an indeclinable (*avyayībhāva*).

From this [base], the suffixes *ñ* and *ñya* shall occur in the sense of "being for the sake of" (*bhavārtha*). Examples: *pārimukhyam*, *pārihanavyam*. [The suffixes do not apply] after words such as *upakūla*: e.g., *aupakūlaḥ*, *aupaśālaḥ*. After a word having *antaḥ* as its prior member, the suffix *ṭhañ* also [occurs].

The suffix *ṭhañ* (which becomes *-ika*) shall be applied after an *avyayībhāva* compound whose prior member ends in *anta*. Examples: *āntardehikaḥ*, *āntarveśmikaḥ*, *āntarvaṃśikaḥ*. And [the suffix *ṭhañ*] is also applied after *adhyātma* and similar words in the sense of "belonging to" (*bhava*). Examples: *ādhyātmikam*, *ādhibhautikam*, *ādhidaivikam*, *aupasargikam*, *cāturarthikam*, *traivarṇikam*, *sāmpratikam*, *gairikam*, and so forth. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class). [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied] after the word *samāna* and after words beginning with *samāna*. Examples: *sāmānikaḥ*, *sāmānagrāmikaḥ*.
[The suffix *ika* is applied] after *ūrdhvanda* and *ūrdhvadeha*: *aurdhvandamikaḥ*, *aurdhvadehikaḥ*.
[The suffix *ika* is applied] also after the word *lokottara*: *aihalaṅkikaḥ*, *pāralaukikaḥ*.

[The suffix *īya* is applied] after *mukha* and *pārśva*: *mukhatīyaḥ*, *pārśvatīyaḥ*. For indeclinables (*avyaya*), there is elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant) when any *bha*-suffix follows.
[The suffix -īya is applied] to *kuja* and *para*. [Examples: *janakīyaḥ*, *parakīyaḥ*.
Furthermore, the suffixes *-īya* and *-maṇmīya* should be applied to *madhya*. [Examples: *madhyīyaḥ*, *mādhyamaḥ*, *madhyamīyaḥ*.
The suffix *dinaṇ* is also applied to *madhya*. [Example: *mādhyandinam upagāyati*.

The suffix *luk* (elision) occurs after [a word ending in] *sthāman*, as well as after a word ending in *ajina*. [Examples: Aśvatthāman; Kṛṣṇājina. [The suffix *luk* occurs] after the word *grāma* when preceded by *pari*, *anu*, or *pūrva*.
The suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *-ika*) shall optionally be applied after this avyayībhāva compound. Examples: *pārigrāmikaḥ*, *ānugrāmikaḥ*.
After the words *jihvāmūla* and *aṅguli*, the suffix *cha* (i.e., *-ya*) is applied.
The suffix *cha* shall be applied after these two [roots]. Since there is an obstruction [to the application of other suffixes], [the forms] *jihvāmūlīya* and *aṅgulīya* are derived.
Furthermore, [the suffix *cha* is applied] after the final letter of a consonant class (*varga*).
The suffix *cha* shall occur after a letter at the end of a class (*varga*). Examples: *kavargīyaḥ*, *pavargīyaḥ*, *cavargīyaḥ*.
When not referring to a word (*aśabda*), the suffixes *yat* or *kha* may optionally be used.

After a word ending in a class-consonant (*varga*), when not meaning "a group," the suffixes *yat* or *kha* may optionally be applied. For example: *mitravargyaḥ*, *mitravargīṇaḥ*, or *mitravargīyaḥ*. Why say "not meaning 'a group'"? Consider: *kavargīyo varṇaḥ* ("a letter belonging to the *ka*-class").
[The suffix *kan* is applied after *karṇa* and *lalāṭa*] when referring to an ornament: *karṇikā* and *lālāṭikā*.
The suffix *kan* is applied after these two [words] when they denote an ornament (*alaṅkāra*). An ornament for the ear is *karṇikā*; [an ornament for the forehead is] *lalāṭikā*.
[The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after the name of that which is to be explained, in the sense of "its explanation."

For the purpose of explaining that [suffix], and for the purpose of expressing its occurrence (*bhava*), the name of what is to be explained should be applied according to the prescribed rule. A treatise explaining *sup* suffixes is called *saupaḥ*; or, one occurring among *sup* suffixes is also *saupaḥ*. Similarly, *taiṅaḥ* and *kārttaḥ*.
According to the rule "after a polysyllabic word ending in an udātta accent, the suffix *ṭhañ* is added": [the forms are derived accordingly].

The suffix *ṭhañ* shall occur after a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) consisting of many syllables that has a name to be explained (*vyākhyeya*), in the senses of "belonging to" (*bhava*) or "explaining" (*vyākhyāna*). [Examples: *ṣātvaṇatvikaḥ*, *kārttaddhitikaḥ*. The base form (*prakṛti*) is oxytone by virtue of the accent of the compound (*samāsasvara*). [The suffix *ṭhañ* also occurs] after words denoting sacrifices (*kratu*) and sacrificial rites (*yajña*).

The suffix *iṣṭhañ* shall be applied after words denoting *kratu*s (sacrificial sessions) and *yajña*s (sacrifices), as well as after the word *bhava*. Examples: *āgniṣṭomikaḥ*, *pāñcaudanikaḥ*, *pākayajñikaḥ*, *nāvayajñikaḥ*.
After the word *ṛṣi*, however, this suffix is applied only when referring to chapters (*adhyāya*s).

The suffix *iṣṭhañ* occurs after words denoting sages (*ṛṣi*) that serve as names of chapters (*adhyāya*) to express the sense of "belonging to" (*pūrvārtha*). For example: *vāsiṣṭhika* (a chapter belonging to Vasiṣṭha), *vaiśvāmitrika* (a chapter belonging to Viśvāmitra). After the words *pauroḍāśa* and *puroḍāśa*, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is used.
The suffix *ṣṭhan* shall be applied after these two [words] when they refer to the preceding meanings. Thus: *pauroḍāśikī* or *puroḍāśikī*.
Regarding the word *chandas*, there are the suffixes *ya* and *aṇ*.
From this [suffix *ya*], these two forms arise: *chandasyaḥ* and *chāndasaḥ*.

After words meaning "consisting of two syllables," "having a short vowel," "belonging to a Brāhmaṇa," "first," "sacrifice" (*adhvara*), "preliminary rite" (*puraścaraṇa*), and proper names, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after words consisting of two or more syllables when they denote the first part [of a work] or the name of a Vedic school (*yus*). Examples of words with two syllables: *naiṣṭhikaḥ*. After words ending in *ṛ*: *cāturhotṛkaḥ*. After the word *ṛc*: *ārcikaḥ*, *brāhmaṇikaḥ*, *prāthamikaḥ*, *ādhvarikaḥ*, *pauścaraṇikaḥ*, *nāmākhyātikaḥ*.
Also after a compound [word]: *nāmikaḥ*, *ākhyātikaḥ*.
[The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after words other than *ṛgayanādi*.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after words such as *ṛgayanādi* when the sense is that of "one who has studied" (*pūrva*) or "the meaning thereof" (*artha*). Examples: *ārgayanaḥ*, *nairuktaḥ*, *śaikṣaḥ*, *naigamaḥ*, *vaiyākaraṇaḥ*, *yaugaḥ*. [The word] *pāda* [is formed] from *pada* with the sense of "explanation" (*vyākhyāna*);
once the sense of "explanation" has ceased, [the suffix is no longer applied].
Then he arrived.

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *sraughraḥ* (one who has come from Śrughna), *māthuraḥ* (one from Mathurā), *rāṣṭriyaḥ* (one from a kingdom). This is a governing rule (*adhikāra*) meaning "it prevails" until the end of the section.
[The suffix] *ṭhak* [is applied] after words denoting non-places.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after words denoting sources of income. For example: *āpaṇikaḥ*, meaning "one who comes from a market"; *śaulkaḥ*, meaning "one who comes from a customs post"; *śālikaḥ*, meaning "one who comes from a granary.
After the word *śuṇḍika* and others, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.
After these words denoting sources of income, the suffix *aṇ* shall be applied as an exception to *ṭhak*. Examples: *śauṇḍikaḥ*, *kārkaṇaḥ*.
After words denoting connections through learning or birth, the suffix *vuñ* is applied.

The suffix *vuñ* is applied to denote that which has come from those who possess a relationship established by learning (*vidyā*) or by birth (*yoni*). Examples include: *aupādhyāyakam*, *ācāryakam*, *paitāmahakam*, and *mātulakam*.
[Furthermore,] the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after words ending in *ṛt*.

The suffixes ṭhañ and ñya are added after words denoting a relationship through learning or birth. [Examples: *hautṛka-* (the office of the Hotṛ priest), *mātṛka-* (relating to the mother), *svasṛka-* (relating to the sister), *bhrātṛka-* (relating to the brother).
After the word *pitṛ-*, the suffix *ya* is also applied: *paitrya-* (relating to the father).
After *pitṛ*, there shall be [the suffixes] *yat* and *ṭhañ*; thus, *paitryaṃ* and *paitṛkaṃ*. After *gotra*, it is like [the suffix] *aṅka*.

The suffix *pratyaya* (denoting "come from") should be applied in the sense of having come from another lineage (*gotra*), just as in the case of a mark (*aṅka*). The mention of "mark" (*aṅka*) is for the purpose of illustrating the meaning "belonging to this. For example: *aupagavakaḥ* ("one who has come from the Aupagavas") and *nāḍāyaṇakaḥ*. [In these cases,] the suffix *vuñ* is applied according to the rule *gotracaraṇād vuñ*. Furthermore, after words denoting a cause or a person, the suffix *rūpya* is optionally applied.

The suffix *rūpya* may optionally be used after a word denoting a person from whom something has been obtained; for example, *samādāgataṃ* becomes *samarūpyam* or *samīyam*. Because [the base] belongs to the *gaha*-class, the suffix *cha* is applied; thus, *devadattarūpyam* or *devadattīyam*.
The suffix *mayaṭ* is also applied in this sense.
The suffix *mayaṭ* may also be applied after these two [stems]. For example: *samamayaṃ* and *devadattamayam*.
It means "originates from" (*prabhavati*).

In the sense of "originating from that," the suffixes shall be applied as prescribed: *haimavatī gaṅgā* ("the Gaṅgā originates from the Himavat"), *dārado nadaḥ* ("the Dārada river"). After *vidūra*, the suffix *ññya* is added.
Therefore, it would be different: the beryl gem originates from afar;
it travels by way of messengers on the road.

In the sense of "it goes to that," the suffix prescribed [by Pāṇini 4.3.85] shall apply if the words refer to a road or a messenger: *sraughnaḥ panthāḥ* ("a road leading to Srughna") and *māthurī dūtaḥ* ("a messenger going to Mathurā"). [The suffix also applies when the destination is] the gate through which one goes out.

In the sense of "departing," the suffix *ṇya* is applied according to the rule [Pāṇini 4.3.85] when the word *dvāra* ("gate") is used as the object; for example, *srughnam abhiniṣkrāmati* (he departs for Srughna) becomes *sraudhnaḥ*, and *kānyakubjam abhiniṣkrāmati* (he departs for Kanyakubja) becomes *kānyakubjaḥ*. Here, by figurative usage (*upacāra*), the gate is treated as the agent.
Furthermore, the suffix *ṇya* is applied to form the name of a work composed concerning a particular subject [Pāṇini 4.3.87].
In this matter, it would be as it is commonly understood: a work composed concerning Subhadrā is called *Subhadrā*; the narrative (*ākhyāyikā*) concerning Bhaimarathī is [called] *Bhaimarathī*.
By association—[a work concerning] Vāsavadattā is called the *Vāsavadattā-ākhyāyikā*, and [a work concerning] Kādambarī is called the *Kādambarī-kathā*.
The suffix *cha* is applied after the words *śiśukranda*, *yamasabha*, *dvandva*, *indrajanana*, and so forth.

The suffix *cha* (forming *-īya*) occurs after these [words] in the sense of "concerning" (*pūrvārthe*). A treatise composed concerning the disease *śiśukanda* is called *śiśukrandīya*. *Yamasabhīya*. From a *dvandva* compound: *śyenakapotīya*, *vākyapadīya*, the section concerning the relationship between word and meaning (*śabdārthasambandhīya*), *kirātārjunīya*. The group beginning with *indrajana* is an *ākṛtigaṇa*: *indrajananīya*, the chapter concerning the initiation of pupils (*śiṣyopanayanīya*), the poem concerning the search for Sītā (*sītānveṣaṇīya*), concerning the arrival of Pradyumna (*pradyumnāgamanīya*). There is a prohibition of this suffix after *devāsura* and similar *dvandva* compounds: *daivāsura*, *gauṇamukhya*.
That is his abode.
In this matter, it should be as it is obtained [by the rules]. *sraughraḥ* means "one whose residence is Sraghara"; likewise, *rāṣṭriyaḥ* ("one from Rāṣṭra") and *māthuraḥ* ("one from Mathurā").
The governing rule *so'sya* ("he belongs to this") applies up until the rule *tena proktam* ("taught by him").
And the term *abhijanaḥ* ("ancestral home") [is also included].

The suffix *cha* is applied after words denoting those who live by arms when the sense is "this is his native land" (*abhijana*), provided that the word refers to a mountain, and the formation follows the prescribed rules. For example: *srodhnaḥ* (one whose native land is Sradhna), *māthuraḥ* (a native of Mathurā), and *rāṣṭriyaḥ* (a native of a kingdom). When the suffix *cha* is added, it is replaced by *īya*. Thus, from *parvata*, we have *pārvatīyaḥ*. From *āyudhajīvibhyaḥ* (words denoting those who live by arms), the suffix *cha* is applied when the sense is "this is their native land. The suffix *cha* occurs after *parvata* in the sense of "eastern" when referring to those who live by weapons; for example, *lohitagirīyāḥ* (those from the Red Mountain) refers to those who live by the scriptures (*śāstrajīvinaḥ*).
What is the purpose of specifying "those who live by weapons"? [Consider: *akṣodaḥ* is a mountain that is their native land (*abhijana*); thus, *ākṣaudāḥ* refers to Brāhmaṇas.
After the group beginning with *śaṇḍika*, the suffix *ñya* is applied.
*Śāṇḍikya* is derived from *śaṇḍika* as his native place (*abhijana*); likewise, *cāṇakya* and *śākya*.
From [names such as] *sindhu*, *takṣaśilā*, and others, the suffixes *aṇ* and *añ* are applied respectively.

The suffix *aṇ* shall apply after *sindhv-ādi* [words]. For example: those whose ancestral home (*abhijana*) is Sindh are *saindhavāḥ*; likewise, *kāśmīrāḥ*. After *takṣaśilādi* [words], the suffix *añ* applies—thus, *tākṣaśilaḥ*; likewise, *pārvataḥ*.
After *tūdī*, *śalātura*, *varmatī*, and *kūcavāra*, the suffixes *ḍhañ* and *ñya* apply respectively.
From these, the following [suffixes] should be applied: *taudeya* (one whose ancestral birthplace is *tūda*), *śālāturīya*, *vārmateya*, *kaucavārya*;
[and the suffix] *bhakti*.

*Bhakti* is that which is worshipped or served. In this sense, it should be applied according to the rule: one who has Buddha as his *bhakti* is a *Bauddha*; likewise, a *Śaiva*, *Saura*, *Cāṇḍa*, *Sraughra*, and *Māthura*.
[The suffix] *ṭhak* is added after words denoting non-sentient objects, as well as place and time.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after a word that is neither a name of a place nor a time. For example: *apūpa-bhaktir asya* (he whose occupation is cakes) becomes *āpūpikaḥ*; *maudakikaḥ*. Why "not a place or a time"? [Consider: *sraughnaḥ* (from Sroghna); *graiṣmaḥ* (from the summer). After the word *mahārāja*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied.
The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after this [word]. For example: one whose devotion is directed toward a Great King (*mahārāja*) is called *māhārājika*.
After the words *vāsudeva* and *arjuna*, the suffix *vuñ* is applied.

The suffix *vun* shall be applied after these two: *vāsudevakaḥ*, *arjunakaḥ*. [The suffix *vuñ* is applied] after names of lineages (*gotra*) and Kṣatriyas, in many cases, in the sense that "this is his devotion" (*so 'sya bhaktiḥ*).

The suffix *vuñ* is frequently applied after words denoting lineages (*gotra*) and those designated as *kṣatriya*. For example: *aupagava* (a descendant of Upagu); "this is his devotion" results in *aupagavaka*. Similarly, *nākulaka*. Because it is stated "frequently," it does not apply here: *pāṇinīya*, *sauramaṣīya*, *pauravīya*.
Regarding names of countries (*janapada*), everything is like that of the country itself when the word for the country is identical [to the name of the inhabitants] in the plural.

When there is plurality, for those inhabitants of a country (*janapadin*) whose names are identical to the name of the country itself, all grammatical operations should be like those of the country (*janapada*). The suffixes previously mentioned by the rule *janapadatadavadhyoḥ* are extended to the inhabitants of the country as well. For example: the country inhabited by the Aṅgas is "Aṅga. By the rule *tatra jātaḥ* and *avṛddhād api vuñ*, the suffix *vuñ* is applied, yielding *āṅgakaḥ*. Similarly, *sauhmakaḥ*. Likewise, when referring to the inhabitants of the country—the Kṣatriyas—the suffix is applied: one who has devotion to the Aṅgas is *āṅgakaḥ*; one who has devotion to the Suhmas is *sauhmakaḥ*. [The suffix is also applied] in the sense of "proclaimed by him" (*tena proktam*).

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *māthurī vṛttiḥ* (the Māthuri commentary) is that which was composed by Mathura, spoken by Mathura, or explained by Mathura. [The suffix] *chaṇ* is applied after the words *tittiri*, *varatantu*, *khaṇḍika*, and *ukha*.

The suffix *chaṇ* shall be applied after these [words]. Its scope here is thus stated: those who study the *chandas* (Vedic texts) proclaimed by Tittiri are called *taittirīyāḥ*; likewise, *vāratantavīyāḥ*, *khāṇḍikīyāḥ*, and *aukhīyāḥ*. After the names of the sages Kāśyapa and Kauśika, the suffix *ṇini* is applied.

The suffix *ṇini* occurs after these two [words] when they mean "proclaimed by him," and it also denotes the subject matter thereof. For example: those who study the *chandas* (Veda) proclaimed by Kāśyapa are called *kāśyapinaḥ*; likewise, *kauśikinaḥ*.
[The suffix *ṇini* is also applied] after the names of the pupils of Kalāpin and Vaiśampāyana.
The suffix *ṇini* shall be applied after the four pupils of Kalāpin: *hāridraviṇaḥ* (those who study what was taught by Haridru), *tumburu*, *ulapa*, and *chagalin*.
It is also applied after the nine pupils of Vaiśampāyana: *ālambinaḥ*, *kāmalinaḥ*, and likewise *palaṅga*, *ṛcābha*, *āruṇi*, *tāṇḍya*, *śyāmāyana*, *kaṭha*, and *kalāpin*.
In the Brāhmaṇas and Kalpas proclaimed by the ancient seers.

The suffix *ṇini* occurs after the names of ancient great sages (*maharṣi*) when they denote *brāhmaṇas* or *kalpas*. For example: *bhāllavinaḥ brāhmaṇāḥ* (the Bhāllavi Brāhmaṇas) and *paiṅgī kalpaḥ* (the Paiṅga Kalpa).
[The suffix *ṇini* is also applied] after *śaunaka* and others when referring to Vedic texts (*chandas*).

In the sense of "belonging to the domain of," the suffix *ṇini* is applied after words such as *śaunaka*. Those who study the *chandas* (Vedic texts) proclaimed by Śaunaka are called *śaunakinaḥ*; likewise, the *vājasaneyinaḥ*. After the words *kaṭha* and *caraka*, there is elision (*luk*) [of the suffix].

There shall be elision (*luk*) of the suffix prescribed by these two [rules]. Those who study the *chandas* taught by Kaṭha are called *Kaṭhāḥ*; likewise, *Carakāḥ*. For those taught by Kalāpin, the suffix is *aṇ*.
It may be so. Those who study the *chandas* taught by Kalāpin are called Kālāpas; here, the suffix *ṭi* is elided by the rule *sabrahmacārin*.
The mention of the suffix *aṇ* is for the purpose of an additional rule—namely, [the formation of] Maudas.

Therefore, the suffix *ḍhinuk* shall be applied. [The form] *chāgaleyinaḥ* [is derived as follows]: there is elision of the *ṭi* [portion] by the rule *na-staddhite*.
[The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after *pārāśarya* and *śilālin* when referring respectively to a mendicant (*bhikṣu*) and a theatrical manual (*naṭasūtra*).

The suffix *ṇini* occurs after *pārāśarya* in the sense of "proclaimed" (*proktārtha*) in the case of the *Bhikṣusūtra*, and after *śilālin* in the case of the *Naṭasūtra*. Those who study the *Bhikṣusūtra* proclaimed by Pārāśarya are called *Pārāśariṇaḥ* (mendicants); those [who study] the *Naṭasūtra* of Śilālin are *Śailālinaḥ* (actors). In other cases, the forms are *Parāśarīyāḥ* and *Śailālīyāḥ*. After *kamraṅka* and *kṛśāśva*, the suffix *ini* is used.

From these two [words], the suffix *ini* is prescribed in their respective sūtras: *karmandī* (an ascetic) and *kṛśāśvī* (an actor). [The suffix *ini* is also applied] with the meaning "in the same direction as that" (*tenaikadik*).

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *saudāmanī* (lightning) is that which shares the same direction (*ekadik*) with Sudāman; *saurī* (a crane) [is so called because it shares the same direction] with Sūrya;
and *tāsikā* [is so called because it shares the same direction] with Tasi.
The suffix *tasi* may occur in the sense of "in front of" (*pūrvārthe*). As in: *sudāmataḥ*, *sūryataḥ*.
[And] after the word *uras*, the suffix *yat* [is also applied].

The suffixes *yat* and *tas* may occur after the word *uras*. [Examples: *urasā ekadik* (being in the same direction as the chest) results in *urasya*; *uraso hāraḥ* (a necklace from the chest) results in *urasya*; *urastaḥ* (from the chest).
[The suffix *yat* occurs] when something is first discovered (*upajñāte*).

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *pāṇinīyam* refers to that which was first conceived or composed by Pāṇini, namely the grammar (*vyākaraṇa*) known as the *Akalaka*; *sauraḥ* refers to the *Saṃgraha*. [The suffix *cha* is applied] when the word denotes a work that has been composed.

When *nāman* is used as the final member, the suffix *vuñ* is applied according to the rule; for example: *mākṣikam*, *madhu*, and *sāragham*. [The suffix *vuñ* is also applied] after *kulāla* and other such words.

The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after these [words] when a name is being formed: *kaulālakaṃ pātram* (a potter’s vessel), *vāruḍakam* (the work of a snake-charmer), *aindriyakaṃ jñānam* (knowledge pertaining to the senses).
After the words *kṣudra*, *bhramara*, *vaṭara*, and *pādapa*, the suffix *añ* is applied.
From these, there may be other [types]: *kṣaudram* honey, *bhrāmaram*, *vāṭaram*, *pādapam*. One who is filled with this has achieved his purpose.
This belongs to him.

In this matter, it should be as prescribed: *aupagavam* (belonging to Upagu), *rāṣṭriyam* (belonging to the kingdom), *śāstrīyam* (pertaining to the treatise). The governing rule *tasyedam* ("this belongs to that") extends as far as the suffix *vikāra* ("modification").

From the root *saṃvah* ending in the suffix *tṛc*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied, and there is also the substitution of *iṭ*. Thus, *sāṃvahitram* (the vehicle of one who carries). After the word *agrīdh* (the priest who kindles the fire), the suffix *raṇ* is applied when meaning "a shelter," and there is the designation *bha*. Thus, *āgrīghram* (the shelter of the *agrīdh*). Because of the *bha*-designation, the rule for the *padapada* (word-final) status does not apply, and thus the substitution of *jaś* (the voiced unaspirated stop) does not occur.
The suffix *ṣyañ* is applied after the word *samidh* in the sense of "placing" (*ādhāna*). [Thus] *sāmidhenī* means a *ṛc* verse used for kindling the fire.
The suffix *yat* is applied after the word *ratha*.
The word *rathya* means "the wheel of a chariot.
From the word *ratha*, with the addition of the suffix *uttara*, one forms *paramarathya*.
After words beginning with *pattra*, the suffix *añ* is applied.
The suffix *añ* shall be applied after words denoting a vehicle and after the word *ratha*; for example, *āśvaratham* (a chariot-wheel drawn by horses).
It is also applied after *patra*, *adhvaryu*, and *pariṣad*.
The suffix *añ* occurs after these [words]. *Āśvam*: belonging to a horse. *Auṣṭraḥ bhāraḥ*: a load of camel. *Ādhvaryavam śakaṭam*: a cart for the Adhvaryu priest.
*Pāriṣado hāsaḥ*: laughter of the assembly. *Pāriṣadaḥ samayaḥ*: a convention of the assembly.
The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after *hala-sīra*.

The suffix *vuñ* is added after a copulative compound (*dvandva*) to denote enmity or sexual union; for example, *hālikam* (the enmity between two plowmen) from *halasya*, and *sairikam* (the sexual union between two plowmen).

The suffix *vuñ* shall occur after a copulative compound (*dvandva*). In the sense of enmity (*vaira*): *kākolūkikā* (the enmity between the crow and the owl), *aśvamahiṣikā* (the enmity between the horse and the buffalo). In the sense of sexual union (*maithunika*)—that is, marriage—: *atribhāradvājikā*.
There is a prohibition [of this suffix] after copulative compounds beginning with *devāsura* and the like: *daivāsuraṃ vairam* (the enmity between gods and demons).

As for the usage *devāsuram abhūd yuddham* found in the *Devīmāhātmya*, it should be explained as being formed by the suffix *ac* under the rule for the *arśa-ādi* group, meaning "that in which the gods and the demons are the combatants."
The suffix *vuñ* is applied after [a word denoting] a lineage (*gotra*) and a practice (*caraṇa*).
The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after these two [words]. For example: *aupagavakam*, meaning "this belongs to the Aupagavas.
Regarding the expression of religious duties (*dharma*) and observances (*vrata*) derived from the names of Vedic schools (*caraṇa*): *kāṭhakam*, *kālāpakam*, *maudakam*.
The suffixes *añ*, *ñya*, *ñiñ*, and *ña* are applied to denote a collection (*saṅgha*), a mark (*aṅka*), or a characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*).

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after words ending in *añ* or *yañ*, when the sense of "a group" (*saṃgha*) and so forth is to be expressed; furthermore, the term "sound" (*ghoṣa*) is included here as well. After a word ending in *añ*: this is the group (*saṃgha*), mark (*aṅka*), characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*), or sound (*ghoṣa*) of the Bidas—*vaidaḥ*. After a word ending in *yañ*: *gārgaḥ*. After a word ending in *iñ*: *dākṣaḥ*.

After the word *śākala*, *aṇ* may optionally be applied, and in the alternative case, *vuñ* is applied. Thus, it is either *śākalaḥ* (meaning a group and so forth) or *śākalakaḥ*. Or [the suffix] may optionally follow from *śākala*.
The suffix *daṇ* may optionally apply after *śākala*, or else *vuñ*; thus, *śākalaḥ* refers to a group (*saṃgha*) and so forth, or alternatively *śākalakaḥ*.
Furthermore, the suffixes *ñ* and *ñya* are applied after the words *chandoga*, *okthika*, *yājñika*, *bahvṛca*, and *naṭa*.
The suffix *ñya* shall be applied after these [words], excluding *saṃgha* and the others, in the general sense of "belonging to this" (*tasyedam*).
According to others, there is a specific rule for *dharma* and *āmnāya*. Examples: *chāndogya*, *aukthikya*, *yājñikya*, *bāhvṛcya*, *nāṭya*.
[This does not apply] in the case of *daṇḍamāṇava* and *antevāsin*.

In these cases, the suffix *vuñ* would not apply due to the [specific] conduct of the lineage (*gotracaraṇa*). For example: *gaukakṣā daṇḍamāṇavāḥ* (the staff-bearing students of the Gaukakṣas); *dākṣā antevāsinaḥ* (the resident pupils of the Dākṣas). [However, for those beginning with Raivatika, the suffix] *cha* applies.
After these [names of lineages], the suffix *cha* shall apply as an exception to the suffix *vuñ* derived from the category of *caraṇa*. Examples: *raivatikīya*, *svāpiśīya*.
After *kaupiññjala* and *hāstipada*, the suffix *aṇ* applies.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these two: *kaupiññjalaḥ* (a follower of Kaupiññjala) and *hāstipādaḥ* (a follower of Hastipāda). For the word *ātharvaṇika*, there is also the elision of the final syllable (*ik*).
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after *ātharvaṇika*, with the elision of the penultimate vowel. Thus, *ātharvaṇaḥ* refers to the dharma or the sacred tradition (*āmnāya*) of that [Atharvaveda].
Its modification is likewise [denoted by this suffix].

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *āśma* means a palace made of stone (*aśman*). And he who bears an arrow resembling a stone, which is otherwise difficult to carry—[the suffix *aṇ* is applied]. [Examples: *bhāsmanaḥ* (made of ashes), *mārttikaḥ* (made of clay).
And [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after words denoting living beings, herbs, and trees when referring to a part [of them].

The suffixes prescribed [in the following rules] shall apply to denote both a modification (*vikāra*) and a part (*avayava*) of living beings (*prāṇin*) and so forth. For living beings, he will state the suffix *añ*.
From *auṣadhi*: *maurvaṃ* (made from the Murvā plant), whether it be a stalk or ashes. From *vṛkṣa*: *kāravīram* (made from the Karavīra tree).
Hereafter, the suffixes apply to modifications and parts of living beings and the like, whereas for others, they apply to the modification alone.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after [the group of words] beginning with *bilva*.

It may denote a modification or a constituent part. For example: *bailvaḥ* (made of Bilva wood), *vraihaḥ* (made of rice), *maudgaḥ* (made of Maudga beans). [The suffix *aṇ* is also applied] after a word ending in the letter *k*.
The suffix *aṇ* shall occur after a word ending in *kopadha*. Examples: *mādhūkam*, *vārttākavam*, *taintiḍīkam*.
[Furthermore,] the suffix *ṣuk* is added after the words *trapu* and *jatun*.
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these two, and there is the augment *ṣuk*. [Examples: *trāpuṣam*, *jātuṣam*. After a word ending in *u*, the suffix *añ* is applied.
The suffix *añ* shall be applied after a word ending in the vowel *u*. For example: *daivadāravam*.
It is also applied after a word whose first syllable is anudātta.
The suffix *añ* may optionally occur after these; [e.g.,] *kāpittha*, *dādhittha*.
Or, after *palāśa* and the others, the suffix *vā* [is applied].
Or it may be *añ* [as in] *pālāśa* or *khādira*; optionally, there is *aṇ*, which causes a difference in accent;
and for *śamyā*, there is *aṣṭalañ*.
The suffix *ṭlañ* may optionally occur [after the word *śamī*]. Thus: *śāmīlaṃ bhasma* (ash from the *śamī* tree) and *śāmīlī srak* (a garland made from *śamī*).
However, in common usage (*bhāṣā*), the suffix *mayaṭ* is used for these two [types of products], except when they refer to food or clothing.

In the common language (*bhāṣā*), the suffix *mayaṭ* may optionally be used after words denoting a modification (*vikāra*) or a part (*avayava*). For example: *aśmamayam* or *āśmam*; *dūrvāmayam* or *daurvam*; *kapotamayam* or *kāpotam*; *lohamayam* or *lauham*. Why specify "not when referring to food or clothing"? [Because in those cases the suffix is not optional. For instance: *maudgaḥ sūpaḥ* (bean soup) and *kārpāsaṃ vāsaḥ* (cotton cloth).
After words with a heavy vowel (*vṛddha*) or the group beginning with *śara*, the suffix is compulsory.

The suffix *mayaṭ* shall always be applied after words designated as *vṛddha* (belonging to the first class of the first five case-endings) that end in *śara*. Examples: *āmramayaṃ*, *śālamayaṃ*, *śaramayaṃ*, *mṛnmayaṃ*, *darbhamayaṃ*, *tṛṇamayaṃ*.

They also desire that it be applied invariably even after monosyllabic words that do not begin with *śara*: *tvamayaṃ*, *vāṅmayaṃ*. [The suffix *mayaṭ* is also applied] after *go* when meaning "excrement."
The suffix *mayaṭ* may be used [to denote "made of" or "consisting of"]. *Gomaya* means the dung of a cow; *gavya* means something else made from it.
It is also used after the word *piṣṭa*.
The suffix *mayaṭ* shall always be applied [to indicate "made of"]; for example, *piṣṭamayaṃ bhasma* ("ashes made of flour"). When it is a technical name (*saṃjñā*), the suffix *kan* is used.
The suffix *kan* occurs after *piṣṭa* when it denotes food; thus, *piṣṭakaḥ* (a cake) and *piṣṭikā* (a small cake).
After *vrīhi*, the suffix *kan* occurs when it denotes a sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*).
In this context, the suffix *mayaṭ* shall be applied after these words: *vrīhimayaḥ puroḍāśaḥ* (a sacrificial cake made of rice); *vraiham anyat* (anything else made of rice).
[Furthermore, the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after *tila* and *yava*, provided they do not form a technical name (*asaṃjñāyām*).
The suffix *mayaṭ* shall be applied after these two [words]. For example: *tilamayam* (made of sesame), *yavamayam* (made of barley).

Why "not when it is a name" (*asaṃjñāyām*)? [Counter-examples: *tailam* (sesame oil), *yāvakaḥ* (barley gruel). In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), [the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after a word consisting of two syllables.
Not from a bilva fruit that has grown on a donkey's ear.
Here follow two sūtras on prosody:
"The suffix *aṇ* is applied after *tāla* and so forth."
The suffix *aṇ* shall apply after these [words], superseding *mayaṭ* and others. [Examples: *tālam* (a bow made of palmyra wood), *bārhiṇam* (made of peacock feathers).
[The suffix *aṇ* applies] after words for gold (*jātarūpa*) when denoting a measure.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after words denoting gold (*suvarṇa*) when expressing a measure or a modification. For example: *hāṭakasya vikāraḥ niṣkaḥ* (a modification of gold is a *niṣka* coin) becomes *hāṭakaḥ*; *jārūpasya vikāraḥ kārṣāpaṇaḥ* (a modification of silver is a *kārṣāpaṇa* coin) becomes *jārūpam*. Why "when expressing a measure"? [Consider: *hāṭakamayī yaṣṭiḥ* (a staff made of gold).
After words denoting living beings (*prāṇin*) and silver (*rajata*), etc., the suffix *añ* is applied.

The suffix *añ* shall replace *mayaṅ* after words denoting living beings and [materials such as] silver and the like. For example: *kāpotam*, *māyūram*, *śyainam*, *rājatam*, *dāravaṃ pātrādi* (a vessel, etc., made of wood), *saisam*, *lauham*, *auḍumbaram*. [Also: "You shall see a golden city" (*purīṃ drakṣyatha kāñcanīm*), "a golden staff" (*kāñcanī vāsa-yaṣṭiḥ*). [This applies] also after a word ending in that same suffix (*ñit*) which has already been applied.

After a word ending in the suffix *ñ* or *ñit* which denotes either a modification (*vikāra*) or a part (*avayava*), the suffix *añ* may again be applied to denote those same two meanings; this supersedes the suffix *mayaṭ*. Examples: *daivadāravasya vikāro 'vayavo vā daivadāravo yūpaḥ* (A sacrificial post made from the modification or a part of *devadāru* wood). *dādhittham* (A modification or part of the *dadhittha* tree). *pālāśam* (A modification or part of the *pālāśa* tree). *śāmīlasya vikāraḥ śāmīlaḥ* (A modification of the *śāmīla* tree is *śāmīla*). Why "after *ñ* or *ñit*"? Consider *bailvamayam* (made of *bilva* wood), which ends in the suffix *aṇ*.
[The suffix *añ* is also applied] after a word denoting a measure, in the same manner as [the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after a word denoting price.

In this context, "measure" (*parimāṇa*) is understood as the three types of number, not merely in its conventional sense. A suffix should be stated after words denoting measure when expressing a derivative (*vikāra*), just as it is used in the sense of "bought for" (*krīta*). For example, just as one bought for a *niṣka* is called *naiṣkika*, so too a derivative of a *niṣka* is *naiṣkika*. Similarly, *śatyaḥ* and *śatikaḥ*.
There is also elision (*luk*) as in the case of "bought": *dvisahasraḥ* and *dvisāhasraḥ*. After the word *uṣṭra*, the suffix *vuñ* is applied.
It may be so: *auṣṭraka* means a modification or a limb of a camel;
or it refers to wool from a camel.
After these two [words], the suffix *vuñ* may optionally occur: *aumakam* or *aumaṃ*; *aurṇakam* or *aurṇam*.
After the word *eṇī*, the suffix *ḍhaṇ* occurs.
There may be *aiṇeyaṃ māṃsam* (deer meat) and *aiṇeyī jaṅghā* (a deer’s shank). From *eṇa*, however, only *añ* [is applied]: *aiṇam*.
[The suffix] *yat* [is applied] after *go* and *payas*.
That which comes from these two [words] is expressed by the suffix -ya: *gavyam* (derived from *go*), *payasyam* (derived from *payas*).
And [the suffix -ya is applied] after the word *dru*.
That which is substantial is a substance;
in the case of measurement, it is age.
The suffix *vaya* should be applied after the word *druma* when it denotes measurement. Thus, *drumasya mānam* (the measure of a tree) becomes *druvayam*.
When the word *phala* is used, there is elision (*luk*) [of the suffix].

The suffix *luk* (elision) should occur for the [secondary] affix denoting a product (*vikāra*) or a part (*avayava*) when the word refers to a fruit. For example: the product or part of a *badarī* tree is a *badara* fruit; likewise, *vakula*, *kadala*, *āmalaka*, and *kuvala*. By the rule "there is *luk* when the *taddhita* suffix is elided" (*luk taddhitaluki*), the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is elided.
[Furthermore, the suffix] *aṇ* is applied after words such as *plakṣa*.

When the fruit of the *plakṣa* and other such trees is to be expressed, the suffix *aṇ* shall be used; this is an exception to the rule for elision (*luk*). Thus: *plākṣam*, *naiyagrodham*, *kākubham*, *bārhatam*, *āśvattham*.
Alternatively, after the word *jambū*, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied].

After the word *jambu*, the suffix *aṇ* may optionally occur in the sense of "fruit. Thus, *jāmbavam* as the fruit. In the alternative case—by the suffix *añ* after a stem ending in *oḥ*—there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix when it refers to the fruit; thus, *jambu* as the fruit.
Furthermore, there is also elision (*lup*) [of the suffix].

The suffix may optionally be elided after *jambu* when the word "fruit" (*phala*) follows. Regarding the elision (*luk*) and the elision by *lup*, there is a distinction based on the treatment as if the gender and number were those of the original base (*yuktavadbhāva*). Examples: *Jambūḥ phalam* (A single jambu fruit). *Jambūḥ phalāni* (Jambu fruits; here the gender and number follow the base). But when there is elision (*luk*), it is: *jambūni phalāni* (the fruits are jambus; here the gender and number follow the object denoted). [In this case,] the gender and number belong only to the thing denoted [by the word]. And for words ending in the suffix *ñ* that wither upon ripening, such as *yava* and others, there is elision of the suffix when "fruit" follows. Examples: *yavānāṃ phalāni* (the fruits of barley) = *yavāḥ*. *tilāḥ* (sesame seeds). *mudgāḥ* (mung beans). *vrīhayaḥ* (rice grains). *godhūmāḥ* (wheat).

In the case of *puṣpa* (flower) and *mūla* (root), the suffix is generally elided (*lup*) when denoting a modification (*vikāra*) or a part (*avayava*). The flower of the *mallikā* is called *mallikā*; likewise *karavīra* and *jātī*. The fruit of the *kramuka* is called *kramuka*; the root of the *vidārī* is called *vidārī*. Due to the rule of general applicability (*bāhulyāt*), it does not apply here: *pāṭala* as a flower, *āśoka* as a flower, or *bailvāni* as fruits. [The suffix is also elided] after *harītakī* and others.

The suffix *lup* shall be applied after the word *harītakī* and others when referring to their fruit; this serves as an exception to the rule for *luk*. Thus, the fruit of *harītakī* is called *harītakī*; the fruits of *harītakī* are called *harītakyaḥ*. [The same applies to] *koṣātakī*, *drākṣā*, *śephālikā*, and *kaṇṭakārikā*.
After the words *kaṃsīya* and *paraśavya*, the suffixes *yañ* and *ñañ* are applied respectively, and there is also *luk* [of the original suffix].

Before the suffix *cha* (applied after words meaning "purchased"), the suffix *cha* is used: *kaṃsīyaḥ*. After words beginning with *u* and *go*, the suffix *yat* is used: *paraśavyaḥ*. After those two (*kaṃsa* and *paraśu*), the suffixes *yañ* and *ñañ* respectively should be applied, and there is elision (*luk*) of *cha* and *yat*. The modification (*vikāra*) of *kaṃsīya* is *kāṃsya*; the modification of *paraśavya* is *pāraśava*.
The categories of modification (*vikāra*) and constituent part (*avayava*), as well as those belonging to the *prāgdīvyatīya* group, have been fully explained.
Thus ends the third quarter of the fourth chapter in the Bhāṣāvṛtti composed by the great preceptor Śrī Puruṣottamadeva.
And the "yuṣmat" section is completed.
Oṃ. The Fourth Pāda of the Fourth Chapter.
In the section on secondary suffixes (taddhita), the governing rule for the suffix *ṭhak* extends up to the rule for the suffix *ṭhañ* in the sense of "carrying" (*vahati*).

He will state [later] that the suffix *ṭhak* is used in the sense of "he carries that"; therefore, the suffix *ṭhak* should be prescribed in the sense of "he says that" (*tad-āha*) after words such as *mā-śabda*. The suffix *ṭhak* shall occur: *He says "the word is eternal"* → *mā-śabdikaḥ*. *He says "the word is eternal"* → *naitya-śabdikaḥ*. *He says "it is abundant"* → *prābhūtikaḥ*. *He says "it is sufficient"* → *pāryāptikaḥ*.

The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after words such as *su-srāta* in the sense of "he asks about that": *He asks about a good bath* → *sau-srātikaḥ*. *He for whom Agastya asks about a good bath* → *sau-srātiko yasya bhavaty Agastyaḥ*. *He asks about a good night* → *sau-kharātrikaḥ*.

The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words such as *paradāra* when meaning "one who goes to" (has sexual intercourse with). For example: *paradārān gacchati* = *pāradārikaḥ* ("an adulterer"); *gaurutalpikaḥ* ("one who violates the bed of his teacher").
The suffix *ṭhak* is also applied after a word denoting an object when meaning "one who plays with it," "one who digs with it," "one who wins by it," or "that which has been won."

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. One who plays with dice or wins by means of dice is called *ākṣikaḥ*. One who plays with a plough, digs with it, or wins by means of it, or that which has been won by means of it, is called *hālikaḥ*. One who digs with a spade is *kauddālikaḥ*. Wealth won by means of dice is *ākṣikam*. One who wins by means of a mallet is *maudgarikaḥ*.
Although this secondary derivative (*taddhita*) is prescribed in the sense of a verbal action, it is by its very nature predominant in respect of the instrument (*sādhana*).
Sanskrit.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be used in the sense of "prepared with that. For example, *dadhnā saṃskṛtam* (prepared with curd) becomes *dādhikam*. "Preparation" (*saṃskāra*) refers to the imparting of excellence.
[Furthermore,] the suffix *aṇ* is applied after words ending in *kulattha* or having *ka* as their penultimate element.
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these two. That which is prepared with *kulattha* beans is *kaulattham*. *Taintiḍīkam*.
[That which] crosses over.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied in the sense of "one who crosses by means of that. For example: one who crosses by means of a grass-raft is *tārṇaplavikaḥ*; one who crosses by means of a reed-raft is *śāraplavikaḥ*. From *gopuccha*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied.
It may be so. One who crosses by means of a cow’s tail is called *gaupucchika*. There is a difference in the accent between the suffixes *ṭhak*, *ṭhañ*, and *ña*.
[The suffix] *ṭhan* is applied after words ending in *nau* (boat) and those consisting of two syllables.
The suffix *ṭhan* shall be applied after these two. One who crosses by boat is a *nāvikaḥ*. After a word of two syllables: *ghaṭikaḥ*; *ghaṭikā* (feminine). *Bāhukaḥ*. *Kumbhakaḥ*.
The letter *ṣ* is for the sake of euphonic combination (*sāṃhitika*), not an indicatory letter (*anubandha*).
[The suffix applies to words meaning] "he moves."

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied in the sense of "he moves by means of that. The root *car* means both "to move" and "to eat. Examples: *śākaṭikaḥ* (one who moves by means of a cart), *dādhikaḥ* (one who moves by means of curds).
After the word *ākarṣa*, the suffix *ṣṭhal* is applied.
The suffix *ṣṭhan* shall occur after this [word]. One who moves by means of a magnet is *ākarṣikaḥ*; [the feminine form is] *ākarṣikī*. "Magnet" (*ākarṣaḥ*) refers to a touchstone.
The suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs after *parpa* and other such words.

One who moves about with a *parpa* (a small cart) is a *parpika*; likewise, an *aśvika* (one with a horse) and a *rathika* (one with a chariot). Because these words end in the suffix *ṣit*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied: *parpikī*, *aśvikī*, and *rathikī*. This has been stated: "From *ākarṣa*, from the group beginning with *parpa*, from those beginning with *bhastrā*, and from *kusīda-sūtra*;
from *āvasatha*, and from the group beginning with *kiśara*—these six [words] ending in *ṣit* are included under the governing rule for the suffix *ṭhak*."
After the word *śvagaṇa*, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñ* [are applied].
The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after the word *śvagaṇa*. From *śvagaṇa*, one who moves about with a pack of dogs is called *śvāgaṇikaḥ* (masculine) or *śvāgaṇikī* (feminine).
Due to the inclusion of the letter *ca*, the suffix *ṭhan* is also applicable—namely, *śvagaṇikaḥ* and *śvagaṇikā*.
[The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after words such as *vetana* when meaning "one who lives by means of that."

The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after these [words] in the sense of "one who lives by means of that. Examples: *vaitanikaḥ*, *vāhikaḥ*, *jālikaḥ*, *vārttikaḥ*. After the words *vasna*, *kraya*, and *vikraya*, the suffix *ṭhan* is used.

The suffix *ṭhan* shall be applied after these two. One who lives by means of a price (*vasna*) is a *vasnika*; one who lives by buying and selling is a *krayavikrayika*. It is also applied after [the members of] a compound—thus, *krayika* and *vikrayika*.
Furthermore, the suffix *cha* is applied after the word *āyudha*.
The suffixes *cha* and *ṭhan* shall also apply. [Examples: *āyudhīyaḥ*, *āyudhikaḥ*.
[The suffix *cha* applies] after words such as *utsaṅga* when meaning "he carries."

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after words such as *utsaṅga* in the sense of "he carries by means of that. For example: *autsaṅgikaḥ* (one who carries on his lap) and *auḍupikaḥ* (one who carries on a raft).
After words such as *bhastrā*, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied.
It may be so. One who carries with a *bhastrā* (bellows) is called *bhastrikaḥ* or *bhastrikī*. [The suffix *ṭhan* is applied] optionally after *vivadha* and *vīvadha*.

From these two [words], the suffix *ṣṭhan* may optionally be applied; in the alternative case, *ṭhak*. From *vivadha*: *vivadhikaḥ*, *vivadhikī*; or *vīvadhikaḥ*, *vīvadhikī*. In the alternative case, *ṭhak*: *vaivadhikaḥ*. These two [terms] refer to a carrying-pole (*paryāhāra*). A carrying-pole is a specific kind of wooden beam with two slings attached at both ends, carried on the shoulder.
[The suffix] *aṇ* is applied after the word *kuṭilikā*.
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied to this [word]. A deer that moves with a crooked gait is called *kauṭilikaḥ*; a courtesan is called *kauṭilikī*.
[The suffix *aṇ* is also applied] after words such as *akṣadyūta* when meaning "completed by means of."

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after these [words] when the meaning is "produced from" (*nirvṛtta*). For example: *ākṣadyūtikam vairam* (a feud produced by dice-gaming); *gātāgatikam premā* (love arising from coming and going); *jāṅghopaghātikam kāryam* (a task resulting from a blow to the leg).
After a word ending in *tri*, the suffix *mam* is always used.

The suffix *imap* should always follow a word ending in the third case (*tryanta*). A pure [word] ending in the third case is not employed [independently]. Formed by cooking is *paktrimam*; *saṃskṛtrimam*; *labdhrimam*. It should be stated that the suffix *imap* follows words ending in abstract suffixes (*bhāvapratyaya*). *kārimaḥ*; "a fruit produced by ripening" (*pākimaṃ phalam*); "a ground made by digging" (*kuṭiṭamā bhūḥ*); "a creeper produced by watering" (*sekimā latā*); *dāhimam*; *dāhimā*; *pūrṇimā*. After the words *apamitya* and *yācita*, the suffixes *kak* and *kan* [respectively] are applied.

The suffixes *kak* and *kan* are applied after these two [words] when the sense is that of something already accomplished (*nirvṛtta*). For example: *āpamityakaṃ dhanaṃ* (wealth obtained by barter) and *yācitakaṃ maṇḍanam* (ornament borrowed). In the word *apamitya*, the suffix *lyap* is used from the root *meṅ*.
[The suffix *kan* is also applied] in the sense of "mixed" (*saṃsṛṣṭa*).
In this case, it should be as prescribed: *dādhikam* is food mixed with curd and made into a single substance;
*gauḍikam* is milk [mixed] with molasses;
[and so on] from flour and other ingredients.
Cakes mixed with powder are called *cūrṇinaḥ*;
[the suffix] *luk* is applied after [the word] *lavaṇa*.
After the word *lavaṇa*, when it signifies the sense of being mixed with, there shall be elision (*luk*) of the suffix. For example: *lavaṇaḥ sūpaḥ* ("salted soup").
[In this case,] the suffix *aṇ* is applied after *mudga*.
Maudgī is a gruel mixed with mung beans;
it is served with side dishes (vyañjana).
In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied as prescribed. That which is sprinkled with curd is *dādhikam*; likewise, *saupikam*. [The suffix applies] after *āja*, *saha*, and *ambhas*.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied in the sense of "he acts by means of these. For example: *aujasikaḥ* (one who acts with vigor), *sāhasikaḥ* (one who acts with rashness), *āmbhasikaḥ* (one who acts with water).
The word *tena* ("by that") is no longer applicable here.
Its furrows run in the opposite direction to that [of the previous field], and its hair-pores are slightly curved.

The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after the words *pratīpa*, *anūpa*, and *pratiloma*, when they are in the second case (accusative) and signify "acting in accordance with" (*vartate*). Examples: *pratīpaṃ vartate* → *prātīpikaḥ*; *ānvīpikaḥ*; *prātilomikaḥ*. Regarding the verse by Bhāravi: *tāṃ prātikūlikīṃ matvā*, [it is said: "Indeed, because of men's favorableness (*ānukūlikatayā*). Here, *pratīpa* and the others function as adverbs (*kriyāviśeṣaṇa*). Since an action is something to be accomplished (*sādhya*), its qualifiers are also things to be accomplished; therefore, the accusative case is used for the object. Furthermore, because an action is an abstract state (*asattvabhūta*), it is impossible to specify it without a general gender; thus, by rule, it takes the neuter gender.
The word "that" (tat) continues [to apply] as far as "its hem" (tasya dhamyam);
and also "around the face" (parimukhaṃ).
One who attends near the face is a *pārimukhika* servant; by the use of the word "and" (*ca*), a *pāripārśvika* [is also included]. He provides what is censurable.

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. A substance for the sake of double [its value] is "double" (*dviguṇa*); and because it involves a short period of time, it is censurable and blameworthy. One who gives such [a substance] is a *dvaiguṇika*. A creditor is a *traiguṇika*. When the suffix *ṭhak* is used, there is the substitution of *vṛdhuṣi* for *vṛddhi*. One who gives blameworthy interest is a *vārdhuṣika*.
The suffixes *ṣṭhan* and *ṣṭac* are added after the word *kusīda* ending in the first case, provided that it signifies "one who lives by usury."
From these two [suffixes], these two forms would arise: *kusīdikaḥ*, who lends money at usury (which is blameworthy), and *daśaikādaśikī*, who gives ten for eleven items;
[and one who] gathers grain by gleaning (*uñchati*).
In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied: one who gathers vegetables is a *śākika*; one who gathers jujubes is a *bādarika*. [The suffix is also used for] one who protects.

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied: one who protects a social assembly is a *sāmājika*; one who protects a settlement is a *sānniveśika*; one who makes a sound like a frog is a *śabdadardurika*.

The suffix *ṭhak* is added after these two [words] in the sense of "he makes" (*karoti*). For example: *śābdikaḥ paṭahaḥ* (a drum-maker) or a student; *dārdurikaḥ kulālaḥ* (a potter who makes clay drums). [Also: one who kills birds, fish, or deer.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after these words in the sense of "one who kills. There is the inclusion of the word-form itself, its synonyms, and its qualifiers. Examples: *pākṣikaḥ*, *śākunikaḥ*, *māyūrikaḥ*, *mātsyikaḥ*, *mainikaḥ*, *mādgurikaḥ*, *śākulikaḥ*, *prauṣṭhikaḥ*, *mārgikaḥ*, *hāriṇikaḥ*, *śaukarikaḥ*.
[Also: "one who stands across the path" (*paripanthaṃ tiṣṭhati*).

The word *paripantha* is an *avyayībhāva* compound; it is thus correct by virtue of its specific grammatical derivation (*nipātana*).
