A highwayman (*pāripanthika*) is a thief who stands upon that [road]—or, according to the particle *ca*, one who strikes it. [The suffix *ṭhak* is added after these: *mātha*, as the final member of a compound, *padavī*, and *anupadam*, when followed by the verb *dhāvati* (he runs).

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after these words when the sense is "he runs toward" (*dhāvati*). From *mātha* (a path) preceded by *upa*—as in *upamātha* (a side-path)—it is formed as *dāṇḍamāthikaḥ*, meaning "one who runs toward a staff-path. From *padavī* (a track), *pādavikaḥ*. From *anupada* (step-by-step), *ānupadikaḥ*.
After *ākranda* (a cry for help), the suffix *ṭhañ* is also applied.
From this [base], both *ṭhañ* and *ṭhak* may occur. *Ākrandikaḥ*.
It takes the word that follows the word *pada*.

The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after a word ending in a case-ending in the sense of "grasping" (*gṛhṇāti*). Examples: *paurvapadikaḥ* (one who grasps the preceding member), *auttarapadikaḥ* (one who grasps the subsequent member), *prātipadikaḥ* (one who grasps the nominal stem). It is also applied after *pratikaṇṭha*, *artha*, and *lalāman*.

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after these [words]. He grasps by the throat: *prātikaṇṭhikaḥ* (a favorite). *Ārthikaḥ* (one who seeks wealth). *Lālāmikaḥ* (one who seeks a livelihood). He practices the Dharma: *dhārmikaḥ*.
The suffix *ika* is applied after *dharma*, and it should be stated that [the suffix] is also applied after *adharma*. Thus, *ādharmika*.
After *pratipatham*, the suffix *ṭhan* is also applied.
The suffixes *ṭhan* and *ṭhak* occur in the sense of "he goes along a path. Examples: *pratipathikaḥ*, *prātipathikaḥ*.
[The suffix *ṭhak* occurs] in the sense of "he joins a group. Example: *samavāyikaḥ*.

The mention of "paryāya" (synonym) here [is for the following purpose]: the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied in this sense after words denoting a collection. Examples: *sāmavāyikaḥ*, *sāmudāyikaḥ*, *sāmūhikaḥ*. After the word *pariṣad*, the suffix *ṇya* is applied.
It may be so. One who joins an assembly is a *pāriṣadya*; or [one who belongs] to an army.
The suffix *ṇya* may optionally be used: one who joins the army is *sainyaḥ*. In the alternative, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied: *sainikaḥ*.
When it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*), [the suffix is applied] to one who looks at a forehead or a hen: *lalāṭikaḥ*, *kukkuṭikaḥ*.

If *saṃjñā* (a name) is intended, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after the words *lalāṭa* and *kukkuṭī* when they refer to a person's purpose (*artha*). Here, the restriction regarding the meaning is that it refers to a conventional designation (*saṃjñā*), not a conventional term (*rūḍhi*). One who merely looks at a forehead from afar, but does not engage in any actual work, is called *lālāṭika*; this refers to a servant or similar person. One who, with an unwavering gaze, walks while looking at a small area sufficient for a hen to step upon, is called *kaukkuṭika*; this refers to an ascetic or similar person. The suffix *dhamya* is added to denote his duty (*dharma*).

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. That which is appropriate (*rdhamya*) is "proper" (*nyāyya*), meaning "customary practice" (*ācāra*). For example, that which is appropriate for a toll (*śulka*) is *śaulkika*; likewise, *āpaṇika*.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after words such as *mahiṣī* and others.
The price of a mahiṣī is māhiṣa; [the price] of a purohita is paurōhita; [the price] of a prajāpati is prājāpata; after the word ṛtu, the suffix añ is applied.

The suffix *añ* shall be applied after a word ending in *ṛ*. From *hotṛ*, [the derivatives] *hautram* and *audgātram* [are formed, meaning] "pertaining to the office of the Hotṛ" and "pertaining to the office of the Udgātṛ.

After the words *nṛ* and *nara*, the suffix *ñ* is also applied. [From *nṛ*: *nāraṃ*; from *nara*: *nārī*. This is a traditional teaching (*āgama*) that this is a generic term (*jāti-śabda*). After the word *viśasitṛ*, there is also the elision of the suffix *iṭ*; [thus] *vaiśastram*.
There is also the elision of the suffix *ṇi* after the root *vibhāj*. [The derivative is] *vaibhājitram*, meaning "a share" or "rent. *Avakrayaḥ* means "rent" or "lease."

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be used in the sense of "its rent. For example: *śulkasyāvakrayaḥ* (the rent of a toll) is *śaulkikaḥ piṇḍaḥ* (a lump-sum payment for a toll); likewise, *āpaṇikaḥ* (a market fee). [The suffix *ṭhañ* is used] in the sense of "this is its merchandise."

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. One whose merchandise (*paṇya*) consists of sweetmeats (*modaka*) is called *maudakika*; one whose merchandise consists of cakes (*āpūpa*) is called *āpūpika*.
After the word *lavaṇa*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied.
*Lāvaṇikaḥ* means "one whose merchandise is salt" (*lavaṇam paṇyam asya*).
The suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied after words such as *kiśara* and others.
The suffix *śala* optionally occurs after the root *lū*.

The suffix *ṭhan* shall occur after words denoting fragrant substances (*gandhadravya*), such as *kiśara*, when the sense is "this is his merchandise" (*tad asya paṇyam*). Examples: *kiśarikaḥ* (masculine), *kiśarikī* (feminine); *śalālukaḥ*. Optionally, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied: *śālālukaḥ*. The word "merchandise" (*paṇyam*) is discontinued;
the phrase "this belongs to him" (*tad asya*) continues in force until the point where it says "it is given to him for that" (*tad asmai dīyate*).
Craftsmanship.

In this case, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. For one whose craft is the playing of the mṛdaṅga drum, [the word is] *mārdaṅgikaḥ*. [Similarly,] *pāṇavikaḥ*. Optionally, the suffix *aṇ* is applied after the words *maḍḍuka* and *jharjhara*.

The suffix *aṇ* may optionally be applied after these two: *tad asya śilpam* ("this is his craft"). Examples: *māḍḍukaḥ*, *jhārjharaḥ*. In the alternative (*pakṣe*), [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied]: *māḍḍukikaḥ*, *jhārjharikaḥ*.
[The rule applies when the word refers to] a weapon (*praharaṇam*).

In these cases, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied: one whose weapon (*praharaṇa*) is a sword (*asi*) is an *āsika*; a *prāsika*; a *dhānuṣka*; a *cākrika*; a *pāśika*. After the word *paraśvadha*, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ṭhak* are also [applied].
From *paraśvadha*, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ṭhak* shall occur; thus, *pāraśvadhikaḥ*. There is a difference in accent. From *śakti* and *yaṣṭi*, the suffix *īkak* occurs.
The suffix *īkak* shall be applied after these two. One whose weapon (*praharaṇa*) is a spear (*śakti*) is a *śāktīka*; likewise, a *yāṣṭīka* or *yāṣṭikī*.
[The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after *asti*, *nāsti*, and *diṣṭa* when they denote an opinion (*mati*).

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. One who possesses such a conviction (*mati*) is an *āstika*; one who does not is an *nāstika*; and one who believes in destiny is a *daiṣṭika*. Some maintain that the words *asti* and *nāsti* are finite verbal forms (*tiṅanta*); others hold that they are particles (*nipāta*) that resemble finite verbal forms. [The suffix *ṭhak* is also applied after the word] *śīla*.

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied: one whose habit is harsh speech is *pāruṣikaḥ*; [one whose habit is] abusive speech is *ākrośikaḥ*; [one whose habit is] compassionate is *kāruṇikaḥ*. After words such as *chatra*, the suffix *ṇa* is applied.

A *chātra* is one whose duty (*śīla*) is to provide shelter (*chādana*), like a parasol (*chatra*). Examples include: a student (*śaikṣa*), an ascetic (*tāpasa*), and a thief (*caura*, from the root *cur* "to steal").
[The suffix *aṇ*] occurs after the word *adhyayana* when it follows *karman*.

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. When one other [lesson] characterized by incorrect recitation has occurred for him, he is called *aikānyikaḥ*. Similarly, *dvaiyanyikaḥ*. This is a compound formed under the rule *taddhitārtha* (Pāṇini 2.1.51). Likewise, *ekarūpikaḥ* and *aikagranthikaḥ*.
When the first member of the compound consists of more than two syllables (*bahvac-pūrva-pada*), the suffix *ṭhac* is used.

The suffix *ṭhac* shall be applied after a word with many vowels (*bahvac*) as its prior member in the sense of "preceded by. For example: *dvādaśānyikaḥ* ("one preceded by twelve others") and *trayodaśagranthikaḥ* ("one preceded by thirteen knots").
[The suffix *ṭhañ* is used] for things that are beneficial when eaten.

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. For example: *āpūpikaḥ* (one to whom cakes are allotted), *audanikaḥ* (one to whom rice is allotted), *maudakikaḥ* (one to whom sweetmeats are allotted). The dative case is used in connection with "what is beneficial" (*hita*). [The suffix is also applied] when something is regularly assigned to someone.

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. That for whom specially prepared first-portion food (*āgrabhojana*) is given is called *āgrabhojanikaḥ*. [Likewise,] *prāthamakalpikaḥ*. From the words *śrāṇā*, *māṃsa*, and *odana*, the suffix *ṭiṭhan* is applied.
From these two [words], *ṭiṭhan* shall be applied in the same sense as the previous [suffixes]. The letter *i* is for the sake of pronunciation. Examples: *śrāṇikaḥ*, *māṃsaudanikaḥ*.
Also from a separated compound: *māṃsikaḥ*, *audanikaḥ*; and *māṃsikī*. From *bhakta*, the suffix *aṇ* is optionally applied.
Or it may be: "food is given to him" (bhaktaṃ asmai dīyate), thus he is *bhāktaḥ* or *bhāktikaḥ*, meaning one appointed to that [task].
In this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. One appointed at the gate is a *dauvārika*; one [appointed] at the customs house is a *śaulkika*.
The word "therein" (*tatra*) continues in force up until the rule "it carries that. After a stem ending in *agāra*, the suffix *ṭhan* is applied.
One appointed to a temple is a *devāgārika*; one in charge of a storehouse is a *bhāṇḍagārika*.
From the root *aga* alone, with the suffix *ṭhañ*, it means a householder (*āgārika*).
One who studies at an improper place or time [is also so called].

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied to denote one who studies in an improper place or at an improper time. For example: *śmāśānikaḥ* (one who studies in a cremation ground); *cātuṣpathikaḥ* (one who studies at a crossroads). Regarding improper time: *cāturdaśikaḥ* (one who studies on the fourteenth day); *āṣṭamikaḥ* (one who studies on the eighth day).
Improper place and time are those prohibited by the scriptures (*śāstra*).
[The suffix *ṭhak* is also applied] in the sense of "dealing with" in relation to *kaṭhina*, *anta*, *prastāra*, and *saṃsthāna*.

The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after these [words] in the sense of "dealing with" (*vyavaharati*). From *vaṃśakaṭhina*, one who deals with it is *vāṃśakaṭhinikaḥ*. *Prāstārikaḥ*. *Sāṃsthānikaḥ*. [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied] in the sense of "dwelling near" (*nikaṭe vasati*).
The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after the word *nikaṭa* in the sense of "dwelling there. For example: *naikaṭiko bhikṣuḥ* ("a mendicant who dwells nearby").
After the word *āvasatha*, the suffix *ṣṭhal* occurs.

One who dwells in a lodging is an *āvasathika*; [the feminine form is] *āvasathikī*. [The suffix] *yat* is applied after [a word ending in] *-dhit-* (i.e., *āvasatha-*) in the sense of "dwelling there."
The suffix *yat* should be understood as having the senses of "beneficial for that" (*tasmai hitam*) and so forth, as well as the sense of "prior to that" (*prāk*);
[and it forms] *rathya*, *yugya*, and *prāsaṅgya*, meaning "that which draws a chariot," "a yoke," and "a side-horse."

The suffix *yat* is applied after words such as *ratha* in the sense of "it carries that. When two chariots carry something, it forms a *dvigu* compound in the sense of a secondary derivative (*taddhita*): *dvirathyaḥ* ("carrying two chariots") and *trirathyaḥ* ("carrying three chariots"). However, there is a traditional rule (*smṛti*) stating that *yat* is not established after the word *ratha* alone. [Examples of other formations are: *yugyaḥ* ("a vehicle") and *prāsaṅyaḥ* ("a side-horse"). After the word *dhur*, the suffixes *yaṅ* and *ḍhak* are applied.
[The suffixes] *ya* and *eya* may [be applied]. One who bears the burden is a *dhurya* or a *dhaureya*.
[The suffix] *kha* is applied after the word *sarvadhura*.
It may be so. One who bears all burdens is *sarvadhurīṇa*.

According to some, by means of a rule-separation (*yogavibhāga*), there are also *uttaradhurīṇa* and *dakṣiṇadhurīṇa*; according to others, simply *dhurīṇa*. [The suffix] *kuk* is added after *ekadhurā*.
The suffix *cha* (īna) is optionally replaced by *luk* (elision) after the word *ekadhura*; there is also the hearing [of the original suffix]. Thus: *ekadhuraḥ* and *ekadhurīṇaḥ*.
After the word *śakaṭa*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.

The word *śākaṭa* means "one who draws a cart. [The suffix] *ṭhañ* is applied after *dvi-śakaṭa* and *hala-sīra*. [Examples: *dvaiśakaṭaḥ* ("one who draws two carts"), *hālikaḥ* ("one who uses a plough").]
*hālikaḥ* (a ploughman), *dvehalikaḥ* (one who owns two ploughs), *sairikaḥ* (a ploughman), *dvaisīrikaḥ* (one who owns two ploughs), *traisīrikaḥ* (one who owns three ploughs);
[the suffix *cha* is applied] after *janya* when it forms a proper name (*saṃjñā*).

The *janyāḥ* (kinsmen) would not be those who cause birth; rather, the *janyāḥ* are those who carry the bride (*janīṃ vadhūm*)—the groom’s maternal uncles and their peers. He pierces [the target] without a bow.

The suffix *yat* shall be applied after an object [denoting the thing struck] in the sense of "he pierces that," provided that the bow is not the instrument [of piercing]. Examples: *padyaḥ pāṣāṇaḥ* ("a stone that pierces the foot"), *hṛdyāḥ kaṇṭakāḥ* ("thorns that pierce the heart"). Not here: *dhānuṣkaś cauraṃ vidhyati* ("the archer pierces the thief"). [Also not here: *dhanagaṇaṃ labdhvā* ("having obtained a mass of wealth").

The suffix *yat* occurs in the sense of "obtained from these two. For example: *dhanyaḥ bālakaḥ* ("a boy who has obtained wealth"), *gaṇyaḥ mṛgaḥ* ("a deer that is counted"). [In these cases,] *tṛn* is used for the sense of "one who has obtained" (*labdhā*).
After the word *anna*, the suffix *ṇa* is applied:
*ānnaḥ chātraḥ* ("a student who has obtained food").
He has come under control.
The suffix *yat* occurs in the sense of "gone under the influence of"; for example, *vaśyaḥ sarvo janaḥ strīṇām* ("all people are subject to women"), where the word is visible in this context.
That which exists in a location beyond a visible spot is called *padya*. For example: "In this place there is a visible footprint (*pada*)," "muddy (*padya*) ground," or "a muddy (*padya*) path.
[The word *padya* is also used] when the root of something has been pulled out.

In this sense, that which occurs is as follows: *mūla* [is used] for these [plants] because they are uprooted; due to their tenderness, they are pulled out by the mere act of grasping. *Mudga* is [used] for the price. The root *budh* means "exertion.
In the sense of a name, *dhenuṣyā* [is formed].

This is prescribed as a nipātana (irregular formation). *Dhenuṣyā* refers to a cow or a buffalo that remains as collateral for a milk-loan. [The suffix] *ñya* is applied when [the word *dhenu*] is connected with *gṛhapati*.
The suffix *ñya* should be applied after the word *gṛhapati* when it does not denote a name; [the resulting form] is *gārhapatya*, a specific type of sacred fire.

[The suffix *ya* is applied] after the words *nau*, *vayas*, *dharma*, *viṣa*, *mūla*, *mūla*, *sītā*, *tulā*, and *bhyaḥ* [respectively], when they mean "to be crossed," "equal in age," "to be performed," "poisonous," "rooted," "to be measured by a furrow," "to be weighed," "to be obtained," "to be tied," "to be bent," "equal," and "measured."

After the eight [stems] beginning with *nau*, when the suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of "crossable by," etc., the following forms arise: *nau-tārya* becomes *nāvya*; *nāvyaṃ payaḥ* ("water crossable by boat"). Some crossed [the river] with their arms (*bhujaiḥ*). *Vayasā tulyaḥ* ("equal in age") becomes *vayasyaḥ*. *Dharmeṇa prāpyaḥ* ("attainable through merit") becomes *dharmyaḥ bhogaḥ* ("enjoyment obtainable through merit"). *Viṣeṇa vadhyaḥ* ("to be killed by poison") becomes *viṣyaḥ śatruḥ* ("an enemy to be killed by poison"). *Mūlena anāmyam* ("not to be bent down, i.e., not to be overcome, by the root-price") becomes *mūlyaṃ kṣetram* ("a field whose price is its root-cost"). *Mūlena samaḥ* ("equal to the root-price") becomes *mūlyaḥ paṭo jātaḥ* ("a cloth has been produced that is equal to its cost"). *Sītayā samitam* ("measured by a furrow") becomes *sītyam*. *Dvisītyam*, *trisītyam*. *Tulayā sammitam* ("weighed by a balance") becomes *tulyaṃ kanakam* ("gold that is equal in weight").
In the rule prescribing the suffix *yat* after *ratha*, *sītā*, and *hal*, the operation applies to the final phoneme of those stems.
The suffix *sīya* is applied after the words *dharma*,
*pathin*, *artha*, and *nyāya* when they mean "not deviating from."

That which does not deviate from these [is called *dharmya*]. A king who does not deviate from dharma is *dharmya*. [The suffix -ya is used] in the sense of "suitable" (*pathya*), "beneficial" (*arthya*), "just" (*nyāya*), and in the sense of "composed in meter" (*chandas*).
In this context, that which is produced by *chandas*—that is, by desire—is called *chandasya*, meaning "created by will.
Furthermore, the suffix *aṇ* is applied after the word *uras*.
A son born from the breast (*uras*) is *aurasa*;
and that which is *urasya* means dear to the heart (*hṛdayasya priyaḥ*).
The suffix *yat* occurs after the word *hṛdaya* in the sense of "dear to"; thus, *hṛdyaḥ*. There is no application [of this suffix] when referring to a son.
[The suffix *yat* also occurs] after *bandhana* in the sense of a "sage" (*ṛṣi*).

The suffix *ṛṣi* is applied after the word *veda* in the sense of "heart" (*hṛdaya*), and after [words ending in] *bandhana* in the sense of a "mantra"; thus, *hṛdayasya bandhanam* becomes *hṛdya*, meaning a mantra for subjugation.
The suffix *mat* is applied after *jana*, *jana*, and *hal* in the senses of instrument (*karaṇa*), chatter (*jalpa*), and drawing (*karṣa*) respectively.

The suffix *yat* occurs after words such as *mata* when they function as the instrument (*karaṇa*) and so forth. For example: *matasya karaṇam* = *matyam*; *janasya jalpaḥ* = *janyaḥ*; *halasya karṣaḥ* = *halyaḥ*; *dvihalyaḥ*.
[It also occurs] in the sense of "skilled therein" (*tatra sādhuh*).

In this sense, that which is appropriate for the *sāmans* is *sāmanya*, as in *vipraḥ sāmanyaḥ* (a sage skilled in the *sāmans*), *brahmaṇyaḥ* (devoted to sacred knowledge), *karmaṇyaḥ* (fit for action), or *vaṃśyaḥ* (belonging to a lineage).
Here, *sādhuḥ* means either "proficient" or "suitable.
The suffix *khañ* (*-īya*) is applied after words such as *pratijana*.

The suffix *khañ* shall be applied after these [words]. For example: one who is good toward all people (*pratijana*) is *prātijanīna*; one who is good in battle (*saṃyuga*) is *sāṃyugīna*; one who is good for all people (*sarvajanān*) is *sārvajanīna*.
After the word *bhakta*, the suffix *ṇa* is applied.
The suffix *sādhu* is applied after the word *bhakta* to form *bhākta*, meaning "fit for rice";
the suffix *ṇya* is applied after the word *pariṣad*.
One who is good in an assembly is *pāriṣadya*. Jayāditya maintains that the suffix *ṇa* is also desired [after this word], as in *pāriṣada*.
After words such as *kathā*, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied.
One who is skilled in a discourse is called *kāthikaḥ*, *vaikathikaḥ*, or *vārttikaḥ*. After words such as *guḍa* and others, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñ* are applied.
The word *gauḍika* refers to sugarcane that is good for molasses (*guḍa*); *kaulmāṣika* refers to barley; *sāṃgrāmika* refers to a warrior; and *prāvāsika* refers to a merchant.
[The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after the words *pathin*, *atithi*, *vasati*, and *svapati*.

The suffix *ḍhañ* occurs after these [words] when meaning "good for" (*sādhu*). For example: *pathi sādhu* = *pātheyam* (provisions for a journey); *ātithayam* (hospitality); *vāsateyam*, *vāsateyī* (lodging); *svāpateyam* (wealth belonging to one's own master).
After the word *sabhā*, the suffix *ya* is applied.
It may be so. One who is proficient in the assembly is called *sabhya*.
[The suffix] *ḍha* occurs in the Veda (*chandas*).
The *Chandaḥsūtra* is one [work];
[the author] resided at Samānatīrtha.

The suffix *ya* occurs after *samānatīrtha* in the sense of "one who dwells there"; thus, *satīrthya* means "those who have the same teacher. In the rule *tīrthe ye*, the substitution of *sa* for *sa-* applies; here, *tīrtha* means "a place of pilgrimage" (*udakadarśana*) as well as "a teacher.
[Furthermore,] the suffix *cha* is added after *samānodara* with the acute accent on the first syllable, meaning "one who has lain in the same womb" (a uterine brother).
In this matter, he who would be a brother from the same womb is one who is born from the same womb as [the deceased].
From this [base *samāna-*], that which would be [the meaning] is "one who has slept in the same womb" (*sodarya*). By the rule *vibhāṣodare*, there is the substitution of *sa-* for *samāna-*.
Now, from here until the end of the chapter, the word *chandas* (Vedic) is the governing authority (*adhikāra*). Furthermore, it applies in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*).
These are Vedic rules (*chāndasāni sūtrāṇi*).
In the Vedic language (chandas), [the suffix -am is used] for the locative case (bhave).
The suffix *ḍyañ* is applied after the words *pātha* and *nadī*.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the words *veśanta* and *himavat*.
After the word *srotas*, the suffixes *ḍya* and *ḍyaṅ* are optionally applied.
From that which arises from the womb, the herd, and the kin.
It may be: "brother from the same creation," "a calf from the same herd," "favor from afar," and "wealth from Tugra."
Because it is from the foremost.
It may be so. [The suffixes] gha and cha [are applied] after the word *agrya*.
The suffix *gha* occurs after the words *samudra* and *abhra*, forming the forms *samudriya* and *abhrīya*. The forms *agriya* and *agrīya* are also [derived in this manner].
The suffix *gha* occurs after these two [words]. *Samudriyam*, *abhriyam*.
And the suffix *cha* also [occurs]: *samudrīyam*, *abhrīyam*.
[The suffix *yañ* occurs] after *barhis* when the meaning is "given upon the sacrificial grass": *bārhaspatyam*.
The share and the duty of the messenger.
From this [it follows] that it shall be the office of a messenger,
the slayer of Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas.
The suffix *praśasya* is applied after the words *revatī*, *jagatī*, and *haviṣyā*.
The property of an Asura.
In illusion, there is no jewel.

When the word *tadvat* (possessing that) refers to these [bricks], the suffix *manuṭ* is applied as a *mantra* for the laying down (*upadhāna*), and there is also elision (*luk*) of the *matup* suffix in the case of bricks (*iṣṭakā*).
The vowel *a* is followed by the consonant *m*.
The suffix *matup* occurs after the word *mūrdhan* when it is followed by words meaning "companions."
The suffix *matup* is applied in the sense of possession when referring to a month or the body.

That which [is derived] from these two [words]: *nabhas* and *madhu*. Where there are clouds, it is *nabhasyaḥ* (the month of Śrāvaṇa); *sahasyaḥ* (the month of Pauṣa); *tapasyaḥ* (the month of Māgha); *tejasyā* (the body).
After *madhu*, the suffix *ñya* is also applied.

The word *mādhava* refers to the month. Likewise, it should be stated that there is elision (*luk*), and the letters *a*, *i*, and *r*. *Luk*: "Madhu" is here present [in this month], thus *madhur māsaḥ* (the month of Madhu). *Akāra*: "iṭ" is here present, thus *iṣaḥ*; "ūrj" is here present, thus *ūrjo māsaḥ* (the month of Ūrja). *Ikāra*: "śuci" is here present, thus *śucir māsaḥ* (the month of Śuci). *Repha*: "śukra" is here present, thus *śukro māsaḥ* (the month of Śukra).
[The suffix] *yat* and *kha* occur after *ojas* when meaning "on the day of."
The suffix *yaL* is applied after the word *bhaga* when it signifies "dwelling," "fame," and so forth.
Kha-ca.
And there is also [the rule] regarding the *mināy* vowels made by the predecessors.
Consecrated with water.
The two [sacrificial posts] are equal to a thousand.
And in the case of the mind as well.
He who is worthy of Soma,
and also of me.
Of spring.
And in the sense of a collection of wealth.
The suffix *gha* is applied after a word denoting a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*).
The suffix *cha* (forming *nakṣatrīya*) and *cha* with the augment *nakṣatrīya*;
[the suffix] *tāti* comes after the word *sarvadeva*.
In the hand of Śiva, who brings peace and freedom from misfortune.
The suffix *tāti* occurs after these [words] with the sense of the instrumental case (*kara*). Examples are *śivatātiḥ*, *śantātiḥ*, and *ariṣṭatātiḥ*.

Although these words are Vedic (*chāndasa*), they are occasionally employed in the common language (*bhāṣā*) according to the *Trikāṇḍa*; or else, due to their inclusion in Bhāguri’s treatise, or because they are technical names not derived from verbal roots, they are in every way correct in the common language.
And [the suffix *kṛtya* is used] in the sense of existence (*bhāva*).
The Chandaḥ Sūtra.
Thus ends the fourth quarter of the fourth chapter in the Bhāṣāvṛtti composed by the Great Preceptor Śrī Puruṣottamadeva.
And the section on the *ṭhak* affix is completed.
The suffix *cha* is applied after a word ending in the locative case when it means "purchased previously."
In the sense of "beneficial before being purchased" (krītāt prāg hitam), the suffix *cha* should be stated;
[and] *yat* is applied after words such as *go*.

The suffix *yat* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *cha* after words ending in the vowel *u* that belong to the *go*-group. Examples: *śaṅkavyaṃ dāru* (wood for a pin), *caravyās taṇḍulāḥ* (rice for sacrificial porridge), *kamaṇḍalavyā mṛd* (clay for a water-pot), *saktavyā dhānāḥ* (barley-grains for flour). Regarding the *go*-group: *gavyam*. For the word *nābhi*, there is the substitution of *nabha*: the base form is *nābhi*; *nabhyaṃ kāṣṭham* (the wood for the nave).
After the word *śvan*, there is optionally vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*), and the resulting vowel is long: *śune hitam* (beneficial for a dog) results in either *śunyam* or *śūnyam*.
After *ūdhas*, the suffix *yat* occurs, and there is also the substitution of *anaṅ*. [Thus:
*ūdhanyaḥ*.
Also after *kambala*, when it is a name (*saṃjñā*).

The word *kambalanābhi* (a woolen blanket) may be used; *kambalya* refers to one hundred palas of wool. The suffix [ya] is optionally applied after words for sacrificial offerings (*havis*) and those beginning with *apūpa*.

Or rather, [the suffix] *yat* may occur after these: denoting sacrificial offerings (*havir-vācinaḥ*)—*āmikṣyam* or *āmikṣīyam* [referring to] curd; *puroḍāśyam* or *puroḍāśīyam* [referring to] the sacrificial cake (*auṣadha*). From the word *havis*, because it is listed in the *gav-ādi* group, *yat* is obligatory: *haviṣyam*. From *apūpa* and so on: *apūpyam* or *apūpīyam*; *taṇḍulyam* or *taṇḍulīyam*. And from words for food preparations (*anna-vikāra*): *surīyāḥ* or *suryāḥ* [referring to] rice grains (*taṇḍula*), meaning "beneficial for that."

In this sense, the suffix prescribed [by the rule] shall apply: *vatsīyam* (beneficial for calves), *navatṛṇam* (fresh grass), *paśavyam* (beneficial for cattle); *gavyam* (beneficial for cows); *paṭavyam* (beneficial for cloth).
The suffix *yat* is applied after words denoting parts of the body.

It may be so. That which is beneficial for the staff is *daṇḍyam* (punishable), *kaṇyam* (to be gained), *tālavyam* (palatal), *nābhyaṃ tailam* (navel-oil), *auṣṭhyam* (labial), and *mūrdhanyam* (cerebral).
Also [the suffix -ya is added] after *ratha*: that which is beneficial for a chariot is *rathyā*, a carriage-way.
And [the word] *vṛṣa* when it means a Brahmin, as well as *khala*, *yava*, *māṣa*, and *tila*, [form a tatpuruṣa compound with a word ending in the sixth case].

The suffix *yat* is applied in the sense of "beneficial for" (*hita*) these [words]. For example: *khalyam* (beneficial for the threshing floor), *yavyam*, *māṣyam*, *tilyam*, *vṛṣyam*. A king who is beneficial for the *brahman* is called *brahmaṇyaḥ*.
The suffix *thyan* is applied after the words *aja* and *avi*.
The suffix *thyan* occurs after these two [words] when they mean "beneficial for" (*hita*). Examples: *ajathyā bhūmiḥ* ("land beneficial for goats"), *avithyā*.
After words ending in *ātman*, *viśvajana*, or as the final member of a compound with *bhoktṛ*, the suffix *kha* occurs.

The suffix *kha* (īna) is used in the sense of "beneficial for" (*hita*) these [words]. The explicit mention of the letter *n* in *ātman* is for the purpose of indicating the limit [of the application]. *Ātmane hitam* (beneficial for oneself) becomes *ātmanīna*. *Kṣaṇaṃ mayā viśvajanīnam ucyate* (for a moment, I speak what is beneficial for all people). *Mātṛbhogīṇaḥ* (belonging to the mother's enjoyment/use). From *ācārya*, there is the substitution of *aṇ* for *ñ*: *ācāryabhogīnaḥ* (belonging to the teacher's enjoyment/use). *svabhogīnaḥ* (belonging to one's own enjoyment/use). According to the commentary (*vṛtti*), *bhoga* means the body. And from *pañcajana*, the suffix *kha* (īna) is used. One who delights in singers, musicians, dancers, female slaves, and jesters is indeed *pañcajanīnaḥ*. From *sarvajana*, the suffixes *ṭhañ* (ika) and *kha* (īna) are used. *Sārvajanikaḥ* (belonging to all people) and *sarvajanīnaḥ* (beneficial for all people).
The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *mahājana* to form a derivative denoting "belonging to" or "relating to. Thus, *māhājanikaḥ*.

The application of the suffix is prescribed after the compound *viśvajana*, etc., when it is a *karmadhāraya*; therefore, it does not apply after a genitive (*ṣaṣṭhī*) compound and so forth—hence, one says *viśvajanīyam*.
After the words *sarva* and *puruṣa*, the suffixes *ṇa* and *ḍhañ* are applied respectively.

The suffixes *ṇa* and *ḍhañ* are applied after these two [words] when the sense is "beneficial for that" (*hita*). In that regard, it should be stated that *ṇa* optionally applies after the word *sarva*. Thus: *sārvaḥ* or *sarvīyaḥ*.

After the word *puruṣa*, the suffix *ḍhañ* is applied in the senses of "killing," "modification," "collection," "made by him," and "done for his sake. Thus: *pauruṣeyaḥ* refers to killing and so forth.
The suffix *khañ* is applied after the words *māṇava* and *caraka*.

The suffix *khañ* shall be applied after these two [words] when they signify "beneficial for that. Examples: *māṇavīnaḥ*, *cārakīṇaḥ*. [Also: when the purpose of that [product] is indicated, [the suffix is applied] to the raw material (*prakṛti*) from which the modification (*vikṛti*) is derived.
When there is a modification of the object, the suffix shall be applied as prescribed, provided that the base word expresses that specific purpose:
*aṅgārebhya etāni aṅgārīyāṇi kāṣṭhāni* ("these are wood for charcoal"), *yūpīyaṃ dāru* ("wood for a sacrificial post"), *śaṅkavyam* ("for a stake"), *picavyaḥ kārpāsaḥ* ("cotton for a brush").
[The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after *chadi*, *upadhi*, and *bali*.

The suffix *ḍhañ* shall be applied after these [stems] when the sense is "for that purpose" (*tadartha*) in the case of the raw material (*prakṛti*). For example: *chādiṣeyāṇi tṛṇāni* ("grass for a roof"); according to the traditional rule (*smṛti*), *ḍhañ* is applied to *upadhī* in its own sense (*svārthe*): *aupadheyaṃ rathadāru* ("wood for a chariot"). *Bāleyāḥ taṇḍulāḥ* ("rice for an offering").
After the words *ṛṣabha* and *upānaha*, the suffix *ñya* is applied.

From these two [stems], likewise, the suffix *ññya* shall be applied: *ārṣabhyaḥ* (a calf belonging to a bull) and *aupānahyam* (leather for a sandal). The suffix *añ* is applied after the word *carman*.

From a derivative form [denoting] leather, the suffix *añ* occurs to denote its source-material; thus, from *vārddhra* or *vāratra*, meaning "leather," we derive *vārdhra* or *vāratra* meaning "that which belongs to it" or "that which is on it."

In these two senses, the suffix prescribed [by the rule] shall apply: *prākārīyā iṣṭakāḥ* means "bricks for which a wall (*prākāra*) may exist"; *prāsādīyā bhūmiḥ* means "ground on which a palace (*prāsāda*) may exist.
After the word *parikhā*, the suffix *ḍhañ* [is applied].
The suffix *ḍhañ* shall be applied to this [root] in the sense of "eastern" (*prāc*). An example is *pārikheyī bhūmiḥ*.
When the two [sides] are full, it is the limit.
The suffix *iṣṭhan* follows [a stem] preceded by *pra*.

From the rule *tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ* onwards, for meanings prior to that, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñ* are to be understood. *gaupucchikam*: bought with a cow’s tail. *pārāyaṇikaḥ*: one who performs the *pārāyaṇa*. *dvaipārāyaṇikaḥ*: one who performs two *pārāyaṇas*. *sāptatikam*: [bought] with seventy.
[This concludes] the section on the *ārhīya* (suffixes denoting price) among the *taddhita* formations.
The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after [words ending in] *arha*, *daṇḍa*, *gopa*, *chāyā*, *saṃkhyā*, and *parimāṇa*.

The prefix *āṅ* is used in the sense of "pervading" (*abhividhi*). Regarding the rule "one who deserves that" (*tadarhati*), the suffix *ṭhak* should be stated in the sense of "he buys," "it is the cause," "he is the master," "it is known," "it is water," "he takes it," "he carries it," "he brings it," "it arises in him," "he removes it," "he cooks it," "he has abandoned it," "he throws it," or "he deserves it. Examples: *naiṣkikaḥ* (one who deserves a *niṣka*). Because of the exclusion of words such as *gopuccha*, only *ṭhañ* applies in the sense of "before *vat*" (*prāgvat*); e.g., *gaupucchikaḥ* (worth a cow’s tail), *sāptatikaḥ* (worth seventy), *prāsthikaḥ* (worth a *prastha*).
There is a difference in accent. [The suffix *ṭhak* applies] after *niṣka* and other such words when not in a compound.

The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words such as *niṣka* and others when they are not in a compound, in the sense of "worth" (*ārhīya*). For example: *naiṣkikaḥ* ("worth one *niṣka*"). [The examples of these words are: *niṣka*, *paṇa*, *māṣa*, *droṇa*, *ṣaṣṭi*, *pāda*.
However, in a compound, only the suffix *ṭhañ* is used—for instance, *dvinaiṣkikam* ("worth two *niṣkas*").

Precisely because of the mention of "non-compound" (*asamāsa*) here, there is an application of the rule regarding the inclusion of that which ends in such a word (*tadantavidhi*) in the preceding cases. By this, [we derive] *gavyam*, *atigavyam*, *dantyam*, *rājadantyam*, and so forth. From here onwards, the traditional rule (*smṛti*) is: "Before the suffix *ṭhak* (which occurs after words meaning 'prior to'—*prāgvateḥ*), when a numeral is the prior member, there is the inclusion of that which ends in it, provided there is no elision (*aluk*). Thus: *pārāyaṇikaḥ*, *dvaipārāyaṇikaḥ*. And [the rule is]: "After the word *śata*, the suffixes *ṭhan* and *yat* occur, except when the sense is 'one hundred'. Thus: *śatikaḥ* / *śatyaḥ*. (But not *śataḥ* when it means one hundred.)

The suffixes *ṭhan* and *yat* occur after the word *śata* when it signifies "worthiness" (*arha*) for that amount; this serves as an exception to [the rule for] *kan*. Examples: *śatyaḥ aśvaḥ* ("a horse worth a hundred"), *śatikaḥ kambalaḥ* ("a blanket worth a hundred"), *śatikaṃ vāsaḥ* ("a garment worth a hundred"), or *śatyaḥ*. Why say "when not meaning a hundred itself"? (Because in cases like) *śatamadhyāyāḥ parimāṇam asya śatakaṃ nidānam* ("this manual has a hundred chapters as its measure") or *śatakaṃ kāvyam* ("a poem of a hundred [verses]"), it is simply "a hundred.
[This is governed by the rule: *kan* occurs after a numeral that does not end in *ati* or *śad*.

The suffix *kan* is applied after a numeral when forming words denoting things worthy of that number. Examples: *pañcakaḥ* ("worth five"), *bahukaḥ* ("worth many"), *gaṇakaḥ* ("worth a group"). Why "after one not ending in *ati* or *śad*"? Consider: *sāptatikaḥ* ("seventieth") and *pāñcāśatkaḥ* ("fiftieth").
There is no prohibition for words ending in *ḍati*: *katikaḥ*.
After a word ending in *vatu*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied.
After a numeral ending in *vat*, the suffixes *kan* or *ḍa* may optionally be applied. Thus, one forms either *tāvatikaḥ* or *tāvatkaḥ*.
After the words *viṃśati* and *triṃśat*, the suffix *ḍvun* is applied, provided it does not form a technical name (*saṃjñā*).
A split of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) is made here. From these two [suffixes], *kan* shall occur in the sense of "worth" (*ārhīya*). Thus: *viṃśatikaḥ* ("worth twenty"), *triṃśatkaḥ* ("worth thirty").

When not used as a name (*asaṃjñā*), the suffix *ḍvun* occurs: *viṃśakaḥ*, *triṃśakaḥ*. In the case of *viṃśati*, there is elision of the final syllable (*ṭilopa*) before a suffix beginning with *ḍ*. After *kaṃsa*, the suffix *ṭiṭhan* occurs.

The suffix *ṭiṭhan* is applied after the word *kaṃsa* when it denotes a measure, provided the object is something worthy of that measure (*ārhīya*). For example: *kaṃsikaḥ paṭaḥ* (a cloth worth one *kaṃsa*) and *kaṃsikī* (a female slave worth one *kaṃsa*). The vowel *i* [in the suffix] is for the sake of pronunciation. [The suffix *ṭiṭhan* is also applied] after the word *ardha*. For example: *ardhikaḥ* and *ardhikī*.
After the word *kārṣāpaṇa*, the suffix *ṭiṭhan* is optionally applied, and there is also the substitution of *prati* [for *kārṣāpaṇa*]. For example: *kārṣāpaṇikaḥ* or *pratikaḥ*.
The suffix *añ* may optionally be applied after *śūrpa*.
In the case of items worthy of being purchased, there may be other suffixes than *añ* after the word *śūrpa*; thus, one may say either *śaurpam* or *śaurpikam*.
After the words *śatamāna*, *viṃśatika*, *sahasra*, and *vasana*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these [words] when they denote a price (*ārhīya*). Examples: *śātamānam*, *vaiśatikam*, *sāhasram*, *vāsanam*.
When preceded by *adhyardha* or being a *dvigu* compound, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix, provided it does not form a technical name (*asaṃjñāyām*).

The suffix *arhīya* (expressing "worth" or "purchasable for") is elided after a *dvigu* compound beginning with *adhyardha*. For example: *adhyardhakamseṇa krītam* becomes *adhyardhakaṃsam*. After a *dvigu* compound: *dvikaṃsam*, *trikaṃsam*. Why specify "not a name"? [Because in the case of a name, it is not elided: *pāñcakapālikaḥ*.
The Vibhāṣā [states] that it is by two thousand kārṣāpaṇas.

Up to this point, the preceding suffix may optionally be elided. For example: *adhyardhakārṣāpaṇam* or *adhyardhakārṣāpaṇikam*; *dvikārṣāpaṇikam* or *dvikārṣāpaṇam*; *adhyardhasahasram* or *adhyardhasāhasram*. When a numeral is followed by a word denoting a year, there is vṛddhi of the first vowel of the final member.

And [the suffix *kan* is added] after the words *suvarṇa* and *śatamāna*. [Examples: *adhyardhasuvarṇam*, or *adhyardhasauvarṇikam*; *adhyardhaśatamānam*, or *adhyardhaśātamānam*; *dvisuvarṇam*, or *dvisauvarṇikam*; *dviśatamānam*, or *dviśātamānam*. In these cases, there is vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of the final syllable of the second member according to the rule "of that which ends in a measure-word" (*parimāṇāntasya*).
[The suffix *kan* is also added] after the word *niṣka* when preceded by the words *dvi* or *tri*.

The suffix *īya* following words such as *niṣka* preceded by *dvi-* and so on may optionally be elided. Thus: *dviniṣkam* or *dvinaiṣkikam*; *triniṣkam* or *trinaiṣkikam*. It is also elided after words preceded by *bahu-*: *bahuniṣkam* or *bahunaiṣkikam*. [The suffix is also elided] after *bista*.

And likewise, from *bista*, there shall be [the suffix *ka*]: *dvibistam* or *dvibaistikam*; *tribistam* or *tribaistikam*; *bahubistam* or *bahubaistikam*. After the word *viṃśatika*, the suffix *kha* [is applied].
In place of the suffix *ārhīya*, there shall be the suffix *kha* when *luk* (elision) is applicable. Examples: *adhyardhaviṃśatikīnaṃ*, *dviviṃśatikīnaṃ*, *khāryāikaṇ*.
In the sense of "belonging to," the suffix *ka* may optionally be added after the word *khārī*. Thus: *adhyardhakhārīkam*, *dvikhārīkam*.
It is also added after *kākiṇī*: *adhyardhakākiṇīkam*, *dvikākiṇīkam*. Furthermore, it is added after these two words when they stand alone: *khārīkam*, *kākiṇīkam*.
That which is [taken] from five hundred pādas and māṣas.
From these [words], there shall be [the suffixes -īya and -ika]: *adhyardhaśāṇyam*, *dvipaṇyam*, *adhyardhapādyam*, *dvipādyam*, *adhyardhamāṣyam*, *adhyardhaśatyam*;
or [the suffix -ika] may optionally follow *śāṇa*.

From *śāṇa*, there may be either [the suffixes] *yat* or *adhyardhaśāṇya*. In the alternative case, only *ṭhañ* and *ña* are applied—namely, *adhyardhaśāṇa* or *dviśāṇa*. From *śata*, [the suffixes] *yat* or *adhyardhaśatma*, or *adhyardhaśata*; *dviśatma*, or *dviśata*.
And the suffix *aṇ* is applied after [compounds] consisting of two or three prior members.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word ending in *dvitri* followed by *śāṇa*, and *yat* may optionally also be used. Thus: *dvaiśāṇam* or *dviśāṇyam*. There is also elision (*luk*): *dviśāṇam*.
[These denote] "bought with that."

In this sense, thirteen suffixes beginning with *ṭhañ* and *ña*, as prescribed prior to the rule for *vati*, are to be understood. [Examples: *sāptatikaṃ* (purchased for seventy); *naiṣkikaṃ* (purchased for a niṣka). *Maudgikaṃ* (purchased for mung beans); *śatyaṃ*, *śatikaṃ* (purchased for a hundred). From a numeral that does not end in *ati* or *śat*, the suffix *kan* is applied: *dvikaṃ* (worth two), *trikaṃ* (worth three), *pañcakaṃ* (worth five).
[The suffix *thañ* is also used] in the sense of "the cause of that" when it refers to a conjunction or an occurrence.

*Saṃyoga* is an accidental connection; *utpāta* is an omen indicating good or evil fortune. In this sense, suffixes such as *ṭhañ* and others are to be understood. A connection with a creditor caused by a hundred [coins] is *śatyaḥ* or *śatikaḥ*; the throbbing of the right eye caused by a thousand [coins] is *sāhasram*. Also, from the words *vāta*, *pitta*, *śleṣman*, and *sannipāta*, there is the designation of their pacification or provocation: that which pacifies or provokes wind (*vāta*) is *vātikam*; likewise, *paittikam*, *śleṣmikam*, and *sānnipātikam*.
The immeasurable expanse of the divine, such as that of the horse and so forth, is beyond calculation.

The suffix *yat* occurs after the word *go* and after words consisting of two syllables (*dvyac*) in the sense of "being the cause" (*nimitta*). It sets aside the suffixes *ṭhañ*, *ñ*, and others. Examples: *gonimittaṃ saṃyoga utpāto vā gavyaḥ* ("a conjunction or portent caused by cows is *gavya*"); after a word of two syllables: *dhanyaḥ* ("caused by wealth"), *svargyaḥ* ("caused by heaven"), *yaśasyam* ("caused by fame"), *āyuṣyam* ("caused by life"). Why is there a prohibition for words beginning with a numeral? [Answer: *pañcānāṃ nimittaṃ pañcakaḥ prāsthakaḥ* ("the cause of five measures is *pañcaka-prāsthaka*"). The group beginning with *aśva* [takes *ṭhak*]: *āśvikaḥ* ("caused by horses"), *hāstikaḥ* ("caused by elephants"). After the word *putra*, the suffix *cha* also occurs.

The suffix *cha* (īya) shall be used after the word *putra*, as well as [the suffix *yat*]. That which is the cause (*nimitta*) for a son—whether it be a conjunction (*saṃyoga*) or a portent (*utpāta*)—is called *putrīya* or *putrya*.
After the words *sarvabhūmi* and *pṛthivī*, the suffixes *aṇ* and *ña* [are respectively applied].

From these two [words], the suffixes *aṇ* and *ñya* respectively occur in the sense of "cause" (*nimitta*). [Examples: *sārvabhaumaḥ* (belonging to the whole earth); it belongs to the *anuśatikādi* group. *Pārthivaḥ* is that which has the earth as its cause;
[it also means] the lord thereof.
In this sense, those two [suffixes] would be applied to both of them. One who is the lord of the entire earth is a *sārvabhauma* or a *pārthiva*;
in that regard, there is also the form *vidita*.
In this sense, the suffixes *aṇ* and *añ* are applied after these two [words]. Examples: *sārvabhaumaḥ* (ruling over the whole earth), *pārthivaḥ* (belonging to the earth).
After the words *loka* and *sarvaloka*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied.

The suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *-ika*) occurs after these two [words] in the sense of "known therein. For example: *laukikaḥ* ("known in the world"). That Rāma is *sārvailaukikaḥ* ("known among all people in the world"). This belongs to the *anuśatikādi* group. [The suffix *ṭhañ* also occurs] in the sense of "his sowing" (*tasya vāpaḥ*).

In this sense, the suffix prescribed [by the previous rule] shall apply. A field that is the sowing of a *prastha* is called *prāsthika*. [Similarly,] *drauṇika*. "Sowing" (*vāpa*) means that in which something is sown. After the word *pātra*, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied.

It may be so: the sowing of a vessel is a field belonging to that vessel (*pātrika*). Because of the suffix *ṣit*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied—thus, "the ground belonging to the vessel" (*pātrikī bhūmiḥ*).
[The suffix *ṭhañ* is added] when interest, profit, gain, toll, or a gift is given for that [field] in this [place].

In this sense, the suffix *pratyaya* shall be applied as prescribed. When five units of interest, profit, tax, or fee are given on this [capital], it is called *pañcakaḥ*; likewise, *śatikaḥ* or *śatyaḥ*. There is also an extension [of the rule] for the sense of the dative case: when a hundred units of interest and so forth are given to him, he is a *śatya* Brahmin.
After words meaning "a part" (*pūraṇa*) and after *ardha*, the suffix *ṭhan* is added.

The suffix *ṭhan* shall be applied after words ending in *pūraṇa* (ordinal numbers) and after the word *ardha*. For example: *dvitīyikaḥ* ("that in which a second [part] consisting of an increase, etc., is given"), *pañcamikaḥ*, and *ardhikaḥ*.
Furthermore, the suffix *ya* is also applied after the word *bhāga*.
The suffixes *ya* and *ṭhan* may occur after the word *bhāga*. When something such as interest (*vṛddhi*) is given in this [transaction], it is called *bhāgya* or *bhāgika*.
[Furthermore, the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs] after words beginning with *vaṃśa* when they denote a load (*bhāra*), in the senses of "carrying that," "bearing that," or "bringing that."

The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after words such as *vaṃśa* when they denote a "load" (*bhāra*) in three senses: carrying, bearing, or bringing forth. For example, one who carries, bears, brings forth, or produces a load of bamboo is called *vāṃśabhārikaḥ*; likewise, *bālvajabhārikaḥ*. After the words *vasna* and *dravya*, the suffixes *ṭhan* and *kan* respectively are applied.
From these two [roots], these two [suffixes] may occur: *vasrikaḥ* (one who wears, carries, or brings clothes), *dravyakaḥ* (one who possesses substance), and [one who] originates, removes, or cooks.

In these cases, it should be as prescribed. That which can hold or cooks one *prastha* is called *prāsthika*, as in *prāsthikaḥ kaṭāhaḥ* (a pot that holds one *prastha*). Similarly, *khārīkaḥ*. "Capacity" (*sambhava*) means not exceeding the measure; "gathering" (*saṃharaṇa*) means taking up. [The suffix] *aṇ* is also applied after *droṇa* when used with the verb *pacati* (to cook). A pot that cooks one *droṇa* is called *droṇaḥ kaṭāhaḥ*; alternatively, a cooking vessel is called *drauṇī* or *drauṇikī* sthālī. After the words *āḍhaka*, *ācita*, and *pātra*, the suffix *kha* is optionally applied.

After these [words], when they signify the aforementioned meanings, the suffix *kha* (i.e., *ika*) may optionally be applied. For example: *āḍhakīnā* or *āḍhakikī* [meaning "a field that yields, receives, or cooks one *āḍhaka*"]; *ācitīnā* or *ācitikī*; *pātrīṇā* or *pātrikī*.
After a *dvigu* compound, the suffix *ṣṭhan* (i.e., *ika*, with the feminine form *ikī*) is also applied.

After a *dvigu* compound ending in *āḍhaka* and so forth, when it refers to its constituent parts (*pūrvārtha*), the suffixes *ṣṭhan* or *kha* may optionally be added. Because they are marked with *ṣ*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied. Thus, one has *dvyāḍhakikī* or *dvyāḍhakīnā*. Similarly, *dvyācitī* or *dvyācitīnā*. In the alternative case, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied; by the rule *adhyardhapūrva-* (Pāṇini 5.1.28), this suffix is elided, and by the rule *dvigoḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.21), the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied: thus, *dvyāḍhakī*. For *dvyācita*, the suffix is simply *a*. After *kulija*, there is elision (*luk*) or the suffix *kha*.

After a *dvigu* compound ending in *kulija*, the suffixes *luc* and *kha* may optionally occur; by the force of the word "and" (*ca*), the suffix *ṣṭhan* also occurs. Thus, there are the forms *dvikulijī*, *dvikulijīnā*, or *dvikulijikī*. In the alternative case, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ña* are heard as well—namely, *dvai-kulijikī*. [The suffixes *aṇ*, *ñ*, *ṭhak*, etc.,] also occur after a word denoting a *dvigu* when it signifies "this is its share," "its price," or "its wages. *so'syāṃśavasnabhṛtayaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.1.47) means: the suffixes [mentioned in the preceding rules] occur after a *dvigu* compound when it expresses "this is its portion," "its price," or "its wages."

In this sense, it should be as prescribed: *pañcāṃśāḥ* (five parts), *vasrāṇi* (cloths), or *bhṛtayaḥ* (wages) belonging to him constitute *pañcakaḥ* (a group of five). Similarly, *śatyaḥ*, *śatikaḥ*, and *saptakaḥ*.
[The suffix *ka* is added] in the sense of "this is its measure."

[The suffix] shall be applied as prescribed after a word in the first case (nominative) that signifies a measure (*parimāṇa*). *Prasthaḥ parimāṇam asya* ("A *prastha* is its measure") → *prāsthikaḥ rāśiḥ* ("a heap measuring a *prastha*"). *Khārīkaḥ*. *Vārṣaśatiko yāgaḥ* ("a sacrifice lasting a hundred years"). *Ṣaṣṭir jīvitaparimāṇam asya* ("Sixty is his life-span") → *ṣaṣṭikaḥ*. In the case of *dve ṣaṣṭhī jīvitaparimāṇam asya*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is elided by the rule *adhyardhapūrva-*. Since the base [of the compound] is already established by the phrase *so 'sya* ("that belongs to him"), the subsequent mention of *tad asya* ("that is its") serves to re-introduce the suffix *ṭhañ*. And because of the force of its specific prescription, there is no elision (*aluk*), according to Jayāditya. [This applies] after a numeral (*saṃkhyā*) and after the word *saṃvatsara*.

And when a numeral is the first member [of a compound], there is vṛddhi of the subsequent member. Examples: *dviṣāṣṭikaḥ* ("consisting of two times sixty-four"), *dvisāptatikaḥ* ("consisting of two times seventy"), *trisāptatikaḥ* ("consisting of three times seventy").
[Furthermore, there is vṛddhi] after a numeral when it denotes a name (*saṃjñā*), a collection (*saṃgha*), a rule (*sūtra*), or a lesson (*adhyayana*).

When expressing a number, [the suffix] shall apply as prescribed to convey the sense of "consisting of. In the case of a technical name (*saṃjñā*), the rule applies to the word's own meaning (*svārtha*): *pañcakā nakulāḥ* ("five-musked mongooses"). When it signifies a measure (*parimāṇa*): *pañcakaḥ saṅghaḥ* ("a group of five"). Regarding the Sūtras: *aṣṭakaṃ pāṇinīyaṃ sūtram* ("the Pāṇinian Sūtra consists of eight chapters"). *pañcakamadhyayanam* ("a study consisting of five recitations"). [The following are the forms for specific numbers:
*paṅkti*, *viṃśati*, *triṃśat*, *catvāriṃśat*, *pañcāśat*, *ṣaṣṭi*, *saptati*, *aśīti*, *navati*, *śata*.

Words such as *paṅkti* and others are correct [as they are]. Like *sahasra* and so on, these are technical terms (*saṃjñāśabda*). Two *pañcatī* make a *paṅkti*; two *daśatī* make a *viṃśati*—this and so forth is merely an etymological derivation (*vyutpatti*), not a grammatical analysis (*anvaya*). As it is stated in the Bhāṣya: "Or rather, there is no [need for] a formal rule (*anārambha*), because they are understood as nominal stems (*prātipadika*), just as in the case of *sahasra* and so on";
and: "*pañca* and *daśa* [denote] a group."

These two suffixes are optionally applied as a class [of taddhita suffixes]. *Pañca* is its measure: *pañcada* is the group; alternatively, with the suffix *kan*, it is *pañcaka*. *Daśa* is the group: *daśada* or *daśaka*.
After *sapta*, the suffix *añ* occurs in the Veda.
*Chandaḥsūtram*:
The suffix *ḍaṇ* is applied after the words "thirty" (*triṃśat*) and "forty" (*catvāriṃśat*) when followed by the word "Brāhmaṇa" to form a compound name.

The suffix *ḍaṇ* is applied after these two [words] when the word *brāhmaṇa* is to be expressed. For example, those whose measure is thirty chapters are called *traiśāni brāhmaṇāni*; likewise, *cātvāriṃśāni*.
[The suffix *yat* is also used] in the sense of "he deserves that" (*tadarhati*).

In this matter, it should be as prescribed. One who deserves an umbrella is called *cchātrikaḥ*. [The suffixes] *-śatya* and *-śatika* [are used for "worth a hundred"]. The rule "he goes to that" (*tadaiti*) applies up to the word *uttarapatha*. After words beginning with *cheda*, the suffix is applied invariably (*nityam*).

In the sense of "one who deserves [punishment] eternally" (*nityam arhati*), the suffixes shall be applied as prescribed. For example: *chaidikaḥ* ("one who deserves the cutting off of the head"), *bhaidikaḥ* ("one who deserves the breaking").
The word "eternally" (*nityam*) is an adverbial modifier of the action.
Furthermore, after the word *śīrṣaccheda*, the suffix *yañ* is also applied.

In the sense of "one who deserves this," the suffix *yat* shall be applied, as well as *ṭhak*. Thus: *śīrṣacchedyaḥ* or *śairṣacchedikaḥ*. By virtue of the co-occurrence with the suffix, there is the substitution of *śīrṣa-* for *śiras-* due to its being a *nipātana*.
[The suffix] *ya-* is applied after words such as *daṇḍa*.

The suffix *yat* occurs after these [words] to form the sense of "one who deserves": *daṇḍya-* (one deserving a staff), *vadhya-* (one deserving death), *kaṇṭhya-* (suitable for the throat), *madhuparkya-* (fit for the honey-mixture), *yugya-* (fit for a yoke), *kaśya-* (deserving a whip), and *dhanya-* (deserving wealth).
It also occurs in the Vedic language (*chandasi*).
The *Chandaḥsūtra*: "And [the suffix] *gham* after *pātra*."

The suffix *ghaṅ* occurs after the word *pātra*, and [the suffix *cha* occurs] after that which it deserves; thus, *pātriyaḥ* and *pātryaḥ*. After the words *kaḍaṅgara* and *dakṣiṇā*, the suffix *cha* also occurs.

After these two [suffixes], there shall be the suffix *cha*, and [the suffix] *yat* as well. A bull worthy of straw is called *kaḍaṅgarīyaḥ* or *kaḍaṅgaryaḥ*. One worthy of a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is called *dakṣiṇīyaḥ* or *dakṣiṇyaḥ*.
[The suffix *cha* is also applied] after *sthālībilāt*.

The suffix *śa* shall be applied after this [word *sthālībila*], as well as *yat*. *Sthālīvilīyāḥ* or *sthālīvilyāḥ* refers to rice grains (*taṇḍula*) that deserve to be placed in a cooking pot; the meaning is "suitable for cooking.
After the words *yajña* and *ṛtvij*, the suffixes *gha* and *khañ* are applied respectively.

The suffixes *gha* and *khañ* shall occur after these [words]. A Brāhmaṇa who is worthy of a sacrifice is called *yajñiya*; a sacrificer who is worthy of officiating as a priest is called *ārtvijīna*.
There is an addition [to the rule]: "after a word meaning 'worthy of that action'. A region worthy of a sacrifice is *yajñiya*; a family of Brahmins worthy of officiating is *ārtvijīna*.
The rules concerning suffixes added to words meaning "worthy of" (*ārhīya*) are complete.
Regarding the secondary suffixes (taddhita), those beginning with *prāgvatīya* are treated as before; from here on, only the suffix *ṭhañ* applies after words ending in *prāgvat*.
[The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied] after the words *pārāyaṇa*, *turāyaṇa*, and *cāndrāyaṇa* when they mean "one who performs" (*vartayati*).
The suffix *ṭhañ* (*ika*) shall be applied in the sense of "one who subsists by means of these. Examples: *pārāyaṇikaḥ*, *dvaipārāyaṇikaḥ*, *taurāyaṇikaḥ*, *cāndrāyaṇikaḥ*.
[When the sense is] "one who has fallen into doubt," the suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied. Example: *sāṃśayikaḥ*.
He goes a yojana.
The suffix *ṭhañ* should be applied. For example: *yaujanikaḥ*.
The forms *krauśaśatika* and *yaujanaśatika* are included by way of supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*).
After the word *pathin*, the suffix *ṣkan* is applied.

A traveler goes on a path (*panthānam gacchati pathikaḥ*). Because it ends in *ṣit*, the feminine suffix *ṅī* is applied: *pathikī*. [In this case,] the suffix *ṇa* is always substituted for *pantha*.

The suffix *ṇa* (forming *pathin*) is applied to the word *path* to denote a way, and the suffix *adeśa* is applied to it to form *panthān* when referring to a traveler; thus, *pānthaḥ* means "a young man who has fallen asleep while traveling. In the feminine, the suffix *ṭāp* is added, yielding *pānthā* for a woman.
Furthermore, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied to the compound *uttarapatha* to mean "brought by way of the northern route."

The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after *uttarapatha*. For example: *auttarapathikaṃ dāru* ("wood brought from the northern route"). Because of the inclusion of the particle *ca*, it is also used in the sense of "going by that [route]": *auttarapathiko dūtaḥ* ("a messenger traveling by the northern route"). Furthermore, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after *pathin* when preceded by *vāri*, *jaṅgala*, *sthala*, *kāntāra*, *aja*, or *śaṅku*. For example: *vāripathikaḥ*, *jaṅgalapathikaḥ*, *sthalapathikaḥ*, *kāntārapathikaḥ*, *ajapathikaḥ*, and *śaṅkupathikaḥ*.

It may be so. By that [suffix], it denotes "carried by" or "going by way of"—namely: *vāripathika* (waterway traveler), *jāṅgalapathika* (traveler on a desert road), *sthālapathika* (traveler on a level road), *kāntārapathika* (traveler on a wilderness road), *ājapathika* (traveler on a goat-track), and *śāṅkupathika* (traveler on a peg-track). The suffix *aṇ* occurs after the words *sthalapatha* and *vāripatha* when they mean *madhuka* or *marica*. That is to say, *sthālapatha* or *vāripatha* may refer to either *madhuka* or *marica*. In this context, there is a governing rule regarding time (*kālādhikāra*).
From time.
The suffixes expressing time are to be stated [as follows]: from *vyuṣṭa* onwards, up to *yāti*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied. [The meaning is: "that by which something is accomplished."

In this sense, the suffix *ṭhañ* (which becomes *-ika*) shall be applied after a word denoting time. For example: *āhnikaṃ* ("produced in a day"). Due to the restrictive rule *ahnaṣṭakhoreva* ("the elision of the final *ṭi* occurs only before the suffixes *ṭa* and *kha*"), there is no elision of the *ṭi*. Examples: *māsikaḥ* ("monthly") and *dvisāṃvatsarikaḥ* ("biennial"). In the latter, the vowel of the second member is lengthened according to the rule *saṃkhyāḥ saṃvatsara-* ("vowel lengthening of the second member after a numeral when followed by *saṃvatsara*"). [The suffix is also applied] in the senses of "appointed for that period," "hired for that period," "having existed for that period," or "about to exist for that period."

From a word denoting time, provided it is in the second case (accusative) construction, the suffix *ṭhañ* shall occur in the sense of "appointed for" (*adhīṣṭa*) and so forth. For example: one appointed for a month, hired, past, or future, is called *māsikaḥ*; likewise, a teacher, a servant, a disease, or a festival lasting for a year is called *sāṃvatsarikaḥ*. After the word *māsa*, when expressing age, the suffixes *yat* and *khañ* are also employed.

When referring to age, these two suffixes [ṭhañ and khañ] should be used after the word *māsa*. One who has lived for or will live for a month is called *māsya* or *māsīna*; as in *māsīnaḥ śiśuḥ* ("a month-old infant"). Why "when referring to age"? [Observe: *māsikaḥ karmakaraḥ* ("a laborer paid monthly"). After a *dvigu* compound, the suffix *yap* is applied.
After the word *dvimāsa*, when referring to age, the suffix *yaP* shall be applied. For example: one who has been two months old, or will be two months old, is called *dvimāsyaḥ*.
Similarly, *trimāsyaḥ*.
After the word *ṣaṇmāsa*, the suffix *ṇyaC* is also applied.
After the word *ṣaṇmāsa*, when it does not denote age, the suffixes *ṇyat* and *yaP* may be applied; thus, *ṣāṇmāsyaḥ* and *ṣaṇmāsyaḥ*. Some say that *ṭhaÑ* is also applied—thus, *ṣāṇmāsikaḥ*.
When it denotes age, the suffix *ṭhaÑ* is also applied.
The suffix *ṭhan* shall be applied after the word *avayasi* (meaning "not yet adult"), and also the suffix *ṇya*. Examples: *ṣāṇmāsiko rogaḥ* ("a six-month-old disease") and *ṣāṇmāsyaḥ*.
Some authorities maintain that the suffix *ṭhañ* is also applicable—hence *ṣāṇmāsikaḥ*.
After the word *samā* (year), the suffix *kha* is applied.
The suffix *kha* occurs after the word *sama* in the five senses beginning with "produced from" (*nirvṛtta*). Thus, *samīnaḥ*.
After a *dvigu* compound, it is optional.

After a *dvigu* compound ending in *samā*, the suffix *kha* (i.e., *ika*) may optionally be applied in the sense of "produced from" (*nirvṛtta*) and so forth; for example, *dvisamīnaḥ* or *dvaisamikaḥ*. [The suffix *kha* is also applied] after compounds ending in *rātri*, *ahar*, and *saṃvatsara*.

After a *dvigu* compound ending in *rātri*, the suffix *kha* (i.e., *īna*) may optionally occur in the sense of "completed" (*nirvṛtta*) and so forth; alternatively, the suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *ika*) applies. Thus: *dvirātrīṇaḥ* or *dvairātrikaḥ*; *dvyahīnaḥ* or *dvaiyahnikaḥ*; *dvisaṃvatsarīṇaḥ* or *dvisāṃvatsarikaḥ*.

In the case of *dvyahīnaḥ*, because the rule for adding a compound-final suffix (*samāsānta*) is not universally obligatory (*anitya*), the suffix *ṭac* is not applied; consequently, there is no substitution of *ahn* [for *aha*]. This is because that substitution is prescribed specifically when *ṭac* follows. Furthermore, after *varṣa*, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix.

After a word ending in *varṣa* (year) that denotes the completion of a period, the suffixes *kha* (*īna*) and *thañ* (*ika*) may optionally be applied to form words meaning "having occurred" (*nirvṛtta*), etc.; furthermore, the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *varṣa* itself is optional. Examples: *dvivarṣīṇo vyādhiḥ* ("a disease lasting two years") or *dvivārṣikaḥ*; in the alternative case of elision: *dvivarṣaḥ*. When the suffix *kha* is applied, there is vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of the second member according to the rule *varṣasyābhaviṣyati*. However, when the suffix *thañ* is applied, it is *dvaivarṣikaḥ*.
[The suffix *thañ*] is obligatory after a word denoting a completed period when it refers to something possessing consciousness (*cittavat*).

In the case of words denoting living beings, following a *dvigu* compound ending in *varṣa*, there shall always be elision (*luk*) of the suffix when the sense of "completed" (*nirvṛtta*) and so forth is intended. For example: *dvivarṣo bālakaḥ* (a two-year-old boy); *dvivarṣo vatsaḥ* (a calf two years old). Also: *ṣaṣṭikāḥ* (rice that ripens in sixty nights).
The suffix *kan* is applied after the word *ṣaṣṭi-rātra*, and the elision of the final member [of the compound] is prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*). Thus, *ṣaṣṭikāḥ*.
The plurality is not restrictive; therefore, they say "a *ṣaṣṭika* rice plant" (*ṣaṣṭiko vrīhiḥ*).
After words ending in *vatsara*, the suffix *cha* is applied in the Veda (*chandas*).
After the prefix *sam-pari*, [the suffix] *kha* also [is applied].
The two meters of the *Chandaḥsūtra*;
by means of that, what is to be mastered becomes easy to accomplish.

In these senses, the suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after a word denoting time. For example: that which can be mastered, obtained, performed, or easily accomplished within a month is *māsika*; likewise, *sāṃvatsarika*. This [suffix] also denotes the period of one's *brahmacarya* (celibate student life).

The suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *-ika*) shall be applied in this sense [of "lasting for"] after a word denoting time. For example: *māsaṃ brahmacaryam asya māsiko vipraḥ* ("A Brahmin who has observed celibacy for a month"). Here, the accusative case in *māsam* is used to express continuous connection (*atyantasaṃyoga*), while *tad* is in the nominative. According to some, the phrase means "that month belongs to his celibacy," thus forming *māsikaṃ brahmacaryam*. The suffix *ṭhañ* shall also be applied after words such as *mahānāmnī* and others in the sense "one who performs that. *Mahānāmnī* refers to certain Vedic verses (*ṛc*); the vow associated with them is also called *mahānāmnī*. One who performs those is a *māhānāmikaḥ*. Similarly, one who performs the *ādityavrata* is an *ādityavratikaḥ*. According to the *Padamañjarī*, the form *māhānāmikaḥ* arises through the substitution of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) by the rule *bhasyāḍhe taddhite*.

The suffix *ḍini* is applied after words such as *avāntaradīkṣā* in the sense of "one who performs that. Thus, *avāntaradīkṣī* (one who undergoes the intermediate initiation) and *devavratī* (one who observes the vow of the gods). The suffix *ḍvuṇ* and *ḍini* are applied after the word *aṣṭacatvāriṃśat*. One who performs the vow for forty-eight years is called *aṣṭacatvāriṃśakaḥ* or *aṣṭacatvāriṃśī* (a Brahmin). After the word *cāturmāsya*, there is also the elision of the *y* sound. One who performs the *cāturmāsya* vows is called *cāturmāsakaḥ* or *cāturmāsī*.
Another [suffix] occurs after *caturmāsa* in the sense of a sacrifice (*yajña*). A sacrifice occurring in four months is *cāturmāsya*.
By the rule *saṃjñāyām-aṇ*, it is called *cāturmāsī*, which is the name for a full-moon day (*paurṇamāsī*). And its sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is derived from words denoting sacrifices.

The suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *-ika*) shall be used in the sense of "the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) for that [sacrifice]"; for example, the sacrificial fee for the *agniṣṭoma* is *āgniṣṭomikī*, and [the fee for the *rājasūya* is] *rājasūyikī*. Furthermore, whatever is given or performed therein follows the same rules as [the primary sacrifice].

In this context, after a word ending in the locative case, when the meanings "is given" (*dīyate*) or "is to be done" (*kāryam*) are intended, suffixes shall occur just as they do in the sense of "belonging to that" (*tatra-bhava*). For example: *māse dīyate kāryaṃ vā* ("given or to be done in a month") results in *māsikam*; *prāvṛṣeṇyam*; *haimanam*.
The section on time (*kāla*) has been explained.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after words such as *vyuṣṭa*.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these [words]. That which is given or performed when it has dawned is called *vaiyuṣṭam*. That which is constant is *nāityam*. By means of those [words], namely *yathākathāc* and *hasta*, the suffixes *ṇa* and *ya* are applied respectively.

The suffixes *ṇya* and *ta* occur after these two [words]. [The forms are: *yāthākathācam*, *hastyam*. The indeclinable compound *yathākathāca* signifies disregard. [The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs] in the sense of "one who accomplishes."

In these cases, the suffix *ṭhañ* (i.e., *-ika*) shall be applied. That which is prepared with or beautified by sandalwood is *cāndanika*. "The body of one whose face is *kārṇaveṣṭakika* (made of black bricks) and whose body is *vāstrayugika* (clothed in a pair of garments). From *karman* and *veśa*, the suffix *yat* is applied.

That which may result from these two is accomplished for the sake of the object; [it serves] for the purpose of action. A body that is "veśya" (suitable for a brothel) is a "veśyāstrī" (a courtesan); a body that is "veśya" is a "vapuh" (form).
It is capable of withstanding [afflictions] such as heat and so forth.

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ñ* shall be applied after [words ending in] *santāpa* and so forth. For example: *sāntāpikam* (that which serves for the sake of torment), *sāṃgrāmikam* (pertaining to battle), *sāktumāṃsaudanikaḥ* (one who deals in groats, meat, and rice), *sāktukaḥ* (a dealer in groats), *māṃsikaḥ* (a dealer in meat), and *audanikaḥ* (a dealer in rice).
After the word *yoga*, the suffix *yat* is also applied.
That which is suitable for yoga is *yogya*; with the suffix *ṭhañ* (ika), it is *yaugika*. With the suffix *ukañ* after the word *karman*, [it is *karmaka*].
That which is capable of action is "kārmuka," meaning a bow;
its proper time has now arrived.

The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied in this sense after the word *samaya*. For example: *sāmayikaṃ kāryam* (a task for which the time has arrived). What is accomplished by one who performs what is *asāmayika* (untimely)?
That [suffix] follows this [word *samaya*] prior to the suffix *vat*.
The end of the season.
Therefore, the suffix *aṇ* should be applied. "The season has arrived for her" (*ṛtuḥ prāpto'syāḥ*); thus, *ārtavám* refers to the flower, and *ārtavám* refers to the fruit.
In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), the suffix *ghas* is also used.
Chandaḥsūtram: [The suffix] *yat* is applied after a word denoting time.
The time has arrived; today’s garment is *kālya*. A cow is fit for breeding at the proper time (*kālya*). The cold is at its peak (*kālyam*).
The suffix *ṭhañ* is used in the sense of "excellent" or "preeminent."
An extended period of time belongs to this; thus it is *kālika* (long-term) enmity.
The suffix *ṭhañ* is used here for the sake of clarity. An example is *kālikam ṛṇam* (a long-term debt). It refers to the purpose.
The suffix *ṭhañ* (ika) shall be applied in the sense of "this is its purpose. Examples: *aindramahikam* ("intended for the festival of Indra"), *autsavikam* ("intended for a festival").
[Furthermore,] the suffix *aṇ* is applied after *viśākhā* and *āṣāḍhā* when referring respectively to a churning-stick (*mantha*) and a staff (*daṇḍa*).

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these two [words]. *Vaiśākha* is a churning-stick (*mantha*). "With mountains cast down by hands moving with great speed in the *vaiśākha* position. *Āṣāḍha* is a staff (*daṇḍa*). "Then the ascetic wearing the deerskin and the *āṣāḍha* staff.
Also [after words] beginning with *cūḍā*. That for which the crest (*cūḍā*) is the purpose is *cauḍa*. That for which faith (*śraddhā*) is the purpose is *śrāddha*. *Khāṭva*.
After [words] beginning with *anupravacana*, the suffix *cha* is applied.
The suffix *cha* shall be applied after these [words] in the sense of "this is its purpose" (*tad-asya prayojanam*). Examples: *anupravacanīyam*, *anuprayojanīyam*, *utthāpanīyam*.

[The suffix *cha* is applied] after a verbal root ending in *viś*, *pad*, *pūri*, or *ruhi*, provided it does not end in the letter *ā* and is preceded by another word as its prior member (*sapūrvapada*). Examples: *gehānupraveśanīyam*, *prapāpūraṇīyam*, *aśvārohaṇīyam*, *aśvaprapadanīyam*, *prāsādārohaṇīyam*.

The suffix *yat* is applied after [words such as] *svarga* and others. For example: that which has heaven (*svarga*) as its purpose is *svargya*; likewise, *āyuṣya* (conducive to long life), *yaśasya* (conducive to fame), and *dhanya* (conducive to prosperity). It should be stated that the suffix is elided (*luk*) after [compounds] such as *puṇyāhavācana*. For instance: the rite of the declaration of an auspicious day is *puṇyāhavācana*; the rite of the declaration of well-being is *svastivācana*.
[The suffix *yat* is also applied] after the word *samāpana*, provided it is preceded by another word [forming a compound].

The suffix *cha* (forming *-īya*) occurs after a compound whose prior member is present [in the sense of completion], in the meaning "this is its purpose," specifically after words meaning "completion of a vow" (*vrata-samāpana*). Examples: *vratasamāpanīyaṃ bhojanam* ("food for the completion of a vow"), *kalahasamāpanīyaṃ dānam* ("a gift for the completion of a quarrel"), *chandaḥsamāpanīyam* ("for the completion of a Vedic meter").
Furthermore, the suffix *aikāgārikaṭ* is used after the word *caura* ("thief") in this same sense: *cauraikāgārikaḥ* ("one who has a thief as his sole companion").
And this [suffix] is applied after *caura* (thief): *aikāgārikaś cauraḥ* (a thief who breaks into a single house). Like a thief, they went out of sight from afar upon the ground.
*Aikāgārikī*: the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied because of the presence of the marker *ṭi*.
[The suffix *ṭhañ*] is applied after *ākālika* in the sense of expressing that which begins and ends at the same time (*ādyantavacana*).

This [suffix] is prescribed when expressing two short durations at the beginning and end. *Ākālikaḥ* means "a cloud that lasts only a moment. Because it has the marker *ṭi*, the feminine form is *ākālikī*. Having observed the commencement of spring, which is *ākālikī* (momentary). [The suffixes] *ṭhañ* and *ñ* have been stated [to apply] before *vati*.
When the action is equal to that [standard], the suffix *vati* is used.

The suffix *vati* occurs after a word in the third case (*tṛtīyā*) when there is equality of action (*kriyā-taulya*). For example: *vipreṇa tulyaṃ vipravad adhīte* ("He studies like a Brahmin"). Since equality with an action is possible only through an action itself, in the expression *vipravad adhīte*, the suffix *vati* is added to the word *vipra*, which denotes the action of studying performed by a Brahmin as its agent. The meaning is: "He studies in such a way that it is equal to [the study] by a Brahmin, that is, equal to the act of studying performed by a Brahmin. Similarly: *putraṃ mitravad ācaret* ("One should behave toward a son as toward a friend"). This means: "One should behave toward a son in such a way that it is equal to the act of behaving toward a friend."

Likewise, as before, the *ātmanepada* occurs after a desiderative (*san*) suffix; that is, just as it occurred due to the action of entering into the *ātmanepada* by virtue of the preceding rule as its cause, so too does the *ātmanepada* occur after a form ending in *san*. Thus, one should behave toward the teacher’s sons as one would toward the teacher himself; for the behavior directed toward his sons is equivalent to the behavior directed toward him in the previous case.

What is the purpose of including the word *kriyā* (action)? It is so that [the suffix] does not apply when there is similarity in quality (*guṇatulya*), as in: "He is as stout as his son" (*putreṇa tulyaḥ sthūlaḥ*).
In that case, [the rule] applies as "like that" (*tasyeva*).

The suffix *vati* occurs after a word ending in the seventh or sixth case, provided that it is semantically equivalent to the sense of "like" (*iva*). Examples: the walls of Mathurā are like garlands; the teeth of a Kṣatriya are as white as those of a Brāhmaṇa. [The suffix *vat*] also expresses "deserving that" (*tadarham*).

In this sense, the suffix *vati* is employed. That which one deserves is called *arham*; [this is formed] with the suffix *ac* from the class beginning with *pac*. "Conduct befitting a king" (*rājavat vṛttam*) means conduct that deserves a king; "character like that of a sage" (*munivaccaritram*).
It is not used here in the case of "curd deserves a Brahmin" (*vipramarhati dadhi*), because such an expression is not sanctioned by usage.
[The suffix *vati* is also applied] after a preverb (*upasarga*) in the Vedic language (*chandas*) when it conveys the meaning of the verbal root itself.
The *Chandaḥsūtra*.
The suffixes *tva* and *tal* express the state (*bhāva*) of that [noun].

The intention is that from this [conceptualization] arise the designation (*abhidhāna*) and the cognition (*pratyaya*); thus, *bhāva* is a property of the object (*vastudharma*), such as a genus (*jāti*) and so forth, which serves as the ground for the application of a word (*śabdapravṛttinimitta*). In the sense of "the state of being that" (*tasya bhāvaḥ*), the suffixes *tva* and *tal* are employed. For example: *gotvam*, *gotā*; *śuklatvam*, *śuklatā*; *rūpatvam*, *rūpatā*; *kriyātvam*, *kriyātā*; *rasatvam*, *rasatā*.

In compounds (*samāsa*), primary derivatives (*kṛt*), and secondary derivatives (*taddhita*), the relation (*sambandha*) is the ground for the application [of the word]: *rājapuruṣatvam* (the state of being a king’s man), *pācakatvam* (the state of being a cook), *gārgyatvam* (the state of being a descendant of Garga), *yauṣmākīṇatvam* (the state of belonging to you).
In the case of arbitrary words (*yadṛcchāśabda*), there is a designation of the mere form itself: *ḍitthatvam*, *ḍavitthatvam*, *kutvam*, *cutvam*.
And because it is so stated in the scripture.

The suffixes *tva* and *tal* occur after a word ending in *brahman* along with its negative prefixes (*apavāda*). By the force of the word "and" (*ca*), they also occur after words ending in *nañ*, *srañ*, and *ña*. Examples: *prathimā*, *pṛthutvam*, *pṛthutā*; likewise, *pāṭavam*, *paṭutvam*, *paṭutā*; *straiṇam*, *strītvam*, *strītā*; *pausnam*, *puṃstvam*, *puṃstā*. [The suffix *tva* occurs] after a *tatpuruṣa* compound beginning with *nañ*, except for those ending in *catura*, *saṅgata*, *lavaṇa*, *vaṭa*, *budha*, *katara*, *salasa*, and *sabhā*.

The suffix denoting an abstract state (*bhāvapratyaya*) to be mentioned hereafter would not occur after a *nañ*-tatpuruṣa compound. For example, the suffix *yak* occurs after words ending in *-pati* and after *purohita*, etc., as in *bārhaspatyam*. It does not occur after compounds preceded by *nañ*, such as *apatitvam* (the state of not being fallen) or *apatitā* (the state of not having fallen).

Why [is it said] "not after *catura*, etc."? [Because they do occur there: *ācaturyam* (inability to count), *āsaṅgatyam* (lack of attachment), *ālavaṇyam* (absence of saltiness), *āvaṭyam* (absence of a pit), *ābudhyam* (lack of understanding), *ākatpam* (absence of skill), *ārasyam* (absence of joy), and *ālasyam* (laziness).
The suffix *iman* is optionally applied after the group of words beginning with *pṛthu*.

The suffix *imanij* may optionally be applied after these [words]. The mention of the word "optionally" (*vā*) is for the purpose of allowing its co-occurrence with the suffix *aṇ*. Thus, the state of being broad (*pṛthu*) is *prathimā*, *pārthava*, *pṛthutva*, or *pṛthutā*. Likewise, it is *tanimā*, *tānava*, *tanutā*, or *tanutva*.
The group beginning with *pṛthu*, *mṛdu*, *paṭu*, *mahat*, *guru*, *laghu*, *priya*, *kṣipra*, *hrasva*, *dīrgha*, *bahula*, and so forth, is known as the *pṛthvādi* group.
The suffix *ṣyañ* is also applied after words beginning with *varṇa* and *dṛḍha*.

The suffixes *ṣyañ* and *imanij* shall occur after these [words]. After a color word (*varṇa*): *śauklyaṃ*, *śuklimā*; *kārṣṇyaṃ*, *kṛṣṇimā*. After words beginning with *dṛḍha*: *dāḍharyaṃ*, *draḍhimā*; *mādhuryaṃ*, *madhurimā*; *vaimanasyaṃ*, *vimanimā*. The letter *ṣ* is for the purpose of [triggering] the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*: *aucitī*, *ānupūrvī*, *vaidagdhī*. The suffixes *tva* and *tal* are to be illustrated in all cases. Since *ṣyañ* is already established after words expressing qualities (*guṇavacana*), the mention of "color" (*varṇa*) is for the sake of *imanij*. Furthermore, the inclusion of words such as *vadhi-ra*, *kṛśa*, *śīta*, *uṣṇa*, and *madhura* in the list beginning with *dṛḍha* is for the sake of optionally applying *imanij*. Moreover, let there not be *ṣyañ* in the sense of an action (*karman*).
