The suffix *aṇ* is applied after words expressing qualities (*guṇavacana*) and after the class beginning with *brāhmaṇa*, in the sense of the object (*karman*).

The suffixes *ṣyañ* and *añ* shall be applied after these [words] when expressing the state (*bhāva*) or an action (*kriyā*). After words denoting qualities (*guṇavacana*):—the state or action of one who is dull-witted is *jāḍyam*, *mauḍhyam*, *kārśyam*, or *sthaulyam*.
From the class beginning with *brāhmaṇa* (an *ākṛtigaṇa*):—*brāhmaṇyam*, *dautyam*.

When a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) is mentioned [in a rule], that which is qualified by gender is also included—thus, *dautyam* (the business of female messengers) from *dūtī*; *abhidautyam* (the state of being a messenger) from *abhidūtī*. The following belong to this class: *brāhmaṇa*, *dūta*, *caura*, *madhyastha*, *kuśala*, *capala*, *nipuṇa*, *piśuna*, *dāyāda*, *kavi*, and *akṣetrajña*. This is an open-ended class (*ākṛtigaṇa*). Furthermore, after the word *capala*, the suffix *num* is added along with *yañ* when derived from a lake (*saras*), as in *cāpalyam* (the tossing of a lake) by the hands of its waves. After the word *arhat*, the suffix *yañ* is applied and the augment *num* is inserted: *ārhantyam* (the state of being an Arhat), *ārhantī* (a female Arhat).

The suffix *ṣyañ* is added to words such as *cāturvarṇya* in their own sense (to form abstract nouns). Examples: *cāturvarṇyam*, *ānyabhāvyam*. Regarding this, Vararuci says: "But *ānyabhāvya* [is formed] because it is a word denoting time. Examples: *aupamyam*, *yaugapadyam*, *sānnidhyam*, *cāturvaidyam*, *ṣāḍguṇyam*, *tādarthyam*, *trailokyam*, *sāhityam*. From here onwards, the rule for the suffix *itya* applies to both the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*).
After the root *sten*, there is the elision of *na* as well.
The suffix *yat* shall be applied after the word *stena*, and there is also the elision of the letter *n*. Thus, *stena* means a thief; its state or action is *steyam* (theft).
As for the word *stainya*, the *Bhāgavṛtti* states that it is based on traditional authority (*āgamika*), like the words *pāñcālaka* and *lauhityaka*.
Jayāditya, however, maintains that the suffix *ṣyañ* is applied due to the division of the rule (*yogavibhāga*).
That which belongs to a friend.

It may be so. According to Jayāditya, the suffix *yañ* is applied after the words *dūta* and *vaṇij*, as in *dautyam* and *vaṇijyā*. Alternatively, because they are read in the *brāhmaṇa*-group [of the *gaṇapāṭha*], the forms are *vāṇijyam* and *dautyam*. After the words *kapi* and *jñāti*, the suffix *ḍhak* is applied.

The suffix *ḍhak* shall be applied after these two [stems]. For example: *kāpeyaḥ* and *jñāteyaḥ*, in the sense of "state" (*bhāva*) or "action" (*karman*). After stems ending in *pati* and after *purohita* and so forth, the suffix *yak* is applied.
The suffix *yaK* shall be applied after these: after words ending in *pati*—*saināpatyam*, *prājāpatyam*, *gārhapatyam*; after *purohita* and others—*paurohityam*, *rājyam*, *sainyam*.
After words denoting a genus of living beings, age, or *udgātṛ* and others, the suffix *añ* is applied.

The suffix *añ* shall occur after these [words]. After a word denoting a class of living beings: *auṣṭram*. After a word expressing age: *kaumāram*. After words beginning with *udgātra*: *audgātram*, *aunnetram*. After words ending in *hāyana* and after *yuvan* and so forth, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these: after a word ending in *hāyana*—*dvaihāyanam*; after *yuvan*, meaning "the state or action of a youth"—*yauvanam*; *sthāviram*; *pauruṣam*; *suhṛd*; *durhṛd*; *capala*; *nipuṇa*; *kuśala*; *akṣetrajña*; *piśuna*; *kutūhala*. After *śrotriya*, there is also the elision of the *gh* [suffix], resulting in *śrautram*.
And [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after a stem ending in *i* or *u*, provided that the preceding syllable is light.

The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word ending in *ḥ* (visarga) where the preceding vowel is light (*laghu*). Examples: *maunaṃ*, *gauravaṃ*, *śaucaṃ*, *pāṭavaṃ*, *lāghavaṃ*, *hārītakaṃ*. Why "after one preceded by a light vowel"? Consider *pāṇḍutvaṃ*;
however, *kāvyam* is formed because it belongs to the *brāhmaṇa*-class (Pāṇini 5.1.124).
The suffix *vuñ* is applied after a word that has *ya* as its penultimate letter and a heavy syllable (*guru*) preceding the penultimate.

Among three or more [syllables], the last is called *uttama* (final), and that which is near it is *upottama* (penultimate). The suffix *vuñ* occurs after a word whose penultimate syllable is heavy (*guru*) and which has *ya* as its penultimate vowel (*yopadha*). Examples: *rāmaṇīyakam*, *ācāryakam*, *sāhāyakam*.

Regarding *sāhāyyam*, Jayāditya states that it is also derived from the *brāhmaṇādi* group [of words taking *ṣyañ*]. The *Bhāgavṛtti*, however, says it is not so. Why "whose penultimate syllable is heavy"? Consider *kṣatriyatvam*.
And [the suffix *ka* is added] after copulative compounds (*dvandva*) and after words such as *manojña*.
The suffix *vuñ* shall be applied after these: after a *dvandva* compound—*śaiṣyopādhyāyikā*, *paitāputrikā*, *kautsakuśikikā*;
after the group beginning with *manojña*—*mānojñakam*, *praiyarūpakam*, *ābhirūpakam*;
and after *amuṣyaputra*, *amuṣyakula*, *āḍhya*, and *chātra*.
From the practice of one's lineage, there arises praise, censure, and the perception of those [qualities].

From these two [categories], namely *gotra* (lineage) and *caraṇa* (Vedic school), the suffix *vuñ* shall be applied in the sense of praise (*ślāghā*), abuse (*adhikṣepa*), and in relation to the attainment of those qualities, whether in the abstract state (*bhāva*) or as an object (*karman*). From *gotra*: - He praises by means of the Gārgya lineage: *gārgikayā ślāghate*. - He abuses by means of the Gārgya lineage: *gārgikayātyākurute*. - He has attained the status of a Dākṣi: *dākṣikāmavetaḥ*. From *caraṇa*: - He praises by means of the Kaṭha school: *kāṭhikayā ślāghate*. - He abuses by means of the Kaṭha school: *kāṭhikayātyākurute*. - He has attained the status of a Bāhvṛcika: *bāhavṛcikāmavetaḥ*. In cases other than praise and so forth, it remains simply *gārgyatvam* (the state of being a Gārgya). [The suffix] *da* is applied after words denoting *hotṛ* priests.

This word *hotrā* is a designation for the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*). The use of the plural number is intended to exclude the rule regarding the specific form [of the singular]. The suffix *cha* shall be applied after words denoting *hotrā*. For example: *acchāvākīya*, *mitrāvaruṇīya*, and *brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya*.
However, after the word *brahman*, the suffix *tva* is applied.
From the word *brahman*, which denotes the office of the *hotṛ*, there should be the suffix *tva* with the substitution of *ān*. Thus: *brahmatvam*.
[End of] the second quarter of the fifth chapter. *Oṃ*.
In the section on secondary derivatives (taddhita), the fifth chapter:
the suffix *khañ* is applied after words denoting grains when referring to the field where they grow.

The suffix *khañ* (īna) is applied here after words denoting types of grain. That in which something exists is called a *bhavana*. A field for growing mung beans is *maudgīna*; likewise, *dhānyīna*, *kaulatthīna*, and *kaudravīṇa*.
After the words *vrīhi* and *śāli*, the suffix *ḍhak* (eya) is applied.
The suffix *ḍhak* shall be applied after these two [words]. Examples: *vraiheyam*, *śāleyam*. After *yava*, *yavaka*, and *ṣaṣṭika*, the suffix *yat* is applied.
The suffix *yat* occurs after these [words] to form the names of fields: *yavyaṃ kṣetram* ("a field of barley"), *yavakyaṃ*, *ṣaṣṭikyaṃ*.
Optionally, the suffix *yat* occurs after *tila*, *māṣa*, *umā*, *bhaṅgā*, and *aṇu*.

From these [words], there may be [the suffixes] -ya or -īna: *tilyaṃ* or *tailīnaṃ* "a field of sesame"; *māṣyam* or *māṣīṇaṃ* "a field of beans"; *umyam* or *aumīnaṃ* "a field of hemp"; *bhaṅgyam* or *bhāṅgīnaṃ* "made of flax"; *aṇavyam* or *āṇavīnaṃ* "made of wool.
The suffixes -kha and -khañ are used after the word *sarvacarman* when it means "made entirely of leather."
From this [base], when the sense is "made," the suffixes *kha* and *khañ* shall occur. For example: *sarvacarmīṇo rathaḥ* (a chariot made entirely of leather) or *sārvacarmīṇaḥ*.
The suffix *kha* occurs after *yathāmukha* and *samukha* in the sense of "showing."

The suffix *kha* (īna) is applied after these two words when meaning "visible to" (*darśana*). *Yathāmukham*: the likeness of the face; this is a compound by virtue of being a fixed form (*nipātana*). *Sammukham*: an even face. *Darśanaḥ*: that in which something is seen. *Yathāmukhīnaḥ*: a mirror visible to the face. *Yathāmukhīnaḥ*: the deer made of gold and jewels [seen] by Sītā. *Sammukhīnaḥ*: visible to the face.
[The suffix *kha* is also applied] after compounds beginning with *sarva*, when they pervade a path, a limb, an action, a leaf, or a vessel.

The suffix *kha* (which becomes *īna*) occurs after words such as *sarvādika*, *pathyaṅga*, and others, in the sense of "pervading that. For example: *sarvapathīno rathaḥ* ("a chariot that pervades all paths"), *sarvāṅgīṇaṃ vāsaḥ* ("a garment that covers all limbs"), *sarvakarmīṇaḥ pāṇiḥ* ("a hand capable of all actions"), *sarvapattrīṇaḥ sārathiḥ* ("a charioteer who reaches every part of the vehicle"), and *sarvapātrīṇa odanaḥ* ("rice that fills every vessel").
[Also, the suffix applies] in the sense of reaching as far as the tips of the feet (*āprapadam*).
In this sense, the suffix *kha* (īna) may be used. For example: *āprapadīnaḥ paṭaḥ* ("a garment reaching to the toes").
The suffixes *anupada*, *sarvānna*, *āyānaya*, *baddha*, *abhakṣayati*, and *ineya* are also applied in these senses.

The suffix *kha* (īna) occurs after *anupada*, *sarvānna*, *ayas*, *apradakṣiṇa*, *anaya*, *ayānaya*, *parovara*, *parampara*, and *putrapautra*. An *anupadīnā* sandal is one that is bound immediately [to the foot]; the meaning is "measuring the foot. A mendicant who eats all kinds of food is called *sarvānnīna*. *Ayas* means clockwise; *anayas* means counter-clockwise. A shuttle (*śāra*) that is led in both directions is called *ayānayīna*. One who experiences the sequence of father, grandfather, son, and grandson is said to experience *parovara*, *parampara*, *putrapautra*, and so on.

The suffix *kha* (īna) is applied after these words when they mean "to experience. From *para* and *avara*, one experiences both higher and lower [states]; by means of a grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*), *para* becomes *parot*, resulting in *parovarīṇaḥ*. You should lead Lakṣmī—who is handed down in succession—to a state extending to sons and grandsons (*putrapautrīṇatā*). By means of a grammatical irregularity, the form *parāṃśca parāṃśca* results in the form *paramparā*.
One who goes to the further shore, the near shore, the end, or as far as desired is called *avārapārātyantānukāmagāmī*.

The suffix *kha* (īna) occurs after these [words] in the sense of "one who goes to" (*gāmī*). *Avāraṃ gāmī* becomes *avārīṇaḥ*. *pārīṇaḥ*. Also from a collective compound: *avārapārīṇaḥ*. And from the reverse order: *pārāvārīṇaḥ*. *atyantīnaḥ*. Abandon the state of being *anukāmīna*.
The mention of *gāmī* (one who will go) is for the sake of variety; the suffix applies to any mere goer. *samāṃ samāṃ vijāyate* ("she gives birth every year").

In this sense, the suffix *kha* (īna) shall be applied. *Samāṃsamīnā gauḥ* ("a cow that calves every year")—the meaning is "one that gives birth every year. It should be stated that there is no elision (*aluk*) of the case-ending (*sup*) of the first member of the compound. [The suffix *kha* is also applied] in the sense of "conceived" in the word *adyaśvīnā*.

This [suffix *kha*] is applied when [the time of delivery] is imminent (*avaṣṭabdha*), that is, close at hand (*āsanna*) for giving birth. A cow that will give birth today or tomorrow is called *adyaśvīnā*; the meaning is "one whose parturition is near. Jayāditya asks: "How can there be a separation [of the suffix] as in *adyaśvīna*? He answers: "Because the word *vijāyate* ('gives birth') does not recur [in the subsequent rule]. Bhāgavṛtti says: "This is not so, because of the feminine gender indication and because the comparison itself is impossible [in this context]."
One who receives [a cow] until the milch-cow returns home.
The suffix *kha* is elided. One who performs work until the cow is returned is called *āgavīnaḥ*.
One who goes as far as the cows is called *anugvalaṅgāmī*.

The suffix *kha* may be used [after *anu*]. *Anugu*, meaning "behind the cow," refers to a cowherd who follows the cows (*anugavīna*). After the word *adhvan*, the suffixes *yat* and *kha* are applied.

From this [word *adhvan*], the suffixes *yat* and *kha* may occur. [Examples: *adhvānam alaṅgāmī* (one who goes the full length of the road) is *adhvanyaḥ* or *adhvanīnaḥ*. [The suffix] *cha* also occurs after *abhyamitra*.

The suffix *śa* shall be applied after this [word], as well as *yat* and *kha*. *Abhyamitrīyaḥ*, *abhyamitryaḥ*, and *abhyamitrīṇaḥ* mean "one who goes well toward the enemy"; that is, one who goes directly toward the enemy. After the word *goṣṭha*, the suffix *khañ* is applied when expressing what formerly was.
It may be so. A place where a cow-pen formerly existed is called *gauṣṭhīna*;
likewise, a place traversed by a horse in a single day is [called *aikāhagama*].
The suffix *khañ* is applied after the word *aśva* when meaning "to be traversed in one day. Thus, *āśvīna* means "a path [traversable in one day].
The words *śālīna* and *kaupīna* signify "timid" and "that which should not be done," respectively.

These two [suffixes] are prescribed as substitutes. A bride who deserves entry into the house (*śālā*) is called *śālīnā*; the meaning is that she is modest (*adhṛṣṭā*). Because of her modesty, she was unable to speak. That which deserves entry into a well (*kūpa*) is called *kaupīna*, meaning a shameful act.
He lives by means of a troop (*vrāta*).

Those who live by means of their own bodies are *vrāta*s, such as hunters and the like; the occupation of such people is also called a *vrāta*. Therefore, the suffix *khañ* (*īna*) occurs in the sense of "living by. For example: *vrātīno vipraḥ* ("a Brahmin living by a *vrāta*"). Vyāḍi says: "The *vrātīna* gangs were quickly brought to distress by the lords of men, those Rākṣasas. *Sāptapadīna* means friendship.

This [suffix -īna] is applied after *sakhi* (friend). Because it functions metaphorically (*upacāra*) by referring to that which possesses the quality [of friendship], one also speaks of a "seven-step friend" (*sāptapadīna*).
[The suffix -īna is also applied] after *haiyaṅgava* when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*).

This [suffix] is prescribed as an irregular form (nipātana) for the naming of a specific kind of clarified butter (*ghṛta*). Regarding its cooking (*pāka*) and root (*mūla*), the suffixes *kṛṇap* and *jāhac* are applied after words beginning with *pīlu* and *karṇa* respectively.

The suffix *kuṇap* occurs after the group beginning with *pīlu* in the sense of "ripening. For example: the ripening of *pīlu* fruits is *pīlukuṇaḥ*; *karkandhukuṇaḥ*; *śamīkuṇaḥ*. [Also included are: *karīra*, *kuvala*, *badara*, *aśvattha*, *khadira*. The suffix *jāhac* occurs after the group beginning with *karṇa* in the sense of "root" (*mūla*). For example: the root of the ear is *karṇajāham*; [one] whose eyes have roots at the ears is *karṇajāhavilocanā*. [Other examples are: *akṣijāham*, *nakha*, *mukha*, *keśa*, *pāda*, *bhrū*, *gulpha*, *oṣṭha*, *śṛṅga*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open-ended class).
The suffix *tiḥ* occurs after the word *pakṣa*.

The suffix *ti* occurs after the word *pakṣa* to form *pakṣati*, meaning "the first day of the lunar fortnight" (*pratipad*). It is like the crescent of the moon at the beginning of the fortnight (*pakṣati*). [Examples include: "by birds with fluttering wings" (*cañcat-pakṣatibhiḥ khagaiḥ*).
By that [rule], the suffixes *cup* and *caṇap* are also [formed].

The suffixes *cuñcup* and *caṇap* are used after a word meaning "wealth" (*vitta*) in the sense of "possessing that wealth. One who is known for his learning (*vidyayā vittaḥ pratītaḥ*) is called *vidyācuñcuḥ* or *vidyācaṇaḥ*. Rāma, too, was *māyācaṇaḥ* (skilled in illusion) and *astracuñcuḥ* (proficient in missiles).
After the prefixes *vi-* and *nañ*, the suffixes *nānā* and *ña* are used respectively, provided they do not coexist with the negative particle *na*.
After the prefixes *vi-* and *na*, the suffixes *añ* and *ñāñ* respectively form *vinā* and *nānā*. This rule applies in their own sense (*svārtha*).
After *vi-*, the suffixes *śālac* and *chaṭac* are added.

The suffix *kaṭac* is applied after the words *vi*, *śāla*, *śaṇḍa*, and *kaṭa*, as well as after *sam* and *pra-ud*. [Examples: *vikaṭaḥ*, *viśālaḥ*, *viśaṇḍakaṭaḥ*; *vi* has the sense of "spread out" (*vitata-artha*). *Sam* and *pra-ud* [also take this suffix].

The suffix *kaṭac* shall be applied after these: *saṃkaṭaḥ*, *prakaṭaḥ*, *utkaṭaḥ*. Because of the word *ca* (and), [the forms] *vikaṭaḥ* and *nikaṭaḥ* [are also included]. After *alābū*, *tila*, *māṣa*, *umā*, *bhaṅgā*, and *aṇu*, when meaning "dust," the suffix *kaṭac* shall be applied: *alābūnāṃ rajo 'lābūkaṭaḥ*, *tilakaṭaḥ*, *umākaṭaḥ*, *aṇukaṭaḥ*. The words *goṣṭha* and others are used in the sense of "place" and so forth, after words denoting cattle and the like: *gavāṃ sthānaṃ gogoṣṭham* ("the place of cows is a cow-pen").
A buffalo pen; a camel pen; a sheep pen.

After the word *avi* (sheep), the suffix *kaṭac* is applied in the sense of a collection: *avikaṭaḥ*, meaning a collection of those [sheep]. The suffix *paṭac* is applied in the sense of extension: *avipaṭaḥ*.

The suffix *ca* is applied after the word *go* to express the sense of duality; e.g., *goyugam* (a pair of cows), *aśvagoyugam* (a pair consisting of a horse and a cow). The suffix *ca* is applied after the word *go* to express the sixfold meanings inherent in its base; e.g., *hastiṣaḍgavam* (six things related to an elephant), *aśvaṣaḍgavam* (six things related to a horse).
The suffix *ca* is applied after the word *taila* to express the sense of an oily substance; e.g., *iḍgudītailam* (oil of the *iḍgudī* tree).

The suffixes *śākaṭa* and *śākina* are applied after *ikṣu* and others when the sense is "in the field" (*bhavane kṣetre*). [Examples: *ikṣuśākaṭam* ("a field of sugarcane"), *mūlakaśākinam* ("a field of radishes").
After the word *ava*, the suffixes *ku* and *tāra* are also applied.
It may be *avakuṭāra*. Because of the word "ca" (and), there is also *kaṭac*: *avakaṭa*.
When denoting a bent nose, the suffixes *ṭīṭan*, *ñnāṭac*, and *bhraṭac* are applied in the sense of a name (*saṃjñāyām*).
The suffixes *avāṭ*, *ṭīṭaja*, and others occur when there is a bending of the nose, provided it is a name: *avaṭīṭaḥ*, *avanāṭaḥ*, *avabhraṭaḥ*.
After the prefix *ni*, the suffixes *biḍac* and *virīsac* are applied.

The forms *nibiram*, *nibiḍam*, and *nibirīsam* signify "dense" or "thick. [The suffixes] *inac*, *piṭac*, *cika*, and *ci* [are also applied]. *Urūnibirīsanitambabhārakhedi* means "exhausted by the weight of broad and thick hips."
When *neri* and *nacpiṭa* occur, by virtue of their association with them, the substitutes *cika* and *ci* respectively take their place. Thus:
*cikinaḥ*, *cipiṭaḥ*. It should be stated that when the suffix *kap* follows, the substitute *cik* takes its place. Thus: *cikkaḥ*.

These are quality-words (*guṇaśabda*) that may be derived in some way or another. For this very reason, the Sūtrakāra has disregarded words such as *cillapilla* and others, which are synonyms for "moist eyes.
[The suffix] *tyakan* is applied after two limiting adjuncts (*upādhi*) to express "near" and "ascended."

The suffix *tyakan* occurs after these two [words]. *Upatyakā* is land near the sea; *vanarājī* is a row of forests near the sea. *Adhityakā* is land ascended upon a mountain; it belongs to the mountain (*gireḥ*). Bhaṭṭi says: "The city is on the coastal plain (*samudropatyakā*) of the golden mountain (*haimī parvatādhityakā*).
The suffix *aṭhac* occurs after *karmaṇi* [to form *kārmaṇa*] and after *ghaṭa*.
One who is engaged in action is *karmaṭha*. [The word] *ghaṭa* is derived from the sense "to strive" (*ghaṭate*), with the suffix *ac* according to the rule for the *pacādi* group.
From that [root], the suffix *itac* is applied by the rule "tad asya sañjātam tārakādibhyaḥ" (Pāṇini 5.2.36).
In this sense, the suffix *itac* shall be applied after words such as *tāraka*. For example: *tārakitaṃ nabhaḥ* (the sky in which stars have appeared); *puṣpito vṛkṣaḥ* (a tree that has blossomed).

[The suffix is also applied after] *sukha*, *duḥkha*, *phala*, *kusuma*, *mukula*, *stavaka*, *tandrā*, *bubhukṣā*, *pipāsā*, *jvara*, *vraṇa*, *roga*, *vyādhi*, *utkaṇṭhā*, and *lajjā*. When [words] such as *garbha* denote a living being, [the suffix is applied]: *garbhitāḥ śālayaḥ* (rice plants that have become pregnant).

Why [is it] not applied when the object is not a living being? For example: *garbhiṇī gauḥ* (a pregnant cow). The phrase *tad asya* (that belongs to this) continues [to apply] up until *tad asmin* (that is in this).
When expressing a measure (*pramāṇe*), the suffixes *dvayasaC*, *daghnaC*, and *mātraC* are added.

In this context, the following forms may occur: *ūrudvayasam* "measuring two thighs," *payas* "water [reaching] up to the thighs," *nadī* "a river [reaching] up to the knees," *ūrudaghnām* "reaching the thighs," and *girikūṭadaghnaiḥ* "by those reaching the mountain peaks.

The suffixes *-dvayasaC-* and *-daghnaC-* are used for measurements above the navel; however, the suffix *-mātra-* is used again without such restriction. Examples include *prasthamātram ghṛtam* "ghee measuring one *prastha*" and *tanmātram* "of that measure. Regarding the rule *pramāṇe laś ca*: *la-* is a technical term (*saṃjñā*) for *luk* (elision) used by ancient teachers. After words denoting measurement, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffixes beginning with *-dvayasaC-*. Examples are *śamaḥ* "a span" (its measurement is a *śama*), *muṣṭiḥ* "a fist," *vitastiḥ* "a cubit," and *hastaḥ* "a hand. A *śama* consists of fourteen finger-breadths (*aṅgula*).

The suffix of a *dvigu* compound is always elided. Examples: *dvijānu* "water reaching to both knees," *dvivitastiḥ* "two spans long. The inclusion of the word "always" (*nityam*) is for the purpose of ensuring the elision of the *mātrac* suffix even when its presence is merely suspected.

The suffix *ḍaṭ* is used after a numeral to denote a *stoma*. Examples: *saptadaśaḥ stomaḥ* "a seventeen-fold hymn-chant," *viṃśaḥ stomaḥ* "a twenty-fold hymn-chant," *ekaviṃśaḥ* "a twenty-one-fold hymn-chant. Due to the marker *ṭ*, there is elision of the final vowel and what follows it (*ṭilopa*). The suffix *ḍini* is used after the words *pañcan* and *śati* to denote those things whose measure is such. Examples: *pañcadaśinaḥ ardhamāsāḥ* "fortnights consisting of fifteen [days]," *triṃśino māsāḥ* "months consisting of thirty [days]."
And [the suffix *mātraC* is added] after the word *viṃśati*. [Examples: *viṃśinaḥ* (twenty-fold), *āṅgirasaḥ*.

The suffix *mātraC* is added after words expressing measure (*pramāṇa*), quantity (*parimāṇa*), and also after numerals (*saṃkhyā*), when there is uncertainty. After a word for measure: *śamaṃ pramāṇam asya syān na vā* ("Is its measure a *śama* or not? → *śamamātram*. *hastamātram*. After a word for quantity: *prasthamātram*. After a numeral: *pañcamātram*, *daśamātram*. The suffixes *dvayasaC* and *mātraC* are added after a word ending in *vatU* in the sense of the base itself (*svārthe*). [Examples: *tāvadeva* ("just that much") → *tāvaddvayasam*, *tāvanmātram*.
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the words *puruṣa* and *hastin*.

The suffix *aṇ* occurs after these two [words] when they denote a measure (*pramāṇa*). For example: *pauruṣam ambhaḥ* ("water whose measure is a man") and *hāstinam* ("measured by an elephant"). Because of the word "and" (*ca*) in the rule, the suffixes *-dvayasaC*, *-daghn-aC*, and *-mātraC* should also be cited as examples.
Furthermore, the suffix *-vat-uP* occurs after the pronouns *yat*, *tat*, and *etad* when denoting a measure.
The suffix *vatup* occurs after these [words] in this sense. That which is its measure (*parimāṇa*) is *yāvān*, *tāvān*, and *etāvān*.
After the words *kim* and *idam*, *va* is substituted for *vatup*.

The suffix *vatup* occurs after these two [words] in the sense of measure, and *va* is replaced by *gha*. [Examples: *kiyān*, *kiyatī*; *iyān*, *iyatī*. Furthermore, the suffix *ḍati* occurs after *kim* in the sense of numerical measure.

The suffix *ḍati* occurs after a numeral used in the sense of delimitation (*pariccheda*). The suffix *vatup* also occurs [in this sense]. For both of these suffixes, *gha* is substituted for *va*. "What is the number of these?"—*kati guṇinaḥ* ("how many possessors of qualities?"). "How many possessors of qualities are there?"—*kiyantaḥ santi guṇinaḥ*.
The suffix *tayap* occurs after a numeral in the sense of a part (*avayava*).

The suffix *tayap* is added to a numeral when it denotes the number of constituent parts (*avayava*) of a whole. For example: *pañcatayam* (a group consisting of five parts), *daśatayam* (a group consisting of ten parts), and *catuṣṭayī rajjuḥ* (a rope consisting of four strands).
After the words *dvi* and *tri*, the suffix *ayaj* is optionally substituted for *tayap*.

After these two [words *dvi* and *tri*], the suffix *tayaP* may optionally take the form *ayaj*. Thus: *dvayam* or *dvitayam*; *trayam* or *tritayam*. Also: *dvayī* or *dvitayī*; *trayī* or *tritayī*.
After *ubha*, the suffix *tayaP* always takes the form *ayaj* and is udātta-accented.

After the word *ubha*, the suffix *tayap* always takes the replacement *ayac*. Thus, that which has both as its two parts is *ubhayo maṇiḥ* (a necklace of both), and *ubhaye devamanuṣyāḥ* (both gods and men).
After a stem ending in *daśan* (ten), the suffix *ḍa* is added in the sense of "this is more than that."

In this sense, the suffix *ḍa* (which becomes *a*) is applied after a word ending in *daśan*. For example: "one hundred with eleven added to it" is *ekādaśaṃ śatam*; likewise, *dvādaśaṃ śatam*, *caturdaśaṃ śatam*, or even *sahasram*. This designation applies only to the numbers one hundred (*śata*) and one thousand (*sahasra*).
Why is it not called *ṣaṣṭhaṃ śatam* here? [Because] the suffix *ac* is used in the sense of possession (*matvarthīya*).
And [the elision of the case-ending] occurs after words ending in *śat* and after the word *viṃśati*.

The suffix *ḍa* occurs after words ending in *śad* and after *viṃśati*, when used in the sense of "one part out of" (*pūrvārtha*). For example: *triṃśaṃ śatam* (one-thirtieth of a hundred), or *catvāriṃśaṃ śatam/sahasram* (one-fortieth of a hundred or a thousand). Also after *viṃśati*: *viṃśaṃ śatam* (one-twentieth of a hundred). And after words ending in those [suffixes]: *ekaviṃśaṃ śatam/sahasram* (one-twenty-first of a hundred or a thousand), or *dvāviṃśaṃ sahasram* (one-twenty-second of a thousand). Because the rule applies to what is preceded by a numeral (*saṃkhyāpūrva*), there is no application of the rule to words such as *gotriṃśat*.
The suffix *mayaṭ* is used after a numeral when expressing a measure of quality (*guṇanimāna*).

By the "frog-leap" method, the word *tad* (that) is understood here as *asya* (of this). The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied after a numeral when expressing the value (*nimāna*) or price of a portion (*bhāga*). For example: *dvimayam udaśvit yavānām* ("two portions of curdled milk are the value of one portion of barley"); *trimayī drākṣā guḍasya* ("three portions of molasses are the value of one portion of grapes"); *caturmayam*. [The suffix] *ḍaṭ* is used in the sense of "completing that" (*tasya pūraṇe*).

In this sense, the suffix *ḍaṭ* shall be applied after a numeral. For example: the eleventh [completing] chapter (*ekādaśaḥ sargaḥ*); the twelfth son (*dvādaśaḥ putraḥ*); the twentieth verse (*viṃśī kārikā*); the eleventh lunar day (*ekādaśī tithiḥ*). After a numeral ending in *n*, but not preceded by another numeral, the suffix *maṭ* is added.

The augment *maṭ* shall not be applied to the suffix *ḍaṭ* when it follows a word ending in *n* or a numeral beginning with a non-numeral (*asaṃkhyādi*). For example: *pañcamaḥ* (the fifth), *saptamaḥ* (the seventh). Why "ending in *n*"? Consider *viṃśaḥ* (the twentieth) and *triṃśaḥ* (the thirtieth). Why "beginning with a non-numeral"? Consider *ekādaśaḥ* (the eleventh).
Furthermore, in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *thaṭ* is also applied.
This is one *chandas*-sūtra:
"After the words *ṣaṭ*, *kati*, *katipaya*, and *catur*, [the suffix] *thuk* [is added]."

The augment *thuk* shall be added to these [words] when the suffix *ḍaṭ* follows. Examples: *ṣaṣṇām pūraṇaḥ* (the filler of six) becomes *ṣaṣṭhaḥ*; *katithaḥ*; *katipayathaḥ*; *caturthaḥ*; *katithī*; *katipayathī*. In the case of *catur*, there is optionally the substitution of *chaya-ta* along with the elision of the initial syllable. Examples: *turīyaḥ*; *turyaḥ*. After the words *bahu*, *pūga*, *gaṇa*, and *saṃgha*, the augment *tithuk* is applied.

In these cases, when the suffix *ḍaṭ* is applied, there is the augment *tithuk*. For example: *bahūnām pūraṇaḥ* becomes *bahutithaḥ*; *pūgatithaḥ*; *gaṇatithaḥ*; and "splitting many enemies" (*bhindan saṃghatithān dviṣaḥ*). Here, because it is the ordinal of many females (*bahvīnām pūraṇī*), there is the substitution of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) since the suffix *ḍaṭ* (which is not *āḍha*) follows a *bha*-stem; subsequently, the augment *tithuk* is added—thus: *bahutithī*.
[Likewise,] *ithuk* is added after the suffix *vat*.
After a stem ending in *vat*, the suffix *ḍaṭ* takes the augment *ithuk*. Thus, *tāvatām pūraṇaḥ* becomes *tāvatithaḥ*; likewise, *yāvatithaḥ*.
After the word *dvi*, the suffix *tīya* is applied.
The suffix *ḍat* would apply [to form] *dvitīyaḥ*. This would subvert [the application of] *ḍaṭ*. Thus, *dvitīyaḥ*. And for *tri*, there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) as well.
In the sense of "completing," there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the vowel *ṛ* in the word *tri*, and the suffix *tīya* shall also be applied. Thus, *tṛtīyaḥ*.
From the words *viṃśati* and so forth, the suffix *tamap* is optionally applied.

After the word *viṃśati* and others, the suffix *ḍaṭ* may optionally take the augment *tamaṭ*. Thus, the ordinal for "twenty" is either *viṃśatitamaḥ* or *viṃśaḥ*; for "thirty," *triṃśattamaḥ* or *triṃśaḥ*; for "twenty-first," *ekaviṃśatitamī* or *ekaviṃśī*; and for "thirty-first," *ekatriṃśattamam* or *ekatriṃśam*. However, after words beginning with *śata*, as well as after *māsa*, *ardhamāsa*, and *saṃvatsara*, the suffix *ḍaṭ* with the augment *tamaṭ* is compulsory.

The suffix *ḍaṭ* following a numeral beginning with *śata*, as well as after the words *māsa*, *ardhamāsa*, and *saṃvatsara*, shall always take the augment *tam*. Examples: the filler of a hundred is *śatatamaḥ*; *sahasratamaḥ*; *lakṣatamaḥ*; *ekaśatatamaḥ*; *dvisahasratamaḥ*; *saptalakṣatamaḥ*. The day that fills a month is *māsatamaḥ*; *ardhamāsatamaḥ*; *saṃvatsaratamaḥ*.
[The same applies] after numerals beginning with sixty, provided they are not *asaṃkhya*.

For the words *ṣaṣṭi*, *saptati*, *aśīti*, and *navati*, the suffix *ḍaṭ* shall always take the augment *tamaṭ*. This serves to set aside the optional application of [suffixes] such as *viṃśati*. Examples: the sixtieth (*ṣaṣṭitamaḥ*), the seventieth (*saptatitamaḥ*), the eightieth (*aśītitamaḥ*), and the ninetieth (*navatitamaḥ*). Why "not preceded by another numeral" (*asaṃkhyādeḥ*)? [In the case of] *ekaṣaṣṭi*, it may be either *ekaṣaṣṭiḥ* or *ekaṣaṣṭitamaḥ*. The suffix *ḍaṭ* has been explained.
And the word *matu* [is used] in the sense of hymns (*sūkta*) and chants (*sāman*).

The suffix *cha* shall be applied after a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) in the sense of possession (*matvartha*), when a hymn (*sūkta*) or a chant (*sāman*) is to be expressed. For example: "The hymn in which the word *acchāvāka* occurs" is called *acchāvākīyam*; "the chant belonging to Vāratanta" is *vāratantavīyam*. [There is] elision (*luk*) of the suffix when referring to a chapter (*adhyāya*) or a section (*anuvāka*).

In these two cases, there shall be elision (*luk*) of the suffix *cha* when it has the sense of possession (*matvartha*). For example: *gardabhāṇḍa* as the name of a chapter (*adhyāya*) or a section (*anuvāka*). Some also accept the form *śrutim*.
This is because the option (*anyatarasyām*) is understood by "frog-leap" (*maṇḍūkapluti*) continuity [from a previous rule]: *gardabhāṇḍīya* as the name of a chapter.
After words beginning with *vimukta*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied.

After these [words], when expressing the sense of possession (*matvartha*), the suffix *aṇ* shall be applied to those two [suffixes, *taddhita* and *svārthika*]. For example: *vaimuktaḥ*, meaning "an adhyāya or anuvāka in which a liberated person exists"; *daivāsuraḥ*.
After the group beginning with *goṣada*, the suffix *vun* is applied.

The suffix *vun* shall likewise be applied after these: *goṣada*, *iṣetva*, *mātariśvan*, and *pathin* when meaning "skilled therein. For example: *goṣadaka* refers to a chapter (*adhyāya*) or a section (*anuvāka*) in which the word *goṣada* occurs; *goṣada* itself [is used similarly]. [Also: *iṣetva*, *mātariśvan*, and *pathaka* (one skilled in the paths).
In this sense, the suffix *vun* occurs after the word *pathin*. For example: one who is skilled on the road is *pathakaḥ*.
After words such as *ākarṣa*, the suffix *kan* is applied.
One who is skilled at attracting is an *ākarṣaka*; likewise, a *jayaka* and a *tsaruka*. [The suffix -aka is applied] after the words *dhana* and *hiraṇya* when desire is intended.

The suffix *kan* is applied after these two [words] when used in the sense of "desire" (*kāma*). For example: *dhanakaḥ*, meaning one whose desire or longing is for wealth; *hiraṇyakaḥ*. [Objection: Since this seeker of liberation (*mumukṣu*) is free from longing even for his own body, how could he have a desire for wealth?
[Reply: Because he is attached to his own limbs.
The suffix *kan* is applied here after these [words]. One who is attached to hair is a *keśakaḥ*; a *nakhakaḥ*; a *dantakaḥ*.
After the word *udara*, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied when it refers to one who is not young (*ādyūna*).
He would be one who is intent on his belly, gluttonous, and voracious; a voracious person is one who lacks the desire for conquest;
he is one who has become fully devoted to grain.

The suffix *kan* occurs after the word *sasya*. That which is fully grown or perfected through the quality (*guṇa*) of grain is called *sasyaka*: a *sasyaka* gem, a *sasyaka* rice plant, a *sasyaka* calf.
[The suffixes] *aṃś* and *ha* occur after [the word] *aṃśa*.
In this sense, the suffix *kan* may be applied: *aṃśakaḥ* means an heir. [The suffix *kan* is also used] after the word *tantra* when meaning "recently removed."
What could it be? A *tantraka* is a new cloth.
[The suffix] *ka* is applied after *brāhmaṇa* and *uṣṇika* when they function as proper names (*saṃjñā*).

These two words, *brāhmaṇaka* and *uṣṇikā*, are derived as irregular forms (*nipātana*). *Brāhmaṇaka* refers to a region where Brāhmaṇas subsist by the profession of arms; *uṣṇikā* refers to a thin gruel.
[The suffix *kan* is applied] after the words *śīta* and *uṣṇa* when they denote one who performs an action [in that manner].
What might they be? One who performs cold tasks slowly is "cold" (śītaka), meaning lazy; one who performs hot tasks quickly is "hot" (uṣṇaka), meaning skillful.
[This applies] additionally.
This [suffix] is elided in the sense of "mounted upon. After a word meaning "mounted upon," the suffix *kan* shall occur with the elision of the subsequent member of the compound.
Thus, *anuka*, *abhika*, and *abhīka* mean "one who desires."
The forms *anukam*, *abhikam*,
and *abhīkam* are derived as irregular substitutes for the verb *kam* (to desire) when used with the sense "he seeks after" (*anvicchati*) by means of the side (*pārśvena*).

The term *pārśva* indicates a crooked or dishonest means (*anṛjūpāya*). From that [root], the suffix *kan* is applied in the sense of "one who seeks" or "one who pursues," resulting in *pārśvaka*, meaning a rogue (*śaṭha*).
After the words *ayaḥśūla* and *daṇḍājina*, the suffixes *ṭhak* and *ṭhañ* are respectively applied.

The suffixes *ṭhak* and *ṭhañ* shall be applied in the sense of "one who seeks after [something] by means of that," when the motivation is either severity (*taikṣṇya*) or hypocrisy (*dambha*). For example: *āyaḥśūlikaḥ* means one who acts with severity; *dāṇḍājinikaḥ* means one who is hypocritical.
Regarding the phrase "taking [a thing] so many times," there is optionally elision (*luk*) of the suffix.

The ordinal number that completes a specific count is called *tāvatitha*. From such an ordinal, which functions as the instrument of grasping, the suffix *kan* is added in its own sense (*svārthe*), and there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of the ordinal suffix. By means of the second form, he grasps the book: *dvikam* or *dvitīyakam*; *trikam* or *tṛtīyakam*; *catuṣkam* or *caturthakam*. It should be stated that when [one grasps] by means of such an ordinal, the suffix *kan* is added and the elision of the suffix is obligatory. One who grasps by means of the sixth form is *ṣaṭkaḥ*, meaning "intelligent. He is the leader (*grāmaṇīḥ*) of these.

In this sense, the suffix *kan* may be applied: "you are a villager," "these are yours" (*tvatkāḥ*), "these are mine" (*matkāḥ*), "these are Devadatta’s" (*devadattakāḥ*). [The word] *matkaṃ* means "my opinion.
[The word] *śṛṅkhala* refers to the tether for a young camel.
The suffix *kan* is applied in the sense of "having a chain as its bond"; thus, *śṛṅkhalakaḥ* is a name for a young camel (*karabha*). *Utka* means "eager" or "anxious."
If one is anxious or distracted in mind due to the timing or the purpose [of the treatment] during an illness, [one should act accordingly].

The suffix *kan* is applied after these two [words] when a disease is meant. From a word denoting time: a fever that occurs on a day is *divasakaḥ*; *māsakaḥ*. That which occurs on the second day is *dvitīyakaḥ*; *caturthakaḥ*.

That by which something is employed is called the "instrument" (*prayojana*), meaning the cause: a fever employed by a *viṣapuṣpa* flower is *viṣapuṣpakaḥ*; *kāśapuṣpakaḥ*. One employed by a future heat is *tāpakaḥ*; *śītakaḥ*.
Jayāditya maintains that the suffix *ka* is used for the fruit (*phala*) and the purpose (*prayojana*). For example, *śītaka* refers to a fever whose effect is coldness.

Here, the subsequent mention of "technical term" (*saṃjñā*) is connected [to this rule], and by means of it, the intended meaning is grasped. [The suffix *ka* is applied] when food is generally found in something, provided it is a technical term.
In this sense, the suffix *kan* may be applied after a name: *guḍāpūpikā* (a festival where molasses-cakes are generally the food), *pūrṇikā*, *tilāpūpikā*.
The suffix *ini* should be prescribed after the word *vaṭaka*: *vaṭakinī* (the full-moon day [when *vaṭaka*s are eaten]), *pṛthukinī*.
After the word *kulmāṣa*, the suffix *añ* is applied.
The suffix *añ* shall occur in the sense of "belonging to" (*pūrvārthe*). Examples: *kaulmāṣī tithiḥ* (the lunar day belonging to the Kaulmāṣas);
*śrotriyaṃśchando'dhīte* (one who studies the Veda belonging to the Śrotriyas).
In this sense, this [suffix] is prescribed as a *ghan* suffix; its *n* is for the sake of the accent. An example is *śrotriya*, meaning a Brāhmaṇa learned in the Vedas.
[The suffixes] *ini* and *ṭhan* are used when it is meant that "this person has eaten the *śrāddha*."
The suffixes *ini* and *ṭhan* occur after the word *śrāddha* in the sense of "having eaten this [śrāddha]. Thus: *śrāddhī* and *śrāddhikaḥ*.
After the word *pūrva*, the suffix *ini* occurs.

The word *anena* (by this) follows as the agent (*kartṛ*), and it requires an action (*kriyā*). Therefore, having supplied any action whatsoever, the suffix *ini* shall be added after [the word] *pūrva* and others. For example: "He has previously sat, grasped, gone, eaten, or drunk"—[one who has done so is called] *pūrvī*, *pūrviṇau*, *pūrviṇaḥ*.
[The suffix is also applied] after a word that has *pūrva* as its prior member (*sapūrvāt*).

The suffix *ini* shall also be applied after the word *pūrva* when it is preceded by another word. The compound *kṛtapūrvamanena* ("this was done by him previously") is formed according to the rule *sup-supā*. Thus: *kṛtapūrvī kaṭān* ("one who has previously made mats"), *bhuktapūrvī odanam* ("one who has previously eaten rice"), and *bhuktapūrvī dadhīni* ("one who has previously eaten curds").
[The suffix *ini* is also applied] after words such as *iṣṭa*.

The suffix *ini* may be used [after a word ending in a case-suffix]. For example: *iṣṭī* means "one by whom sacrifices have been performed"; *adhītī* means "one who has studied grammar"; *nirākṛtī*, *gṛhītī*, *kṛtī*, *śrutī*—these denote one who is wise according to the opinions of the elders.
In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the forms *paripanthin* and *pariparin* are used in the sense of "an adversary" or "one who stands in the way."
The Chandaḥsūtra is one;
it is to be sought in every verse.
The suffix *an* is applied after the word *pad*, provided that the sense is "one who seeks" (*anveṣṭṛ*). For example: *mṛgasyānupadī rāmaḥ* ("Rāma is a tracker of the deer").
[Furthermore, the suffix *an* is applied] after the word *sākṣāt* when it denotes a person who sees directly, provided the word is a proper name (*saṃjñāyām*).

If the word *sākṣin* is intended as a technical term (*saṃjñā*) denoting a "witness" (*draṣṭṛ*), it would be derived from the suffix *ini* added directly to the word *sākṣāt*. Thus: *sākṣāt draṣṭā* = *sākṣī*; *sākṣiṇau*.
A hereditary disease is to be treated in another's field.

Another's field (*parakṣetra*) refers to the body of another birth; one who is to be treated therein is designated as *kṣetriya*. *Kṣetriya* refers to the disease of leprosy (*kuṣṭha*), meaning it is incurable.
*Indriya* means the mark of Indra, seen by Indra, created by Indra, favored by Indra, or given by Indra.
The suffix *indra* is replaced by *indriya*; *indra* means the self (*ātman*), and [the suffix] denotes that which is its mark (*liṅga*), or that which was seen or created by it, and so forth.

This rule (*yoga*) is intended to show that there is no fixed restriction in the etymological derivation (*vyutpatti*) of technical names (*saṃjñā-śabda*). [This concludes the section on] possessive suffixes (*matvarthīya*) among the secondary derivatives (*taddhita*).
The suffix *matup* occurs [after a nominal stem] when the sense is "this belongs to him" or "this is in this."

The suffix *matup* occurs after the word *tat*, when it ends in the nominative case and is qualified by the sense of the verb *asti* (to exist), in the sense of the genitive and locative cases. For example: *gāvo 'sya santi* (he has cows) becomes *gomān*; *yavā asmin santi* (barley exists in this place) becomes *yavamān deśaḥ* (a land possessing barley).

By the use of the particle *iti*, the scope of the meaning is restricted: [the suffix is used] in the senses of abundance (*bhūman*), censure (*nindā*), praise (*praśaṃsā*), constant connection (*nityayoga*), and excellence (*atiśāyana*).
When there is a desire to express the existence [of a quality] in a connection, the suffixes *matup* and others are employed.
One who possesses cows; one with a hump on the back; one endowed with beauty; a tree that yields milk; a girl with a large belly; one who carries a staff; one who carries an umbrella.
It should be stated that the suffix *matup* is elided after words expressing qualities: "that which has whiteness" is called "white," as in "a white cloth."

But when the accepted position is that words such as "white" (śukla) apply to both a quality-possessor (guṇin) and a quality (guṇa) by virtue of their own inherent nature (svabhāva), then there is no purpose for the elision (luk).
This also applies to [the case of] "taste" (rasa) and so forth.

The suffix *matup* alone would apply after words such as *rasa*, and no other *matvarthīya* suffixes [would apply]. For example: *rasavān*, *rūpavān*, *gandhavān*, *śabdavān*, *sparśavān*, *snehavān*.

However, the author of the Bhāṣya favors the rejection (*pratyākhyāna*) of this rule, because we observe forms such as *rasiko rājā* (a king who enjoys flavors), *rūpiṇyo 'psarasaḥ* (apsarases possessing beauty), and *sparśī vāyuḥ* (wind possessing touch). [Furthermore:
*prāṇisthād āto laj anyatarasyām* (after a word ending in *ā* that denotes something residing in a living being, the suffix *lac* is optionally applied).
After words denoting parts of a living being that end in a short vowel, the suffix *lac* may optionally occur in the sense of possession (*matvarthe*). Examples: *cūḍālaḥ*, *śirālaḥ*, *jaṅghālaḥ*.
The optionality is intended to allow for the addition of *matup*: thus, *cūḍāvān*. Why "denoting parts of a living being"? [Consider: *śikhāvān pradīpaḥ* ("a lamp with a flame").
And [the suffix *matup* is applied] after *sidhma* and the others.
The suffix *lac* shall be applied after these: *sidhmalaḥ*, *gaḍulaḥ*.

After *pārṣṇi* and *dhamani*, there is also lengthening [of the penultimate vowel]: *pārṣṇīlaḥ*, *dhamanīlaḥ*. After *vāta*, *danta*, *bala*, *lalāṭa*, and *gala*, there is also the suffix *ūṅ*: *vātūlaḥ*, *dantūlaḥ*, *balūlaḥ*, *lalāṭūlaḥ*, *galūlaḥ*.
The suffix *lac* occurs after the words *jaṭā*, *ghaṭā*, and *kālā* when expressing "delay. [Examples: *jaṭālaḥ*, *ghaṭālaḥ*, *kālālaḥ*.
It also occurs after words meaning "small creatures" and "affliction. [Examples: *yūkālaḥ*, *mūrcchālaḥ*, *vicarcikālaḥ*.
The suffix *matup* is added everywhere according to the recurrence of conceptual construction—as in the case of "one who has *sidhma*" (*sidhmavān*).
[Furthermore, the suffix *ini* is applied] after the words *vatsa* and *aṃsa* when expressing desire and strength, respectively.

The suffix *lac* occurs after these two—*kāma* and *bala*—in the sense of the possessive (*matvartha*). *Vatsalaḥ* means "possessing affection" (*kāmavān*); *aṃsalaḥ* means "possessing strength" (*balavān*). After *phena*, *ilac* also occurs.
The suffixes *lac* and *lac* occur after the words beginning with *phena*; thus, *phenilaḥ* and *phenalaḥ*. The suffix *matup* also occurs: *phenavān*.
The suffixes *śa*, *na*, and *lac* occur after the groups of words beginning with *loman*, *pāman*, and *piccha*, respectively.

The suffix *śa* occurs after words such as *loman* in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). Examples: *lomaśaḥ* (hairy), *lomavān*; *kapiśaḥ*, *giriśaḥ*. The suffix *na* occurs after words such as *pāman*: *pāmanaḥ*, *pāmavān*; *śleṣmaṇaḥ*; *hemana*; *balinaḥ*. After the word *aṅga*, [the suffix *na* occurs] in the sense of "beautiful": *aṅganā* (a woman with beautiful limbs).
[The suffix] *ilac* is applied after *lakṣmī*, and also after *accas*. *Lakṣmaṇaḥ*. [The suffix] *naṅ* is applied after *dadru*, and there is also shortening [of the vowel]. *Dadruṇaḥ*.
[The suffix] *ilac* is applied after words beginning with *piccha*: *picchilaḥ*, *jaṭilaḥ*, *urasilaḥ*.
The suffix *ṇa* is applied after the words *prajñā*, *śraddhā*, *arcā*, and *vṛtti*.

The suffix *ṇa* occurs after these [stems] in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). *prājñaḥ*, *prajñāvān*: wise, learned; *prājñā*: a wise woman. *śrāddhaḥ*, *śraddhāvān*: faithful; *ārcaḥ*, *arcāvān*: venerable; *vārttaḥ*, *vṛttimān*: subsisting by a livelihood. After the words *tapas* and *sahasra*, the suffixes *vin* and *ini* [are added].
From these two [words *tapas* and *sahasra*], these two suffixes—*vin* and *ini*—are applied: *tapasvī* and *sahasrī*.
This rule is stated so that the suffix *aṇ* may not supersede them;
for there is also the suffix *aṇ*.
The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these two [words]. Examples: *tāpasaḥ*, *sāhasraḥ*.
There is an extension of the rule for *jyotsnā* and others: the suffix *aṇ* shall be applied. Examples: *jyautsnaḥ pakṣaḥ*, *tāmisraḥ*, *kauṇḍinaḥ*.
Furthermore, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after *sikatā* and *śarkarā*.

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after these two [words]. For example: *saikataḥ ghaṭaḥ* (a pot made of sand) and *śārkaraṃ madhu* (honey produced from sugar). Furthermore, when the word refers to a region (*deśa*), the suffixes *lub*, *ilac*, and *ca* [are also applied].

After these two [words], when denoting a region (*deśa*), there is the elision (*lup*) of the suffix, and *ilac* is also applied; by the force of the word "and" (*ca*), the suffix *aṇ* is also applied. [Examples: *sikatā* as a region: *sikatilaḥ*, *saikataḥ*, and with the suffix *matup*: *sikatāvān*. *Śarkarā*: *śarkarilaḥ*, *śārkaraḥ*, *śarkarāvān*.
After *danta*, when meaning "protruding," the suffix *urac* is applied.
One who has protruding teeth is called *danturaḥ*.
[This is formed by adding] the suffix *ra* after the words *ūṣa*, *suṣi*, *muṣka*, and *madhu*.

The suffix *ra* occurs after these words in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). *ūṣaraḥ* (saline soil), *suṣiram* (a hole), *muṣkaraḥ* (having testicles), *madhuraḥ* (sweet). And [the suffix *ra* occurs] after *kha*, *mukha*, *kuñjara*, *nagara*, *nakha*, *pāṇḍu*, and *pāṃsu*. *kharaḥ* (donkey), *mukharaḥ* (talkative), *kuñjaraḥ* (elephant), *nagaram* (city), *nakharaḥ* (clawed), *pāṇḍuraḥ* (pale), *pāṃsuraḥ* (dusty). *pādaḥ* (foot).
Jayāditya states that *kaccha* is also short [in this formation], as in *kacchura*. [The suffix] *ma* is applied after [stems ending in] *dyu* and *dru*.
The suffix *ma* shall be applied after these two: *dyu-maḥ*, *drumaḥ*. After the word *keśa*, the suffix *va* is optionally applied.
The suffix *va* may optionally be applied after the word *keśa*. Thus: *keśavaḥ*, *keśī*, *keśikaḥ*, or *keśavān*.

It should be stated that it is also seen after other words. The suffix *va* may be applied [after these]: *maṇivaḥ*, *hiraṇyavaḥ*, *iṣṭakāvaḥ*, *rājīvam*. After the word *arṇas*, there is also elision [of the final syllable]. Thus: *arṇavaḥ*.

The suffix *i* is applied after the words *medhā* and *ratha* [to form the possessive suffix *in*], according to some: *medhiraḥ* ("intelligent") and *rathiraḥ* ("charioteer"). Amara states: "The forms *rathira*, *rathika*, and *rathī* all mean 'charioteer'.
Furthermore, the suffix *a* is applied after the word *gāṇḍī* when forming a proper name (*saṃjñāyām*).
From these two [suffixes], there is the form *nāmni* for you. *Gāṇḍīva* is the bow of Pārtha;
Jayāditya says that even after a short vowel it becomes *gāṇḍiva*. *Ajagava* is the Pināka bow; others say it is *ajakava* because of its connection with Aja (Viṣṇu) and Ka (Brahmā).
The suffixes *ra* and *nīra* are added after the words *kāṇḍa*, *aṇḍa*, and others.
From these two, these two forms should be derived: *kāṇḍīraḥ* and *aṇḍīraḥ*. There is a difference in accent.
[The suffix] *valac* is applied after the words *rajas*, *kṛṣi*, *āsuti*, and *pariṣad*.

The suffix *valac* is applied after these [words] in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). *rajasvalā* (a woman possessing menstrual flow); here, by the rule *valaḥ*, the vowel is lengthened. *kṛṣīvalaḥ* (a farmer). *āsutīvalaḥ* (a liquor-seller); he is a *śauṇḍika*. *pariṣadvalaḥ* (a king who possesses an assembly); from the root *sad* preceded by *pari*, the suffix *kvip* is applied by the rule *satsūdviṣa-* etc., and the substitution of *ṣ* occurs by the rule *sadiraprateḥ*. Regarding the phrase "that which was formerly possessed by the *pariṣadvalas*" (*yā samprati prāk pariṣadvalānām*), there is the *vyoṣa* meter. Regarding "the *pariṣadvalas* by the great Brahmins" (*pariṣadvalān mahābrahmaiḥ*), there is the *bhaṭiṭa* meter. However, in this case, even though there is one foot of nine syllables, there is a difference in meter; as stated in the *Bhāgavṛtti*: "In the case of roots with two objects, they say that the *la*-suffixes [denote] the primary object when it is to be expressed."

Keśava [the author of the Kāśikāvṛtti] maintains that the elision of the letter *i* occurs by virtue of the *pṛṣodarādi* group, through the principle of partial modification (*ekadeśavikāra*), so that the suffix *valac* is applied even to the word *parpa*.

It should be stated that [this suffix] is seen after other words as well; for example, with *valac*: *bhrātṛvalaḥ* (one who has brothers as strength) and *putravalaḥ* (one who has sons as strength). [The suffix *valac* is also applied] after *danta* and *śikhā* when a technical name (*saṃjñā*) is formed.

The suffix *valac* is applied after these two [words]. Examples: *dantāvalaḥ* (an elephant), *śikhāvalaḥ* (a peacock). [The following are also formed with this suffix: *jyotsnā*, *tāmisrā*, *śṛṅgī*, *gaṇī*, *ūrjasvī*, *ūrjasvalaḥ*, *gomī*, *malinaḥ*, and *malīmasaḥ*.
These eight are irregularly formed (nipātita) with the suffix *a*. In the word *tamiśrā*, the feminine gender is not restrictive; it is also seen elsewhere—as in *tamiśram nabhaḥ* (the dark sky).
From this [root], the suffixes *ini* and *ṭhan* are applied.

The suffixes *ini* and *niṭhan* may occur after [stems ending in] vowels other than *a*. For example: *daṇḍī* (staff-bearer), *daṇḍikaḥ* (one who has a staff). The suffix *matup* occurs everywhere: *daṇḍavān* (possessing a staff). Examples: *taṇḍulī*, *taṇḍulikaḥ*; *kāryī*, *kāryikaḥ*; *hāryī*, *hāryikaḥ*. In some cases, due to lack of conventional usage (*anabhidhāna*), they do not occur: *khavān*, *kārakavān*, *vṛkṣavān*, *vyāghravān*. When the sense is "there are staffs in this," it is *daṇḍavatī śālā* (a hall possessing staffs). Thus it has been said:

"Those two [suffixes, *ini* and *niṭhan*,] are traditionally taught not to occur after a monosyllabic stem, nor after a word formed with a *kṛt* suffix, nor after a genus name (*jāti*), nor when the locative case is used."
"In the formulation of secondary derivatives (taddhita), that which is required as the denotation [is the base]. Thus [it is said].
And [the suffix -matup is applied] after vrīhi and other words.

The suffixes *ini* and *iṭhan* should be applied after words such as *vrīhi* according to their specific designations. Thus: *vrīhī*, *vrīhikaḥ*. It has been stated that the suffix *matup* is also used everywhere; thus: *vrīhimān*. After words such as *māyā*, only *ini* is used—thus: *māyī*, *māyikaḥ*. After words such as *śikhā*, only *ini* is used—thus: *śikhī*, *śikhāvān*; *mālī*, *mālāvān*.

The suffix *ṭhan* (ika) is applied after the words *mekhalā*, *vīṇā*, *saṃjñā*, *manīṣā*, *patākā*, *karman*, and *varman*; likewise, it is applied after words ending in *nau* and others—thus: *nāvikaḥ*, *yavakhadikaḥ*, and *yavakhadavān*. Furthermore, the suffix *ilac* is applied after words beginning with *tuṇḍa*.

The suffix *ilac* shall be applied after these [words], and both [the suffixes *ilac* and *ika*] as well. [Examples: *tundilaḥ*, *tundikaḥ*, *tundī*, *tundavān*; *udarilaḥ*, *udarikaḥ*, *udarī*, *udaravān*; *piciṇḍilaḥ*; likewise *picinda*. [The suffixes apply to] *yava* and *vrīhi*. Regarding *vrīhi*, there is an inclusion of its synonyms. [Examples: *śālilaḥ*, *śālikaḥ*. The suffix *śī* is also used. It has been stated that the suffix *matup* applies everywhere.

When there is growth in a limb of one's own body, [the suffixes *matup*, *ini*, and *thañ* are used]. For example: *sthalakarṇaḥ*, *karṇī*, *karṇilaḥ*, *karṇikaḥ*. But when there is no such growth—[as in the case of a natural ear]—one says *karṇavān*. For here [in the latter case], it is not so;
for [by the rule] "after words preceded by *eka* or *go*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is always used," [the form would be *kārnikaḥ*].
The suffix *ṭhañ* shall always be applied after [compounds] preceded by *eka* and preceded by *go*. Examples: *aikaśatikaḥ*, *aikasahasrikaḥ*, *gosahasrikaḥ*.

How is it that [the word] *ekadeśī* refers to the whole (*avayavī*)? Because of the continued application of the particle *iti*. This suffix *ṭhañ* is intended to follow only from a *karmadhāraya* compound.
The inclusion of the word "nitya" (always) is for the purpose of excluding other suffixes;
[this applies] from a *niṣka* up to a hundred thousand.
The suffix *ṭhañ* shall always be applied [in these senses]. Examples: *naiṣkaśatikaḥ*, *naiṣkasahasrikaḥ*.
After the word *rūpa*, the suffix *yaP* is applied in the senses of "struck" (*āhata*) and "praise" (*praśaṃsā*).

The suffix *yap* occurs after the word *rūpa* in the sense of "struck," in the sense of "praise," and in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). That which is produced by being struck—such as a coin—is called *āhata*. Thus, a *dīnāra* (gold coin) is called *rūpya* because it possesses beauty (*rūpa*). A man is called *rūpya* because he possesses a praiseworthy form. It is also seen after other words; for example, *yap*: mountains are called *himyāḥ* because snow (*hima*) is present there; a verse is called *padya*; sages are called *guṇyāḥ*. [In the phrase] "He did not deliberate between the seeker of merit and the one devoid of merit" (*arthinaṃ guṇyaguṇya iti na vyacārayat*), the suffix is applied. The suffix *vini* occurs after the words *asmāya*, *medhā*, and *sraj*.

The suffix *vin* shall be applied after these [words]. After a word ending in *asan*: *payasvī*, *yaśasvī*. Regarding those who possess illusion (*māyāvin*) but are not themselves illusory (*māyin*): *māyī*, *māyikaḥ*. From the word *māyā*, the suffixes *ini* and *iṭhan* also occur because it belongs to the *vrīhy-ādi* group. *medhāvī*, *sragvī*. Regarding the rule *tasau matvarthe* (Pāṇini 1.4.19), since the *Bhāṣya* provides examples such as *payasvān* and *yaśasvān*, it is inferred that even beyond the scope of the rule *ekagopūrvāṭ ṭhañ ñ nityam* (Pāṇini 5.2.118), there is an inclusion of the suffix *matup*. In the cases *sarasvān* and *sarasvatī*, there is no application of the suffix *vin*.
In the Vedic language, [the substitution of *o* for *as*] occurs frequently.
The *Chandaḥsūtra*:
[The suffix] *dīrgha* is applied to *āmaya*. It shall be *viniśca*. [Thus: *āmayāvī*.
The suffix *ārakan* is applied after *śṛṅga* and *vṛnda*. After these two, *ārakan* shall be applied. [Thus: *śṛṅgārakaḥ*, *vṛndārakaḥ*.

The suffix *inac* is applied after the words *phala* and *barhas*. Thus: *phalinaḥ* (fruit-bearing) and *barhiṇaḥ* (peacock). The suffix *ini* is also seen [after these]: *phalī* and *barhī*. The suffix *āluc* is optionally applied after the word *hṛdaya*. Thus: *hṛdayāluḥ*, *hṛdayī*, *hṛdayikaḥ*, or *hṛdayavān* (sensitive/possessing a heart).

The suffix *āluc* is applied after the words *śīta*, *uṣṇa*, and *tigma* when it denotes "not being able to endure that. Thus: *śītāluḥ* (unable to bear cold), *uṣṇāluḥ* (unable to bear heat), and *tigmāluḥ* (unable to bear sharpness). This is a designation used in the sense of censure (*kutsā*).

*Hima* takes *cela*, *elu*, and *ūla*: *himela* (a snowy region), *himelu* (snowy). *Balāt* takes *ūla*: *balūlaḥ* (one who cannot endure strength). *Vātāt* takes *ūla* in the sense of a collection (*samūha*) as well: *vātūlaḥ* (one who cannot endure wind, or a whirlwind).
The suffix *tap* is applied after the words *parvan* and *marut*; thus, *parvataḥ* and *maruttaḥ*.
The suffix *yuṣ* is applied after the word *ūrṇā*.
*Ūrṇāyuḥ* means "made of wool" or "a woolen blanket";
*vāco gminiḥ* means "one who possesses speech."
One who possesses speech is "vāggmī"; it contains two *ga* sounds. The suffixes *ālaj* and *aṭac* are used for one who speaks excessively.
The suffixes *vāca* and *imau* occur after the word *vāc* when it means "one who speaks much": *vācālaḥ*, *vācāṭaḥ*. These denote censure.
The suffix *svāmin* occurs in the sense of sovereignty.
The term *svāmin* occurs when lordship (*aiśvarya*) is to be understood. One who possesses something is a *svāmī*;
[this is formed] by adding the suffix *ac* to the group beginning with *arśas*.

After the class of words beginning with *arśas* (which is an *ākṛtigaṇa*), the suffix *ac* occurs in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). Examples: *arśasaḥ*, *urasaḥ*, *tundaḥ*, *kāṇaḥ*, *khañjaḥ*, *palitaḥ*, *malinaḥ*, *lavaṇaḥ*, *śuklaḥ*, *nīlaḥ*, *kālaḥ*, *godhūlaḥ*.
After a word denoting a disease, a physical defect, or something censurable, provided it resides in a living being, the suffix *ini* occurs [in the sense of possession].

The suffix *ini* occurs after these [words]. It supersedes [the application of] *ṭhan* and others. After a *dvandva* compound: *kaṭakavalayinī* (possessing bracelets and bangles), *śaṅkhanūpuriṇī* (possessing anklets). After words meaning "affliction" (*upatāpa*) or "disease" (*roga*): *kuṣṭhī* (one afflicted by leprosy), *kilāsī* (one afflicted by white leprosy), *śūlī* (one suffering from colic). [This applies] because of eating bad food. [The word] *garhya* means "blameworthy. *Kakudāvartī* (one with a hump and a curl). Why say "located on a living being" (*prāṇisthāt*)? [Consider: *puṣphalavān taruḥ* (a tree possessing flowers and fruits).
[The suffix *matup*] is not desired after parts of living beings—e.g., *pāṇipādavatī* ("having hands and feet") and *stanakeśavatī* ("having breasts and hair").

[The word] "from this" (*ataḥ*) applies only in these cases—e.g., *citrakalalāṭikāvatī* ("having a variegated forehead-mark"). [The suffix *matup*] is applied after words meaning "fainting" (*mūrchā*), and the augment *kuk* is added after the words "wind" (*vāta*) and "diarrhea" (*atisāra*).
The suffix *ini* shall be applied after these two, and the augment *kuk* is also added: *vātakī*, *atisārakī*.
It is also applied after *piśāca*: *piśācakī* (Vaiśravaṇa).
It is also applied after ordinal numerals when expressing age: [e.g., *dvitīyaka*].

When age (*vayas*) is to be expressed, only a word ending in a ordinal number (*pūraṇa*) followed by the suffix *ini* shall be used. For example: *pañcamī uṣṭraḥ* ("a camel that is five months or five years old") and *daśamī vṛddhaḥ* ("an old man who is ten years old"). [The suffix *ini* is also applied] after words such as *sukha* ("happiness") and others.
The suffix *ini* shall be applied [after a word ending in *sukha*, *kṛcchra*, *duḥkha*, or after words ending in *dharma*, *śīla*, and *varṇa*]. Examples: *sukhī*, *kṛcchrī*, *duḥkhī*.
[Also] from those ending in *dharma*, *śīla*, and *varṇa*.

The suffix *ini* occurs after words such as *dharma*, *anta*, and *ādi*. Examples: *dvijadharmī* (one whose duty is that of a twice-born), *bhikṣuśīlī* (one whose conduct is that of a mendicant), *brāhmaṇavarṇī* (one belonging to the Brahmin caste).
[The suffix *ini* also occurs] after words denoting hands when joined together.
The suffix *ini* occurs after "hasta" and other such words [to denote possession]. For example: *hastī*. Why [is it said] "in the sense of a genus"? [Consider: *hastavān* (one who possesses hands).
[The suffix *ini* occurs] after a word denoting color when referring to a religious student (*brahmacārin*).
The suffix *ni* shall be applied after words such as *varṇa*, provided they refer to a religious student (*brahmacārin*); thus, [one who is a student] is called *varṇī*.
After words such as *puṣkara*, it is applied when referring to a region (*deśa*).
The suffix *ini* shall be applied after these [words]. Examples: *puṣkariṇī*, *padminī*, *utpalinī*. Why "when referring to a place"? [Counter-example: *puṣkaravān*.
After the word *bala*, when preceded by *bāhu* or *ūru*, the suffix *ini* shall be applied. Examples: *bāhubalī*; a certain person is called *ūrubalī*.

[The suffix *ini* is applied] after the word *sarva*. Examples: *sarvadhanī*, *sarvabījī*, *sarvakeśī naṭaḥ* (an actor with all his hair). [The suffix *ini* is applied] after the word *artha* when it does not denote presence. The suffix *ini* occurs after *artha*; one whose wealth (*artha*) is not present is *arthī*, meaning "poor. In other cases, it is *arthavān* (wealthy). However, in the Bhāṣya, this rule is rejected; instead, by taking *artha* to mean "requesting" (*arthana*) based on its etymological sense of "begging," the possessive suffix *matup* is applied to derive both *arthī* and *arthikaḥ*. Thus, it should be stated that the suffix *ini* does not occur after the word *artha* when it denotes wealth, nor after the word *artha* when it denotes requesting, because the suffix *matup* is not prescribed in those instances.
And [the suffix *cha*] follows words ending in *tad*. [Examples: *dhanārthī*, *hiraṇyārthī*.
After words such as *bala*, the suffix *matup* is optionally used.
The suffix *matup* may optionally occur after these [words]: *balavān* or *balī*; *utsāhavān* or *utsāhī*. [The suffix] *man* occurs after [a word ending in] *m* when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*).

The suffix *ini* occurs after nominal stems ending in *man* and *mat*. Examples: *dāminī*, *sāminī*, *heminī*. After a stem ending in *mat*: *sominī*. Why "after a nominal stem" (*nāmni*)? [Because it does not apply to adjectives; e.g.,] *somavān*.
After the words *kam* and *śam*, the suffixes *va*, *bha*, *yu*, *tu*, *ta*, *ya*, and *sa* [are applied].

The words *kam* and *śam* signify "water" and "well-being," respectively; from these two, seven suffixes are formed. With the suffix *vaḥ*: *kaṃvaḥ* (meghaḥ) "cloud"; *śaṃvaḥ* (vajraḥ) "thunderbolt. With the suffix *bhaḥ*: *kaṃbhaḥ*, *śambhaḥ*. Because the suffix *yus* is marked with *s*, it becomes a word (*pada*) when followed by a vowel, resulting in an *anusvāra*: *kaṃyuḥ*. [Example: "Look at the *śaṃyūn* (those bringing well-being) who are acting. With the suffix *tiḥ*: *kantiḥ*, *śantiḥ*. With the suffix *tuḥ*: *kantuḥ*, *śantuḥ*. With the suffix *taḥ*: *kantaḥ*, *śantaḥ*. With the suffix *yas*: *kaṃyaḥ*, *śaṃyaḥ*. The suffix *bhaḥ* is added to *tundi*, *vali*, and *vaṭi*.

The suffix *bha* occurs after these [words] in the sense of possession (*matvartha*). Examples: *tundibhaḥ* (one who has a large belly); *balibhaṃ madhyam dadhānā* (possessing a middle with folds). Because it belongs to the *pāmādi* group, we also have *valinaḥ* (having wrinkles). *Vaṭibho vṛkṣaḥ* (a tree with a girth). After the words *aham* and *śubham*, the suffix *yus* is applied.

In the two indeclinables *aham* and *śubham*, the meanings are "I" (*ahaṃkāra*) and "auspiciousness" (*kalyāṇa*) respectively. The suffix *yu* is applied after these two when they signify "devoted to me" (*matcartha*). Examples: *ahaṃyunāthaḥ* ("a lord devoted to me") and *śubhaṃyuḥ* ("one who possesses auspiciousness").
The suffixes expressing possession (*matvarthīya*) have been explained.
The division of the eastern direction.

Those suffixes beginning with *tasil* that occur prior to the rule *dikśabdebhyaḥ* [5.3.27] shall bear the technical designation *vibhakti*. The purpose [of this designation] is for the application of rules such as the substitution of *yat* for pronouns beginning with *tyad* (P. 7.2.102). Here, the phrase "from the first [word] among those that are semantically connected" (*samarthānāṃ prathamāt*) is no longer in force. The particle *vā* ("optionally") continues to apply. Consequently, in the alternative case, *tasil* and the other suffixes may occur—such as *kutaḥ* and *kasmāt*.
[The suffix *tasil* is applied] after words meaning "what" (*kim*), all pronouns (*sarvanāman*), and "many" (*bahu*), excluding the group beginning with *dvi*.

The suffixes beginning with *tasil* (i.e., *tra*, *tas*, etc. should be prescribed after a pronominal stem (*sarvanāman*) that is not *dvi* and so forth, and also after the word *bahu*. From what [examples]? *kutaḥ*, *kutra*; *yataḥ*, *yatra*.

Here, the word *bahu* is understood in the sense of number: *bahutaḥ*, *bahutra*. But in the sense of "extensiveness" (*vaipulya*), it is: *bahoḥ kālāt*. Why [is it said] "not *dvi* and so forth"? [Examples: *dvābhyām*, *dvayoḥ*.
This is the [section on] *iś*.

When a suffix belonging to the *prāgdiśīya* group follows, the substitution of *iś* for *idam* is prescribed: *itaḥ* (from here), *iha* (here). Furthermore, the substitutions *eta* and *etau* occur before the locative suffixes *r* (*re*) and *th* (*tha*).

The forms *idam* and *etad* are prescribed in this sequence before the letters *r* and *th*, respectively: *bhavantam etarhi manasvin garhitam* (O wise one, you are now censured), and *ittham pravādam yudhi samprahāram* (thus the report of the clash in battle). [In these cases, *idam* and *etad* become *eta-*].
*Etado'ś*.
When a suffix belonging to the *prāgdiśīya* group follows, *etad* is prescribed as *as*. [Examples: *ataḥ*, *atra*.
A split of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) must be made here; by means of it—[we obtain] *etarhi*. [The rule continues:
"In place of the whole [of *etad*], *sa-* is optionally substituted before a *prāgdiśīya* suffix."
Before the suffix *dā*, the final syllable of the whole word may optionally become *sa*: thus, either *sadā* or *sarvadā*. [The suffix] *tasil* is added after the fifth case ending.

It could be so. Why? From *sarvataḥ*, *bahutaḥ*, and *viśvataḥ*. Now, what is this suffix *tasil*? It is a suffix applied after a word ending in the fifth case (*pañcamī*). If it were a substitute for the fifth case, then in forms such as *hitataḥ* and *yataḥ*, the rule *supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ* would require the elision (*luk*) of the case-ending. Furthermore, in the case of *yadā* and *tadā*, the accent would be governed by the rule *anudāttau suppitau*. In *kutaḥ*, there would be the *guṇa* substitution according to *gher ḍiti*. In *tarhi*, there would be the lengthening (*dīrgha*) according to *supi ca*. In *kutra*, there would be the substitution of *at* according to *acca gheḥ*. Finally, in *tataḥ* and *tatra*, the substitutes *smāt* and *smin* would apply.

This has been stated in the Bhāṣya: "If *tasil* and the others were substitutes for case-endings (*vibhakti*), then the rules for the elision of *su*, accentuation, *guṇa*, lengthening, *attva*, *auttva*, and the substitution of *smāt* and so forth would [inappropriately] apply.
And [the rule] *taseś ca*.
Thus is the rule for the sake of accentuation.
And [the suffix *kha* is applied] after the prepositions *pari* and *abhi*.
The suffix *tasil* is applied after these two [words]. Examples: *paritaḥ*, *abhitaḥ*. The suffix *tral* is applied after a word in the locative case.
The suffix *tral* may be added after a word ending in the seventh case; for example, *yatra* and *bahutra*.
After the pronoun *idam*, the suffix *ha* is used [in the same sense].
The suffix *dha* shall occur after the word *idam* when it ends in the locative case; [thus] *iha*. After *kim*, the suffix *at* occurs.
The suffix *at* is added after the interrogative pronoun *kim* when it ends in the locative case. For example: *kva*. Some also accept *tral*, as in *kutra*, according to Jayāditya.
Furthermore, in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *vāh* is also used.
The *chandas* [section] is the *sūtra*:
"They are seen even after other [suffixes]."

The suffixes beginning with *tasil* are to be understood as being applicable to all case endings (*vibhakti*). Due to the inclusion of the term *dṛśi* (in Pāṇini’s rule), there is a prescribed usage when joined with words such as *bhavat*. Examples include: *sa bhavān*, *tato bhavān*, and *tatra bhavān*. One says: "I speak to him—[to] that long-lived one—from there, there, and there. Or: "It was done by him—[by] that beloved of the gods—from there, there, and there," and so forth. The suffix *dā* is applied to the words *sarva*, *eka*, *anya*, *kim*, *yat*, and *tat* when referring to time (*kāla*).

After these words ending in the locative case, the suffix *dā* shall be used to denote time. Examples: *sadā* (always), *sarvadā* (at all times), *ekadā* (once/at one time), *anyadā* (at another time), *yadā* (when), *tadā* (then), *kadā* (whenever).
Why "time"? [Counter-example: *sarvatra deśe* (in every place).
And this suffix *dā* applies when time in general is intended; therefore, it does not occur when a specific time is meant—as in "at such-and-such a day.
The suffix *thāl* is prescribed for time.
[The suffix] *hil* follows *idam*.
The suffix *rhil* shall be applied after the word *idam* when it ends in the seventh case; [it denotes] "at this time," as in *etarhi* and *adhunā*.
It is elided;
and *dānīm* [is also used].
The suffix *dānīm* shall be added after *idam* when it ends in the seventh case, as well as *ñ*; thus, *idānīm*.
After *tad*, *dā* is also [added].
Then *dā* and *dānīm* [are used for the locative]. *Tadā* means "at that time. *Tadānīm* [is also used].
And in the Vedic language (*chandas*), *dā*, *rhi*, and *ila* are used for those two [the locative and instrumental].
The *Chandaḥsūtra* is one [work].
[The suffix] *rhil* is optionally used after a word ending in the past passive participle suffix *kta*, provided that it does not refer to the current day.

The suffix *rhil* may optionally occur after interrogative pronouns, all nominal stems (*sarvanāman*), and numerals ending in the locative case when referring to a time other than the current day (*anadyatana*). For example: *karhi* or *kadā*; *yarhi* or *yadā*; *tarhi* or *tadā*.

[The following are indeclinable adverbs formed with specific suffixes: *sadyas*, *parut*, *parāri*, *aiṣamas*, *paredyavi*, *adya*, *pūrvedyus*, *anyedyus*, *anyataredyus*, *itaredyus*, *aparedyus*, *adharedyus*, *ubhayedyus*, and *uttaredyus*.

These fourteen [suffixes] are applied to the words *ahar* (day) and *varṣa* (year). When the day is the same, the suffix *sadyas* is used. In the previous year, *parut*; in the year before that, *parāri*; in this year, *aiṣamas*; on the following day, *paredyavi*; on this day, *adya*; on the previous day, *pūrvedyus*, and so forth. From the word *ubhaya* (both), the suffix *dyus* is added by the rule *dyuścobhayāt*. Thus, *ubhayadyus*. The suffix *thāl* is used in the sense of expressing a manner (*prakāra*).
The suffix *thāl* occurs after words meaning "similarity" or "manner. [Examples: *tena prakāreṇa* = *tathā*; *yathā*; *sarvathā*. After the word *idam*, the suffix *thamu* occurs.
And what more?
The suffix *thamu* occurs after the words *idam* and *kim* in the sense of manner (*prakāra*). [Examples: *ittham* (thus), *katham* (how).
It has been stated that the case-endings (*vibhakti*) are suffixes (*pratyaya*) following all pronouns (*sarvanāman*) beginning with *kim*.
From here onwards, the suffixes are used in their own right (svārthika). [The suffix] *thā* is used in the sense of cause (*hetu*) as well, in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
The *Chandas-sūtra*: from words denoting directions, the suffix *astāti* is applied in the sense of direction, place, and time, after [words ending in] the seventh, fifth, and first case endings.

The suffix *astāti* is applied in its own sense after words denoting directions (*digvācin*) that end in the locative case (*saptamī*) and so forth, provided they refer to direction, place, or time. For example: "dwelt in the eastern direction, place, or time" is expressed as *puraḥstād uṣitaḥ*. From a word ending in the ablative (*pañcamī*): *purastād āgataḥ* ("come from the east"). From a word ending in the nominative (*prathamā*): *purastād ramyā dik* ("the beautiful eastern direction"), *adhastād ramyo deśaḥ* ("the beautiful lower region/place").
This rule applies up to the point where the suffix *dhā* is used in the scope of *astāti*.
After the words *dakṣiṇa* and *uttara*, the suffix *atsuc* is applied.
The suffix *atasuc* shall be applied after these two [words, *dakṣiṇa* and *uttara*]: *dakṣiṇataḥ*, *uttarataḥ*.
After *para* and *avara*, it is optional (*vibhāṣā*).
The suffixes *atasuc* may optionally follow these two [words], either as *parataḥ* or *parastāt*, or as *avarataḥ* or *avarastāt*. There is elision (*luk*) of the suffix after the word *añc*.

The suffix *asti* (the feminine marker *ṅīp*) is elided after a directional term ending in *añc*, when *asti* itself is elided. By the rule "when a *taddhita* suffix is elided, [the feminine marker] is also elided," the *ṅīp* is dropped. Examples: he dwells in the east (*prāk*), he has come from the east (*prāgāgataḥ*), the east is to be traversed (*prāgramaṇīyam*). Likewise for *pratyak*. Also: above (*upari*), above (*upariṣṭāt*).
These two [suffixes] are prescribed as substitutes for the word *ūrdhva* in the sense of "later" (*astāti*). They occur after [the word *ūrdhva*].
The substitution of *paśca* for the word *avara* is prescribed when the suffix *atipratyaya* follows: *paścāt vasati*, *āgataḥ*, or *ramaṇīyam*.
And [the same substitution applies] when it is preceded by a word denoting direction: *dakṣiṇapaścāt*, *uttarapaścāt*.
And in a compound where the second member is [the word] *ardha*, [the substitution of *paśca* for *pañcan* occurs]. For example: *dakṣiṇapaścārdhaḥ*.
And [this applies] after *adhas* as well. It should be stated that the form *paścā* is also used; thus: *paścārdhaḥ*. In the Vedic language (*chandas*), both *pañca* and *paścā* are used.
The *chandas* is the aphorism;
the extraction [of phonemes] occurs through the successive moments of the upper and lower directions.
The suffix *āti* may be added after these: *uttarāt*, *adharāt*, and *dakṣiṇāt*.
Optionally, when not denoting distance, the suffix *enap* is added after these same words, provided they are not in the ablative case.

The suffix *enap* may optionally be used after words denoting directions (*dik-śabda*), provided that there is a proximate limit (*avadhimān*). The meaning is "not far away" (*adūre*) when [the distance] is to be understood. For example: *uttareṇa* or *uttarāt*, *dakṣiṇena* or *dakṣiṇāt*—[he] dwells there or [the place] is pleasant. Why say "not far away"? [Consider: *uttarato himavān* ("the Himalayas are to the north"). Why say "except for the fifth case" (*apañcamyāḥ*)? [Consider: *grāmasya dakṣiṇataḥ parvatād āgataḥ* ("he has come from the mountain to the south of the village"). This restriction "except for the fifth case" (*apañcamyāḥ*) is an governing rule (*adhikāra*) until the suffix *asi* is reached.
From the south, [it is] āc.
The suffix *āc* occurs after *dakṣiṇa* when it means "not far" (*adūra*), as in *dakṣiṇā vasati* ("she lives not far to the south") or *dakṣiṇā ramyam* ("the lovely place is not far to the south").
The suffix *āhi* also occurs [after *dakṣiṇa*] when it means "far" (*dūra*).
The suffix *āh* may be used after *dakṣiṇa* when [the direction] to be traversed is distant; by the force of the word *ca*, it is also used after *uttara*. Thus: *dakṣiṇāhi*, *dakṣiṇā*;
and *uttarāhi*, *uttarā*.
The forms *uttarāt* and *uttarāhi* may be used [with the ablative]. For example: *uttarā*, *uttarāhi vasati ramyam vā* (he dwells to the north, or it is pleasant there).
Dwelling to the north of the ocean, how could Rāma [not have seen] the city of the Rākṣasas situated on the southern shore of the salt waters?

The phrase "before the fifth case-ending" (*apañcamyāḥ*) is no longer applicable. For the words *pūrva*, *adhara*, and *avara*, the suffix *asi* is substituted [for the locative case-ending], and *pur*, *adha*, and *ava* are respectively substituted for these [three words].
